structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides zero percent interest loans or grants to help seniors make their homes more accessible and functional, allowing them to remain independent in their homes as they age.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years to finance accessibility improvements, or grants up to $25,000. Loans may cover up to 110 percent of the property value and must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans have interest rates based on the applicant's ability to pay, ranging from 0% to 6%. The maximum loan is generally $50,000. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their primary residence
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accessibility improvements for disabled and seniors, including chairlifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, doors, widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, grab bars, lever handles, and first floor bathrooms and laundry rooms. Also covers fall and injury prevention measures such as handrails, rubber treads, and bathroom grab bars.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Income limits vary based on household size and location (Washington, D.C. PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, with separate limits for the rest of the state).
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one resident age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered case by case)
Reside in a home that is structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
Not have outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. MSA median income (see income limits document for specific limits by household size)
Provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Submit valid photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant
Provide property tax bill and homeowners insurance documentation
If applicable, provide flood insurance policy documentation

Provide income verification documentation including recent paystubs, federal income tax returns, bank statements, award letters for Social Security/disability/pension/public assistance, or zero income statement if applicable

Provide a contractor bid from a licensed Maryland tradesperson documenting the accessibility repairs, not more than 60 days old, with photographs, contractor contact information, MHIC license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form
Total scope of work should not exceed $50,000
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency or through an in-home appointment. Applicants must submit a completed application along with all required supporting documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, property insurance information, and contractor bid documentation. Applications can be submitted via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mailed to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Once submitted, the application is processed by the department and the applicant will be contacted.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) provides strategic investment in local housing and businesses to support healthy, sustainable communities with growing tax bases and improved quality of life. The program focuses on areas where coordinated investment and strategy will have meaningful neighborhood revitalization impact, targeting designated Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City and the inner beltway areas of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for community development projects that support neighborhood revitalization, including down payment assistance for home buyers, property acquisition or rehabilitation programs, energy efficiency improvements through weatherization and retrofits, mixed-use development combining housing and retail space, community open space and public infrastructure development, workforce and employment development, strategic demolition, and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kevin Baynes; Regional Project Managers (contact information varies by region)
structured_extraction.contact_email: kevin.baynes@maryland.gov, jessica.degaine@maryland.gov, katherine.howard@maryland.gov, sarah.kim1@maryland.gov, erin.lavitt@maryland.gov, sara.jackson@maryland.gov, jean.cannon@maryland.gov, maria.mougridis@maryland.gov, jessica.argueta@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan are eligible to apply.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can support various activities, including: down payment assistance to attract home buyers; acquisition or rehabilitation of vacant or blighted properties; improvement of residential and business properties; energy efficiency through weatherization and retrofits; mixed-use development combining housing, retail, and office space; community open space or public infrastructure development; workforce and employment development; strategic demolition; and operating costs for community enhancement projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Community Areas within Baltimore City and the inner beltway of Baltimore and Anne Arundel counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to view BRNI boundaries. Contact your Regional Project Manager to confirm specific address eligibility.
requirements_list: Community Development Organization must have an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
If organization does not have an approved plan, it must submit one at time of application
Strategic neighborhood revitalization plan must be approved by the Department prior to any funding awards
Projects must be part of the approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan
Projects should capitalize on community strengths and be targeted to specific neighborhoods
Applying with partner organizations, like Community Development Financial Institutions and cross-jurisdictional partners, is strongly recommended
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Development Organizations with an approved strategic neighborhood revitalization plan submit applications for projects in eligible areas. Organizations without an approved plan must submit the plan along with project requests at time of application. Organizations are encouraged to apply with partner organizations including Community Development Financial Institutions and cross-jurisdictional partners. For more information on how to apply, visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage. Contact your Regional Project Manager to confirm specific address eligibility. Regional Project Managers are assigned by geographic region to assist applicants.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides low-interest financing to help homeowners improve the energy efficiency, comfort, livability, and safety of their homes by replacing and upgrading appliances, heating and cooling systems, insulation, and other energy-saving measures. Homeowners can save on utility bills and reduce heating and cooling costs through these improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% APR for up to $30,000 in financing available for energy efficiency measures with a term up to 10 years. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Borrowers can choose their own loan term (less than or equal to 10 years). Solar photovoltaic projects can be financed at up to 50% of the total loan amount (1:1 match to energy efficiency costs). Health and safety costs related to energy improvements, including mold remediation and radon mitigation, can be financed at up to 25% of the total loan. There are no pre-payment penalties, and borrowers can avoid interest by paying off the loan early. The loan cannot finance projects or upgrades that have already been purchased or completed. Initial funding is provided as a 30% down payment (2-party check to borrower and contractor, or 1-party check for retail purchases). Final funding (70% of loan amount) is issued upon completion after submission of signed Certificates of Completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who want to improve energy efficiency, comfort, livability, and safety in their homes.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency measures including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment (excluding ENERGY STAR stoves, ovens, and microwave ovens), ENERGY STAR appliances, windows and doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic installation (capped at 50% of total loan amount/1:1 match to energy efficiency costs), health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
Unsecured loan based on verification of credit and ability to pay
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland (proof required)
Cannot have work done or purchases made prior to receiving BeSMART funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the online BeSMART Loan Application along with a valid Driver's License, 30 days of pay stubs, and a recent mortgage statement. DHCD will send a DocuSign document to privately receive your Social Security number and obtain credit report authorization. Provide an estimate or proposal from your contractor (or retailer for appliance purchases). DHCD will send loan documents for signature and return. Upon approval, DHCD will send an initial 30% down payment as a 2-party check (made payable to both borrower and contractor, or 1-party check for retail purchases with no contractor). After project completion, you and the contractor sign Certificates of Completion and submit photos. DHCD will then issue the remaining 70% payment. Begin making loan payments after funding is received.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant is a microgrant program offered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program that provides grant funding to assist early-stage for-profit businesses in growing and expanding within designated Sustainable Communities areas in Maryland. The program particularly supports home-based businesses looking to establish their first commercial location outside the home. Microgrants range from $20,000 to $50,000, with up to $2,000,000 in total program funding available.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 are provided to support for-profit small businesses seeking capital for growth and expansion opportunities. The total program offers up to $2,000,000 in funding. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount (for example, a $50,000 grant requires a $50,000 matching contribution). Grant funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses supporting revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses cannot be counted. Businesses must have more than 2 employees and no more than 50 employees (full-time equivalent), annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million, and be located in a Sustainable Communities area. Grant awards are expected to be paid in February-March 2025. Award winners must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, and provide a one-page summary nine months after receiving funds detailing how the grant was used and its impact.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The Business Boost application round closed on October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST. Note: The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses with growth and expansion plans, particularly home-based businesses looking to establish a first commercial location outside the home, located in designated Sustainable Communities. Businesses must have greater than 2 and no more than 50 full-time equivalent employees, annual revenue between $50,000 and $1 million, and be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses supporting revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including but not limited to salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Funds support business expansion through increased rent, increased payroll for new employees, new equipment, and marketing. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses such as current rent and payroll cannot be counted—only the increase in rent and payroll qualifies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Sustainable Communities in Maryland. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper (https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html) to verify if a business location qualifies by entering the business address in the incentive look-up tool. The business must be located in a Sustainable Communities area as shown in the mapper results.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit business demonstrating plans for growth
Must be a new or expanding small business
Must be located in a designated Sustainable Community in Maryland
Must have a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount
Must have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) as of September 23, 2024
Must have annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million
Must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must be in good financial and legal standing with no past due amounts, liens, or judgments
Professional services and sales-based businesses (including Insurance, Accounting, Real Estate, Legal, Finance) are not eligible

Non-profit organizations, cannabis-based businesses, pawn shops, gun shops, massage parlors, adult video/book shops, adult entertainment facilities, rental real estate businesses, insurance companies, tanning salons, check-cashing facilities, gambling facilities, tattoo parlors, and liquor stores are not eligible
Previous award winners of an NBW Opportunity Zone grant and NBW Business Boost grant are not eligible
Business name must exactly match on application, W-9, and SDAT Good Standing Certificate

Must provide required documentation including Articles of Organization, bylaws, most recent annual tax return (Tax Year 2023), financial statements as of August 31, 2024, screenshot of eligible location, proof of matching funds, Certificate of Good Standing screenshot from SDAT, and IRS W-9
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application is submitted online at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. Applicants create an account, provide a brief description of their organization, answer questions about the organization, complete a budget table showing how grant funds and matching contributions will be used, and describe how funds will advance the business within a sustainable community. Required documents include Articles of Organization, bylaws, most recent annual tax return (Tax Year 2023), financial statements as of August 31, 2024, screenshot showing the business is in an eligible location, proof of matching funds (bank statement or loan statement showing available funds as of August 31, 2024), Certificate of Good Standing screenshot from SDAT, and IRS W-9. Only fully completed applications submitted by the deadline are considered; incomplete applications will be returned. The application round was projected to open September 23, 2024, at 12:00 noon and close October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST (may close sooner if funding is exhausted). Applications are prioritized based on (1) business location, (2) impact of business expansion including new employees to be hired, capital investment, and additional square footage, and (3) presentation of business financials and supporting documents. Priority impact attributes include innovative businesses driving innovation or technology advancements, businesses growing in new industries, businesses focused on regional strengths, businesses leveraging partnerships with local school districts and higher education institutions, and Minority Business Enterprises (MBE). Award announcements were made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant funds were expected to be paid in February-March 2025 after local resolution approval from the applicant's governing executive body. Upon receiving an award, applicants must sign a grant agreement, and DHCD initiates the process with the local jurisdiction for approval (45 days to respond). Award recipients must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, and provide a one-page summary nine months after receiving funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance - Hurricane Sandy
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provided funding to help Somerset County and other eligible Maryland counties recover from the damage caused by Hurricane Sandy, which struck the eastern seaboard on October 28, 2012. The state received a total of $28.64 million from Congress through the Disaster Relief Appropriations Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development through the Community Development Block Grant Program. The first award of $8.6 million was designated for recovery activities in Somerset County. A second award of $20 million was distributed across eligible counties (Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, Garrett, and Somerset) with 80% ($16 million) going to Somerset County as the most impacted and distressed area. Funds were used for housing recovery, economic development, infrastructure improvements, and public facilities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provided federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) disaster recovery funds totaling $28.64 million. In Somerset County, funds were distributed through multiple phases for: (1) Housing Recovery - providing deferred loans to low and moderate income homeowners for rehabilitation (repairs under 49% of assessed home value) or replacement (repairs of 50% or greater of assessed home value) of hurricane-damaged homes; (2) Economic Recovery - providing grants to watermen for equipment losses, facade improvement grants for businesses, and business loans up to $60,000 interest-free for up to 10 years for working capital, construction, inventory, and equipment; (3) Infrastructure - funding dike repairs and improvements, shoreline stabilization, dredging, drainage improvements, water/sewer system upgrades, street resurfacing, and building replacements; (4) Public Facilities - funding homeless shelter construction, Head Start facility construction, and emergency generator installation at critical facilities; (5) Public Services - job training programs. Housing assistance was provided as deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property. All assistance required beneficiaries to be low and moderate income persons (household income not exceeding 80% of area median income for Somerset County). Projects had to meet CDBG national objectives: benefit to low/moderate income persons, elimination of slums/blight, or meeting an urgent need related to Hurricane Sandy damage.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications were accepted by January 28, 2014 for the second round of funding. Individual project phases had varying implementation deadlines, with most activities required to be completed by October 1, 2022.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residents and organizations in Somerset County, Allegany County, Charles County, Dorchester County, and Garrett County recovering from Hurricane Sandy and other qualifying disaster damage (Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, and the Derecho). Priority focus on low and moderate income persons and households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery activities in eligible counties affected by Hurricane Sandy and other qualifying disaster events, including: housing rehabilitation and replacement for low/moderate income homeowners; business loans and grants for economic recovery; infrastructure improvements including flood protection, drainage systems, waterway improvements, and utility upgrades; public facility repairs and construction including shelters and community buildings; temporary housing assistance; job training; planning and feasibility studies; and related administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All funds for the first grant ($8.6 million) were designated for Somerset County. For the second grant ($20 million), at least 80% must be used in Somerset County as the most impacted and distressed area. The remaining 20% could be used in other counties with Presidential Disaster Declarations for Hurricane Sandy, Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, or the Derecho (including Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, and Garrett Counties). Specific projects were limited to areas within these designated counties that experienced qualifying disaster damage.
requirements_list: Applicant organizations must comply with CDBG program requirements including fair housing and non-discrimination provisions
Projects must meet one of three CDBG national objectives: benefit low/moderate income persons, eliminate slums/blight, or meet an urgent need
Housing assistance recipients must have household income not exceeding 80% of HUD-determined area median income for Somerset County
Housing applicants must provide proof of storm damage and proof of homeownership
Business loan recipients must prove business ownership and storm damage to business or equipment
Counties must adopt and maintain a current Citizen Participation Plan
Counties must conduct minimum of two public hearings prior to application submission
Counties must pass local resolution authorizing application and specific projects
Counties must adopt and maintain Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan
For housing rehabilitation: repairs must be 49% or less of current assessed home value
For housing replacement: repairs must be 50% or greater of current assessed home value
All housing assistance provided as deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property after grant closure
Projects must incorporate mitigation and resiliency measures to protect against future hazards
Projects must promote sound, sustainable, and long-term recovery planning with responsible floodplain management
Project activities must be completed within specified timeframes (generally 2 years from grant agreement date)
For public housing: Housing Authority must maintain flood insurance in perpetuity on assisted units
State administrative costs limited to percentage of total grant amount
At least 50% of total disaster recovery grant funds must benefit low and moderate income persons
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This was a retrospective disaster recovery program. The application process occurred in early 2014 for the second round of funding. Counties conducted comprehensive needs assessments through citizen participation process, including two public hearings. Counties submitted applications by January 28, 2014, with supporting documentation including local resolutions, citizen participation plans, and detailed project descriptions. Applications were reviewed and ranked by DHCD staff using criteria including project type/benefit (75 points), readiness to proceed (50 points), and leveraging of other funds (25 points). The State submitted Action Plans to HUD for approval in phases, with the initial partial plan submitted March 25, 2014. Amendments were submitted as additional funding was obligated through 2017. For individual homeowners and businesses seeking assistance, the process required proof of income, proof of storm damage, proof of ownership, and submission through county programs. Housing Authority relocation planning was conducted prior to project implementation. The program operated through multiple phases with funding being obligated and expended over several years (2013-2022).

structured_extraction.program_description: Federally funded program designed to assist county and municipal governments with activities directed toward neighborhood revitalization, housing opportunities, economic development and improved public facilities and services. Funds help strengthen Maryland communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods and improving overall quality of life.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State receives annual Congressional allocations and distributes federal funds to non-entitlement counties, small cities, and towns. Funds are awarded through two competitive categories: Community Development (accepted once per year) and Special Projects (submitted anytime after approval). The state must cumulatively use at least 70% of its allocation to benefit low-income and moderate-income persons over a three-year period. For State Fiscal Year 2026/Federal Fiscal Year 2025, the State has received $7,416,560, allocated as follows: State Administration (2% + $100,000): $248,331; Technical Assistance (1%): $74,165; Community Development (82% - $100,000): $6,000,000; Special Projects (15%): $1,094,064. Funds serve as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions to meet their needs. All funded projects must benefit persons of low-to-moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development Applications accepted once each year; Special Projects accepted anytime after written approval
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Public or private entities may be sub-recipients of eligible local government. Eligible subrecipients include governmental agencies such as housing authorities; non-profit organizations that are corporations, associations, agencies or faith-based organizations with non-profit status under IRS Section 501(c)(3); for-profit businesses that are in Good Standing in the State of Maryland for economic development projects; Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs) certified by the CDBG Program for new housing construction projects; and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) certified by the State HOME Program for new housing construction projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Housing (including acquisition, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, and installation); public facilities (water/sewer, streets, childcare centers, senior centers, community centers, shelters); economic development projects; acquisition of real property; code enforcement; clearance and demolition; removal of barriers for elderly or handicapped persons; public services; planning; administrative costs; assistance to neighborhood-based non-profit organizations; and housing services such as counseling, energy auditing, and downpayment assistance. All funded projects must benefit persons of low-to-moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Non-entitlement counties and non-entitlement cities and towns. Ineligible entitlement counties: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's. Ineligible cities: Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, Salisbury. Municipalities in ineligible entitlement counties cannot apply. Projects must generally be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services, single family housing rehabilitation, acquisition/renovation and resale of existing houses, downpayment assistance, or where the Secretary of DHCD determines that the project is necessary to protect public health, alleviate personal economic hardship in an emergency, promote economically integrated housing, is consistent with an overall economic development strategy, or where an exception is necessary and has been granted through the Maryland Department of Planning exception process.
requirements_list: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population of less than 200,000
Non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended
Project must meet one of three national objectives: benefit low- and moderate-income persons; eliminate slum and blight; or meet urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible
Project must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (with specified exceptions)
Grantees must comply with Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act if acquiring property or displacing residents/businesses
Grantees must comply with National Environmental Policy Act and complete environmental review prior to project initiation
Grantees must comply with fair housing and equal opportunity requirements
For construction projects funded with minimum $200,000 of CDBG and other HUD funding, Section 3 requirements apply
Grantees must comply with Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements for infrastructure projects (with exceptions for projects under $250,000)
For housing funded with CDBG, no subprime or adjustable rate mortgages allowed; minimum 30-year fixed rate mortgage required
Minimum 8 hours of housing counseling from HUD-approved housing counseling agency required for homebuyers
If spending more than $750,000 of federal funds in fiscal year, Single Audit required
Grantees must have written Conflict of Interest Policy
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions on application development. Community Development applications are competitive and accepted once per year. Special Projects applications can be submitted anytime after receiving written approval. Applicants must submit applications with required documentation including local resolution, citizen participation plan, public hearing notice, and proposed project details. Applications are rated and evaluated based on criteria established by DHCD. Applicants seeking funds for projects meeting the urgent need national objective must contact CDBG program staff to determine eligibility before applying under the Special Projects category. Upon award, grantees must execute grant agreements and comply with all program regulations including financial management, procurement, environmental review, and reporting requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Community Investment Tax Credits support 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits for use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services. Businesses and individuals that donate $500 or more to a qualified organization's approved project can earn tax credits equal to 50% of the value of the money, goods, or real property contribution.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations apply for tax credit allocations ranging from a minimum of $10,000 to a maximum of $50,000. The total annual funding available is $1.75M in Maryland income tax credits. When donors contribute $500 or more to a qualified nonprofit's approved project, they receive Community Investment Tax Credits equal to 50% of the value of money, goods, or real property contributions. For example, a $50,000 tax credit award requires the organization to raise $100,000 in eligible donations. Tax credits can be used against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made and may not be used retroactively. These tax credits are in addition to deductions on both Federal and State taxes as a result of the charitable contribution. All award contracts have a 24-month life. The FY26 award contract period runs from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027. Tax credits must be used during this two-year period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations applying for tax credit allocations, and individuals and businesses making charitable contributions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects can be capital and/or operating and typically involve activities such as education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, enhancing neighborhoods and business districts, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible budget line items include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area. Projects may also receive additional consideration if they are located in designated Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households (ENOUGH) areas or designated Just Communities. For capital projects, the project site must be within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, if the primary project site is not in a PFA, organizations must document that clients served reside within PFA boundaries.
requirements_list: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations are eligible applicants
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Office of the Secretary of State or have religious exemption documentation
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Donors must make contributions of $500 or more
Donors must obtain a Donor Acknowledgement Form from the nonprofit
Individuals and businesses must use tax credits against taxes owed for the year in which the contribution was made
Donors must be individuals with personal tax liability in Maryland or businesses conducting trade or business in Maryland and subject to income tax, franchise tax or insurance premiums tax
Maximum tax credit request is $50,000; minimum typical award is $10,000
For capital projects, organization must document site control via deed, lease, title/real estate settlement documents, or similar evidence
Organization must maintain annual charitable registration and good standing status throughout award period
Organization must submit Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving each donation
Organization must submit four Semi-Annual Reports during the 24-month award period (due July 10 and January 10)
Organization must maintain records for seven years following award completion
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: FY26 applications open Monday, May 19, 2025 and close Thursday, June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM. Nonprofit organizations must apply through the Department's IGX Project Portal online grants management system. New users must complete a registration request in the Project Portal (click 'New User? Register Here' below the login box) and indicate interest in the FY26 CITC round; registration typically takes up to 72 hours for approval. Existing Portal users will find the application in the 'My Opportunities' section of their Dashboard. Before starting an application, organizations must ensure their Profile Organization Information and Organization Uploads pages contain all current required documents (Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, Board list, Secretary of State charitable registration or exemption letter, SDAT Good Standing screenshot, and Executed Corporate Resolution). Applicants must also provide Priority Funding Area (PFA) maps for each project site using the Department's Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper 4.0 tool and evidence of site control if requesting capital funds. Applications must include complete project descriptions, task and timeline tables covering the full 24-month award period (January 1, 2026 - December 31, 2027), and detailed budgets with narratives. All documents must be submitted in PDF format through the Portal. Award notifications will be announced in Fall 2025.

structured_extraction.program_description: A funding program that provides local governments and community development organizations with money for projects that strengthen communities. Projects focus on business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership, and commercial revitalization in areas targeted for recovery.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided to local governments, community development organizations, and groups of local governments for revitalization projects in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones in specific counties. The grant supports activities such as mixed-use development, business retention and expansion, streetscape improvements, homeownership programs, façade improvements, and real estate acquisition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community development organizations, and groups of local governments working on revitalization projects in designated Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects that strengthen communities including mixed-use development, business retention and attraction, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation, residential and commercial façade improvements, real estate acquisition, land banking, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones specifically in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset, and Wicomico Counties. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must capitalize on community strengths while addressing revitalization challenges
Project should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects should aim to stabilize a community, reverse social/economic/physical decline, or encourage sustainable growth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For application instructions and more information, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides emergency rental assistance to eligible student households enrolled in Maryland community schools who are experiencing housing instability and homelessness.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Emergency rental assistance provided to eligible student households experiencing housing instability and homelessness.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Student households enrolled in Maryland community schools experiencing housing instability or homelessness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Emergency rental assistance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland community schools.
requirements_list: Must be enrolled in a Maryland community school
Must be experiencing housing instability or homelessness

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funds to seventeen Community Action Agencies and other non-profit organizations across Maryland to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. These agencies use the money to offer direct services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, including programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Funds may also support training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program distributes 90% of Maryland's allocated funds to designated Community Action Agencies. The state uses the other 5% for discretionary funding to support activities that fight poverty. Funding supports activities and programs to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization, plus training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland's designated Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and local government units focused on poverty elimination and community development that serve low-income individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support direct services for low-income individuals to help them become self-sufficient, including programs for employment, education, housing, and health. Funds can also support training, technical assistance, community revitalization projects, and coordination and communication among Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Services must benefit individuals and households with incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
Community Action Agencies must have a specific board composition: one-third public officials, one-third representatives of low-income persons, and one-third from community groups.
Applicants for discretionary funds must propose a program with measurable outcomes for self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application period for fiscal year 2025 has closed. You should check the program's webpage for information about future application opportunities.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions create or upgrade computer labs and centers. These labs provide public computer access for individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 covering 100% of costs for creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers, plus up to $10,000 for internet service subscription costs for up to three years. Funding covers computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors, webcams, headphones, microphones), networking equipment (routers, switches, cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls), internet service subscription, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses including staff salaries (up to 15% of budget), administrative expenses including training and security monitoring (up to 15% of budget), software (operating systems, productivity suites, educational and training software, antivirus), audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards, speakers), and assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards and mice). The majority (50% or higher) of those served must fall into covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, incarcerated or returning citizens. Total program funding is $2 million from American Rescue Plan Act State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (ARPA). Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 29, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local jurisdictions (City, County, Municipal), incorporated municipalities, local government agencies, not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entities, and Community Anchor Institutions serving targeted populations including individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade, and retrofit of computer labs and centers providing public computer access for individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, and incarcerated or returning citizens. Funds may be used for computer equipment purchases, networking equipment, internet service subscription (up to 3 years), marketing and outreach to covered populations, operational expenses including staff salaries, administrative and training expenses, software, audiovisual equipment, and assistive technology for accessibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties
requirements_list: Applicant must be legally organized as one of the following: Maryland local jurisdiction, Incorporated Municipality within Maryland, Local Government Agency delegated by local Maryland jurisdiction, Not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or Community Anchor Institution within Maryland
Grant funding not to exceed $65,000 per application for computer equipment purchase
Internet Service Subscription funding not to exceed $10,000 per application
Majority (50% or higher) of those served must be from covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2026
Computers must come with standard manufacturer warranty or extended warranty
All purchases must be necessary for successful operation of computer lab and program effectiveness
Applicant must provide W-9 form, Certificate of Good Standing, and 501(c) documentation for nonprofits
Applicant must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to by applicant
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET. Applications may be submitted electronically to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application – Organizational Applicant name', by mail postmarked by the deadline with proof of mailing to Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or hand-delivered between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM ET (except weekends and state/federal holidays) with proper identification. Complete application must include: (1) Application Form with all required information including applicant details, budget breakdown, and project information; (2) Executive Summary and Scope of Work including timeline; (3) Project Budget with detailed itemized breakdown; (4) Federal Form W-9; (5) 501(c) documentation for nonprofits if applicable; (6) Certificate of Good Standing if applicable; (7) Project Narrative addressing executive summary, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and metrics, statement of experience, and timeline; (8) Technical specifications of equipment; (9) Community engagement plan; and (10) Letters of support. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications and evaluation of responses, and may be selected for interview. Awards are expected to begin in December 2024. Prior to official submission, applicants may request technical assistance by November 22, 2024. OSB reserves right to contact applicants for clarification. Late applications will not be considered.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. The program utilizes $95 million in Federal Coronavirus Capital Projects Funding from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) to support broadband infrastructure expansion in unserved areas of Maryland. Grants cover 70% to 90% of capital construction costs depending on service area density, with applicants providing required matching funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $800,000 and $4,500,000 providing 70% to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband networks serving unserved premises. Grant coverage depends on service area density: Wired projects with fewer than 8 premises per mile receive 90% (10% match required); 8-14 premises per mile receive 80% (20% match required); 15+ premises per mile receive 70% (30% match required). Wireless projects with fewer than 40 premises per tower receive 90% (10% match required); 40-69 premises per tower receive 80% (20% match required); 70+ premises per tower receive 70% (30% match required). Matching funds must be cash and cannot be used for operational costs. Eligible grant purposes include construction of facilities, middle mile infrastructure, electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment cabinets, shelters), outside plant (fiber, coaxial, copper), and customer drops. Ineligible purposes include operating expenses, tower/land/building purchases, building renovations, tower upgrades, facility/company acquisitions, customer devices (handsets, laptops, tablets), and supplanting of federal funds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners seeking to construct broadband infrastructure in unserved areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks including: outside plant (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment necessary to deliver service, customer drops to individual homes and businesses, fiber optic cable, conduit, vaults, cabinets, wireless radios, antennas, access points, OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, equipment shelters, and other capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Funds may also support middle mile infrastructure when another provider cannot supply suitable service. Not eligible for operating expenses, leases, bandwidth/spectrum expenses, salaries unrelated to construction, customer devices, or acquisition of facilities/companies.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Areas that have received state grant funding in the past are ineligible for additional funding. All premises in the proposed funded service area (PFSA) must be unserved with no existing broadband service at 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload speeds. The PFSA may span multiple jurisdictions but must be entirely within an eligible area.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, or other legal entity (cooperative, private corporation, LLC) organized for-profit or non-profit and recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction
Applicants cannot be individuals or partnerships
Grant request minimum: $800,000; maximum: $4,500,000
Required matching funds: 10%-30% of total construction costs based on service area density (wired or wireless)
Service area must consist entirely of unserved premises with no existing broadband service
All premises in proposed service area must be offered service at Broadband Grant Speed (100 Mbps download/100 Mbps upload, or 100/20 if scalable with certification)
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities
Applicant must be registered with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and in good standing
Applicant must have Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must submit current IRS Form W-9
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Matching funds must be cash available at time of award (not in-kind contributions)
Must commence project by September 1, 2023
Must complete project by August 31, 2026
Must expend at least 50% of grant funds by second anniversary of agreement
Areas with past state broadband funding are ineligible for additional funding
All necessary federal, state, and local permits and approvals must be obtained before project commencement
Federal funds previously awarded cannot be supplanted by this grant, only supplemented
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Prepare complete application package including: Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, evidence of legal existence and good standing, letters from local jurisdiction(s) identifying applicant as recognized partner, DUNS number, Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov. 2. Complete Executive Summary describing proposed funded service area (PFSA), project need, benefits to subscribers, number of households/businesses to be served, applicant history and qualifications, partnership details if applicable, and project timeline. 3. Submit Scoring Criteria Documentation including network diagram and pro forma financial statement assumptions. 4. Provide System Design documentation. 5. Include Service Area Demographics and map (shape file or KML/KMZ format) showing all properties to receive service. 6. Submit Scope of Work with construction build-out timeline, project milestones, and detailed project budget (Schedule F-1 and F-2) broken down by category (electronic equipment, outside plant, middle mile, customer drops, CPE, towers, buildings, bandwidth, engineering). 7. Provide Financial Information and Sustainability documentation (Schedule G-1) with historical financial statements and pro forma projections. 8. Submit Statement of Experience for applicant and any partner organizations. 9. Document Evidence of Funding Commitments from Other Sources including confirmation letters from funding sources. 10. Complete Application Checklist certifying all required documents are included. 11. Submit by December 5, 2022 at 11:59pm ET via: (a) Postmarked/shipped paper copy with original signatures and electronic version on USB flash drive mailed to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, Office of Statewide Broadband, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; (b) Email as zipped file to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line "Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – [company name]". 12. Proof of mailing required if submitted by USPS (dated postmark, dated mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier). 13. Prior to application submission, may request technical assistance from OSB before November 18, 2022. 14. Upon award, enter into Network Infrastructure Grant Program Agreement with Department.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program – Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program provides funding specifically for Smith Island to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. The program covers up to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband infrastructure with a required local match of at least 10%.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $1,000,000 to $3,000,000 covering up to 90% of capital construction costs for broadband networks serving unserved homes and businesses on Smith Island. Grant funds may cover construction of outside plant (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), and other capital costs directly necessary to provide broadband service. Applicants must provide a minimum match of 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of requested grant amount) in cash. Matching funds exceptions may apply for federal funding, Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul service costs (up to 3 years), or tower construction/structural improvements. Operating expenses, equipment purchases prior to application submission, land, buildings, and customer premise equipment beyond the ONT are not eligible. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 31, 2024 by 11:59 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, incorporated organizations recognized as partners by local jurisdictions, cooperatives, private corporations, limited liability companies, and other legal entities (except individuals and sole proprietorships) on Smith Island seeking to construct broadband infrastructure
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband networks including: outside plant infrastructure (fiber optic cabling, copper, coaxial cable for last mile and middle mile deployment), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters, access points), tower construction and structural improvements (as match only), customer drops, engineering costs tied to funded capital assets, and other capital expenses directly necessary to provide broadband service at minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds). Customer premise equipment beyond the ONT or fixed wireless antenna, laptop/tablet/handset devices, operating expenses, land purchases, building purchases or renovations, and bandwidth costs are not eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Maryland. The Identified Service Area (ISA) includes all locations on Smith Island where broadband service does not currently exist at speeds of at least 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload. All 278 unserved premises on the island must be served by the project.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction, cooperative, private corporation, limited liability company organized on for-profit or non-profit basis recognized as a partner by local jurisdiction, or other legal entity recognized as a partner by the local jurisdiction (not an individual or sole proprietorship)
Applicant must be legally organized and in good standing in Maryland
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities and enter into contracts
Applicant must provide IRS Form W-9, DUNS Number, and Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov
Applicant must provide evidence of legal existence and good standing with State of Maryland
If partnering with another entity, draft or final partnership agreement must be provided detailing financial terms and entity qualifications
Local jurisdiction partnership letter required documenting extent of participation and support
Grant request must be between $1,000,000 and $3,000,000
Project must serve entire Identified Service Area where broadband service does not currently exist
Network must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 millisecond latency (or 100 Mbps down and 20 Mbps up if scalable to symmetrical speeds with certification)
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Matching funds contribution minimum of 10% of total construction costs (11.11% of requested grant amount) must be in cash and available at time of award
Project must commence by September 1, 2024
Project must be completed by August 31, 2027
At least 50% of grant funds must be expended by second anniversary of effective date unless otherwise agreed in writing
Applicant must have not been debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity in past four years
Applicant must not have civil claims for non-payment of $30,000 or more
Applicant must comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations
Applicant must obtain all necessary federal, state, and local approvals, permits, and licenses prior to project commencement
Grant funds may not supplant previously awarded federal funds for broadband construction in the service area
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a complete application package by January 31, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET via one of three methods: (1) postmarked or shipped paper copy with original signatures plus electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706; (2) email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – your company name' with files attached as zipped file; or (3) commercial shipping with dated receipt. Paper applications must show proof of USPS postmark, dated mail receipt from USPS, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier. The application package must include: completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9 (Schedule A-2), proof of legal existence and good standing, partnership documentation if applicable, Executive Summary covering project description, applicant qualifications, total project costs and system overview, Scoring Criteria Documentation, System Design with network diagram, Scope of Work including construction build-out milestones (Schedule F-1) and project budget (Schedule F-2), Service Area Demographics, Financial Information and Sustainability including historical financial statements and Pro Forma Financial Statement (Schedule G-1) with assumptions (Schedule G-2), Statement of Experience, and Evidence of Funding Commitments. Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. Technical assistance requests must be made by January 19, 2024. All files should be converted to PDF format except those with specific file format requirements. Files should be named clearly to reflect content. Approved applicants will enter into a Network Infrastructure Grant Agreement with DHCD with exhibits including the approved application form, project budget, project map, and any certification regarding exemption from standard minimum network requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions create, build, and operate broadband gap networks and community networks. These networks address affordability challenges that prevent low- and moderate-income households and other covered populations from subscribing to internet service, providing affordable or free broadband access.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $25,000 and $250,000 covering up to 100% of capital costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks. Total program funding was $5 million from American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. Funds cover equipment including network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless equipment, antennas, access points, modems, equipment shelters, Optical Line Terminals (OLTs), Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), and any necessary equipment shelters needed to deliver broadband service to end users. Funds can also support operations and maintenance of new or existing gap networks and community networks.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), non-profit 501(c) organizations, community-based anchor institutions, and other community-based organizations serving low- and moderate-income households and covered populations including individuals living at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and those with low literacy levels), and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Equipment, instrumentation, networking capability, hardware and software, and digital network technology to provide broadband services to covered populations at low or no cost. Funds can be used to: build and deploy new gap networks or community networks at minimum 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds; upgrade or expand existing gap networks or community networks; operate and maintain new or existing gap networks or community networks; and purchase electronics necessary to deliver service to end users including Optical Line Terminals (OLTs), Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters. Travel related to program deployment is also eligible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Applicants must be providing services within the State of Maryland and registered and, if applicable, in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. Project areas must be identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to a connection that reliably meets or exceeds symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lack of affordable access to broadband service, or lack of reliable broadband.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), non-profit 501(c) entity, community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Applicant must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Projects must reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with a maximum latency of 50 milliseconds measured at the served subscribers' location

Projects providing 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload must be scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds based on future technology advances, with a maximum latency of 50 milliseconds; ISP must submit a certificate if unable to achieve minimum connectivity due to geography, topography, or excessive cost
Grant range: $25,000 to $250,000
Subscriber cost must be low or no cost for covered populations
Only complete applications will be considered for funding

Applicant must submit completed application form, project summary with executive summary and network design, IRS determination letter if applicable, certificate of good standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, IRS W-9 form, and DUNS number
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to by the applicant if an award is made
Applicant responsible for overall funding, implementation, and operation of the project
All awardees must execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining the obligations of the awardee and State to the project
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications were submitted via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization'. The application submission period opened February 15, 2022 and closed March 31, 2022. Required submissions included: completed application form (must be completed in entirety), project summary addressing executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost information, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and sustainability, implementation schedule, and funding scope and budget, IRS determination letter (if applicable), certificate of good standing verification, IRS W-9 form, and DUNS number. The budget submission must include categories for: operations (equipment, payroll, supplies, materials), contracted services (payments to independent contractors and external organizations), travel (related to program deployment), and any other funding necessary for the project including anticipated sources. Successful applicants were chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interview. Funding announcements were made on or before April 15, 2022. It was the OSB's intent to award funds beginning in May 2022. No reimbursement was made for costs incurred in responding to the RFA or for developing submissions. The OSB reserved the right to waive formalities, re-issue, amend, extend dates, or suspend the RFA at its discretion.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program supports digital equity and inclusion by providing new, internet-enabled devices to eligible households. The program addresses the need for devices among Marylanders who cannot afford to purchase them, working alongside discounted and free internet services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of internet-enabled devices (HP Chromebook 14 G7 or similar) to county and municipal governments for distribution to eligible households. A $6 per device stipend is available to help cover distribution costs. Round one awarded 91,300 devices; round two will award remaining devices with priority for new eligible applicants.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 29, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County and municipal government entities distributing devices to eligible households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Distribution of internet-enabled devices to households with income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines, with one device per household address
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide
requirements_list: Eligible households have income at or below 200% of Federal Poverty Guidelines
One device per household address maximum
Program performance period is 6 months

structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: No-cost grants for eligible income-qualified participants to make energy-saving upgrades to their homes.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and single-family renters in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy-saving upgrades including energy-efficient appliances, heating and cooling system repairs or replacements, insulation replacement, and other energy efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Income-eligible

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides low-interest construction loans or loan enhancements to support the building of energy-efficient homes that produce as much or more energy than they use. Eligible projects include new construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest construction loans available to builders, developers, owners, and investors building or retrofitting in Maryland. Interest rates range from 3% to 5% for market-rate projects and 2% to 4% for projects where more than 50% of units are at or below 60% of Area Median Income, depending on HERS score. Loan-to-value up to 90%. Administration fee of 1% of total loan, appraisal fee of $290, and title fees apply. Construction period typically 12 months with 12-month loan repayment period for projects for sale. Loan enhancements available for applicants using private lenders. An additional fee may apply if funding is provided as a loan. Borrowers must provide ACORD certificates for property/builder's risk and borrower's liability insurance with DHCD listed as certificate holder and additional insured.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Open until available funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, investors, and non-profit organizations constructing or retrofitting homes to net-zero energy standards.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or deep energy retrofit of residential homes to achieve net-zero energy status with HERS rating of 50 or lower.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be constructed or rehabilitated in Maryland in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes and be properly zoned for residential use. Property must not be in a flood hazard area.
requirements_list: Qualified to do business in Maryland
Have legal capacity and all necessary authorization to incur the obligation of the loan
Demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability acceptable to the department
Demonstrate ability to complete the project
New construction or deep energy retrofit of existing home
Must reach low energy status with HERS rating of 50 or lower
Properly zoned for residential use
Must be constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes
Property must not be in a flood hazard area
Provide Certificate of Good Standing, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, and Corporate Resolutions (if applicable)
Submit Financial Statements
Provide evidence of ownership (Deed or Purchase Contract) and Zoning Letter
Provide Property/Builder's Risk insurance with DHCD as certificate holder and Mortgagee/Lender Loss Payable
Provide Borrower's Liability insurance with DHCD as certificate holder and additional insured
