structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps county jurisdictions pay for capital construction costs to install broadband service in remote or difficult-to-serve properties. The program addresses geographic barriers that discourage internet service providers from delivering service to these locations. Funding is provided through the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), Capital Projects Fund (CPF) administered by the United States Treasury to facilitate partnerships between local county jurisdictions and internet service providers to extend existing broadband service to unserved difficult-to-serve premises.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $1,100,000 per eligible county jurisdiction applicant for capital construction costs of broadband service installation in difficult-to-serve properties. Maximum funding per unserved location is $8,000. Required cash match of 25% of eligible project costs, which can be provided by the local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination of sources including foundations or non-profit agencies. Match contributions from local jurisdiction and/or ISP partner receive greater consideration. Projects with match commitments exceeding the required 25% receive additional consideration. The OSB will review applications to ensure no duplication of funding from federal or state sources. Applicants must pay all non-capital expenses related to required state and federal reporting and ongoing administrative costs for the duration of the project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions developing sub-grant programs with internet service provider partners to extend broadband service to unserved difficult-to-serve premises
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation to premises with difficulty obtaining service due to remoteness, distance from infrastructure, or other geographic issues. Eligible uses include: construction of facilities to deploy service to difficult-to-serve premises beyond standard ISP construction practices; minor extensions of ISP existing infrastructure; electronics necessary to deliver service including Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters; satellite receiving equipment for satellite providers meeting program requirements. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; focus on unserved difficult-to-serve properties lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local county jurisdiction
Applicant must have entered into partnership with an ISP partner or partners prior to funding agreement
ISP partner must participate in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
Maximum funding per location: $8,000
Maximum funding per applicant: $1,100,000
Required match: 25% of eligible capital construction costs (must be in form of cash; in-kind matches not acceptable)

Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds, or with proper certification, 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds (network must be scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical speeds)
Eligible locations must be unserved premises lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds
All equipment and materials purchased must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant responsible for developing jurisdictional-specific funding program
Program must include outreach component to promote the program
Program must address treatment of financially distressed property owners
ISP must promote ACP and provide assistance to those wishing to utilize the program
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025
No duplication of existing broadband service or other state, local, federal funding for the location
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application response to osb.md@maryland.gov on or before December 22, 2023 with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and local county jurisdiction name. All application items must be combined into one zip file (.zip) to ensure submission is bound together. File names should clearly identify file contents. If application exceeds email size limits, files may be uploaded to Google Drive or cloud service with link shared. Required application components include: completed FY24 Grant Application Form, Executive Summary describing unserved premises to be served and community problems/benefits, Application Partnership section naming ISP partner(s), Experience statement for senior team from both Applicant and ISP Partner, Network Discussion describing ISP partner network, technology, speed capabilities and offerings, Subscriber Profile with demographic data, Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing service options and pricing, Budget estimate of capital construction costs, Program Overview with sufficient detail on end user selection, low-income assistance, billing methods, ACP promotion and assistance, Schedule with key milestones assuming Spring 2024 start. Certifications required from both Local Jurisdictional Applicant and ISP Partner. Applications scored on high to low basis as funding permits with maximum 45 points based on: Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source and Percentage (up to 15 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 5 points), and Subscriber Options including affordability programs (up to 20 points). Awards intended to be facilitated in February 2024.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program designed to help Housing Voucher participants achieve higher education, improve employment status, and guide them toward self-sufficiency. The program evaluates skills and determines family needs, providing guidance in financial literacy, job training, childcare, and other support to help participants gain success in the workforce and achieve economic independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 5-year contract (extendable for up to 2 additional years with good cause) between participants and FSS case managers. Participants complete a Needs Assessment and develop an individual family plan with goals including obtaining employment and becoming free of temporary cash assistance (TANF). All FSS participants are eligible for an interest-bearing escrow account. As employment wages increase, the difference between rent increases is credited to the escrow account monthly. Participants who successfully complete contract goals, maintain suitable employment, and become free of TANF receive all escrow funds plus interest, which are nontaxable according to IRS guidelines. Case managers connect families with community supportive services including childcare, education, employment counseling, financial literacy, health services, homeownership assistance, job training and retention, and transportation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Housing Voucher participants seeking to improve their employment status, education level, and achieve economic self-sufficiency. Eligible participants include families receiving assistance under Housing Voucher programs, including disabled individuals who can designate another adult household member as head of household.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Support for pursuing higher education, job training, employment advancement, financial literacy, childcare, health services, homeownership, entrepreneurship, and achieving economic independence. Escrow funds can be used for any purpose once contract is completed, including down payments on homes, vehicle repair, testing fees, or other goals supporting the family's self-sufficiency plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Cambridge, Maryland area (Dorchester County); broader eligibility available throughout Maryland for Housing Voucher participants.
requirements_list: Must be a Housing Voucher participant
Must complete an application and sign a Contract of Participation
Must complete a Needs Assessment with FSS coordinator
Must establish goals including obtaining employment and becoming free of TANF benefits (social security and assistance for disabled family members do not count toward TANF requirement)
Can join at any time after receiving rental assistance
Participation is voluntary
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested individuals can contact DHCD by phone at 410-901-4080 or email fss.dhcd@maryland.gov, visit dhcd.maryland.gov/CambridgeCEC, ask their case manager at any meeting or redetermination, or complete an online FSS Inquiry Form at dhcd.wufoo.com/forms/family-selfsufficiency-program. The head of household meets with an FSS coordinator to review the family's strengths, barriers, and goals, and creates an individual family plan. Once the application is submitted, the head of household signs a Contract of Participation and completes a Needs Assessment. The FSS case manager then assists the family with creating realistic and achievable goals and directs them to supportive services from the community.

structured_extraction.program_name: HAF WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Grant helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by providing grants for critical repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. Without addressing these repairs, it will cause the homeowner to be involuntarily displaced from the property. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $10,000 grant per project for critical home repairs. There is no minimum amount. The grant is non-lien assistance with no deed of trust recorded on the property. Payment can be structured as either 33% deposit with 67% at completion or 0% deposit with 100% at completion, based on applicant preference. This is one-time financial assistance per household.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners experiencing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic who need critical repairs to their primary residence to avoid involuntary displacement.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs to primary residences including mold/mildew remediation, asbestos removal, no heat/no air conditioning, electrical repairs, plumbing and septic repairs, wells, roof repair/replacement, lead paint hazard reduction/elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip hazards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for primary residences. County-specific income limits apply based on 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI).
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship due to COVID-19 after January 21, 2020
Income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI) based on household size
Must be a Maryland homeowner of the subject property
Must reside in the primary residence as principal residence
Must be named on the deed of the property
If others are named on the deed but do not occupy the property, proof must be provided that they live elsewhere (driver's license copy, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
Must provide at least one detailed work proposal estimate dated within the last 60 days from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor
Contractor must be currently licensed with the State of Maryland and in good standing
Contractor must have active liability insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000
Work proposal must include photographs documenting the critical repairs
Applicant must attest to COVID-19 financial hardship
No minimum credit score required
One-time assistance per household only
Payments or deposits made by homeowners for work or materials will not be reimbursed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application. 2) Gather and submit required income documentation including photo ID, paystubs (or employer verification letter), tax returns if self-employed, award letters for Social Security/disability/pension/public assistance, and notarized zero income statement if applicable. 3) Provide proof of home ownership and documentation that any other deed holders live elsewhere if applicable. 4) Obtain at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor dated within the past 60 days that includes: photographs of the critical repairs, scope of work, contractor's phone and email, and total cost not exceeding $10,000. 5) Contractor must complete the Bid Cover Page and provide: current MHIC or Trade License, Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with $1M+ per occurrence), Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form. 6) Select payment preference: 33% deposit with 67% at completion OR 0% deposit with 100% at completion. 7) Submit completed application and all supporting documentation by email to Rehab.HAFApplications@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs- Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 8) Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. 9) Once approved, applicant must sign: commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor(s) certifying work completion. 10) DHCD staff reviews estimates to verify work meets health and safety requirements and contractor meets State of Maryland business requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to support affordable housing development. The program helps build, buy, or rehabilitate rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds are used primarily to serve very low-income and low-income households at or below 80% of area median household income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds may be provided as non-interest bearing or deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years depending on the type of housing financed, as amortizing loans, as recoverable grants requiring repayment upon sale or discontinuation of low-income use, or as outright grants at the State's discretion. The maximum amount of assistance to a single project generally will not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable. For rental housing projects, HOME funds are targeted to serve households at or below 80% of area median household income. For owner-occupied housing and homeownership projects, HOME funds are targeted to serve households at or below 80% of area median household income. Equity sharing for rental projects may be required when low-income usage is discontinued, with the State sharing in proportion to the amount of HOME funds involved. If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with CDA. HOME funds are disbursed among multifamily rental housing programs, single-family homeownership programs, and the HOME Special Reserve Fund. The HOME Special Reserve Fund uses up to 5% of HOME allocation for special projects or programs that fill a need not met by existing housing programs, with first-come, first-serve basis allocation and priority given to Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing; Special Reserve Fund applications reviewed on first-come, first-serve basis
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dale Quisgard, HOME Program Manager; Kiaya Nickens, Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) seeking to develop affordable housing for low-income residents. Special Reserve Fund applications from CHDOs and non-profit organizations as well as local governments applying in conjunction with non-profits are given priority.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building, buying, or rehabilitating rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. Funds may be used for soft seconds to reduce home costs, land acquisition, development costs, and construction financing. Funds may also be used for acquisition of properties for resale or rental, rehabilitation of owner-occupied housing, tenant-based rental assistance on a limited basis including security deposit assistance and disaster relief. HOME funds may be combined with existing DHCD programs including Community Development Programs, Homeownership Programs, and Special Loan Programs. Funds may not be used for activities that do not comply with federal HOME regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland counties except Baltimore City and Anne Arundel except City of Annapolis, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct HOME allocations). State government agencies are automatically eligible for HOME funds and receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater. For FFY 2023, the State of Maryland received $7,319,907.00 in federal HOME funds.
requirements_list: For rental housing units, residents' household incomes must be 50% or less of the area median household income (based on household size, set annually by HUD), or up to 80% for very low-income targeting

For owner-occupied housing units, the owner's household income must be 55% or less of the area median household income (based on household size, set annually by HUD), or up to 80% for homeownership projects

The number of income-restricted units is usually calculated by dividing the amount of HOME funds by the total cost of the project, then multiplying that result by the total number of units in the project, though in some cases proportionality may not be feasible such as when there are high development costs or an area with low median incomes
Projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements when using HOME funds in conjunction with other CDA programs
If the property is sold or stops being used for low-income housing, the borrower must share any equity gain with CDA

Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) must be certified by the State and may receive up to 15% of the State's HOME formula allocation; CHDO set-asides must include at least 15% of the State's HOME formula allocation with up to 10% available for predevelopment costs

For CHDOs receiving operating assistance, organizations must provide financial statements and evidence of good standing; may not receive more than 50% of operating expenses or $50,000 maximum per year (up to $30,000 for newly formed CHDOs); must enter written agreement to receive project development funding within 24 months; must be recertified annually meeting all HUD requirements

CHDO predevelopment loans available up to $50,000 for feasibility or site control costs; non-amortizing principal-only with repayment due at settlement; expected to be repaid through project financing though Department may waive repayment if project cannot support cost through no fault of borrower
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications may be submitted as part of project applications for use of HOME funds or DHCD staff may propose the use of HOME funds during project evaluation and underwriting. HOME Special Reserve Fund applications are reviewed and funds allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs and non-profit organizations. Applications from Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs) and non-profit organizations as well as local governments applying in conjunction with non-profits receive priority. Rating criteria include readiness to proceed, demonstrated ability, matching contributions, geographic distribution, and performance and disbursements on prior HOME awards. Awards are recommended to the Director of the Community Development Administration and HFRC for approval if applications are part of a competitive round. Special Reserve Fund applications must demonstrate how the project fills a need not met by other DHCD housing programs or addresses an existing program at full funding. For CHDO operating assistance, organizations must enter into a written agreement and meet recertification requirements annually. For CHDO predevelopment loans, nonprofits may request up to $50,000 on a first-come, first-serve basis with preference given to applications that provide a match.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: This initiative helps families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, in partnership with the Maryland Department of Health, pays for lead elimination from houses or apartments where children live or spend time, at no cost to the owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Covers lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed for eligible families with children who have elevated blood lead levels. The program pays for lead elimination from the house or apartment where the child lives or spends time, at no cost to the owner or tenant.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under age 19 living in Maryland who have elevated blood lead levels and are enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in homes, apartments, or day care facilities where children live or spend time
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Child must be under 19 years old
Child must live in Maryland
Child must have recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL) or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location where lead exposure occurred (home, apartment, or day care)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 (toll-free) or email mdh.healthyhomes@maryland.gov to inquire about eligibility and program details. You may also contact your local health department for more information. Visit the Maryland Department of Health website for additional information and application details.

structured_extraction.program_description: This grant program helps public housing owners install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units and provides free WiFi in common areas. The program addresses digital equity and inclusion issues by ensuring low-income residents in publicly-owned housing can access broadband service. Funding is available through two rounds: the original Round 1 for publicly owned housing and an expanded round for municipally owned and non-profit affordable housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1 (Publicly Owned Housing): Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with required 5% match. Expanded Round (FY24 Affordable Housing - Municipally Owned/Non-Profit): Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible costs with required 5% match. Total funding for expanded round is $26.9 million. Grants fund installation of broadband-capable internal wiring to individual dwelling units, extension of fiber optic facilities, installation of wireless access points in common areas providing free broadband service, and educational/technical assistance for broadband adoption including ACP registration assistance. Non-capital administrative costs are capped at 1% of total project costs (or up to 3% for engagement costs not to exceed $15,000). All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 7, 2025 (Expanded Round); December 22, 2023 (Round 1)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Round 1: Owners of public housing including municipal and non-profit entities, and internet service providers. Expanded Round: Internet Service Providers serving municipally owned or non-profit low-income multi-dwelling units (MDUs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable internal wiring to individual dwelling units in public/affordable housing, extension of fiber optic facilities to housing structures, installation of wireless access points in common areas providing free WiFi service, community engagement activities including ACP registration assistance and broadband education, engineering and design services, broadband networking equipment, low voltage contracting work, network installation and configuration labor costs, and taxes/shipping/insurance costs directly related to broadband equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; eligible for publicly owned housing developments or municipally owned/non-profit low-income multi-dwelling units identified as having a need for additional broadband investment including lack of access to reliable connections meeting minimum speeds or lack of affordable access.
requirements_list: Round 1 grant range: $500,000 to $9,000,000; Expanded Round range: $250,000 to $5,000,000
5% match of eligible project costs required (can be other local, state, or federal funds)
Applicant must own and maintain publicly supported housing (Round 1) or be an existing ISP with letter of support from municipal/non-profit property owner (Expanded Round)

Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at each dwelling unit (or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable to 100/100 with documented justification)
For Expanded Round: ISP must verify municipal or non-profit ownership status with documentation (IRS 501(c)(3) for non-profits)
Applicant must agree to maintain and secure equipment and acquire hardware warranty and service agreement for at least 5 years after project completion
Installation of wireless access points in common areas providing free broadband service required
Community engagement strategies including ACP registration assistance must be in place during project development
Projects must be completed by June 30, 2026 (Round 1)
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
All projects must comply with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) and Treasury Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (CPF) requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Round 1: Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application package including application form, project summary (executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost information, potential barriers, partners/engagement, schedule, and funding scope/budget), and supporting documentation to osb.md@maryland.gov with subject line including 'Broadband for Public Housing', jurisdiction name, and project name. Expanded Round: Submit applications via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov including completed application form, project detail with executive summary, statement of experience, letter of support from property owners, project proposal, MDU prioritization information, network design and engineering diagrams, community profile, subscriber cost, barriers/risks/mitigation, partners and engagement, schedule, funding scope and budget, sustainability plan, and financial information. All applications must include IRS W-9 form and all required sections to be considered complete. Applications are scored based on project impact and need, technical feasibility, match contribution percentage, cost effectiveness, network delivery speed, latency, affordable internet plans, low-cost offerings, and sustainability/maintenance plan.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and support innovative solutions to housing scarcity. The program also allows counties to purchase existing privately owned housing in conjunction with local housing authorities or housing developers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to support rental housing development projects, including new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation. Funds can also be used for purchasing existing privately owned housing. Loan terms available: Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate, or longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP loans are subordinate loans, with positioning considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum award per project is $2.5 million. Total FY 2026 funding available is $5 million with maximum of one award per jurisdiction. Loans will follow DHCD's Multifamily Fee Schedule.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments, particularly those partnering with housing developers to create mixed-income rental housing.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing, including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing with affordability requirements. Projects can acquire land, conduct new construction, acquire and substantially renovate multifamily properties, or acquire multifamily properties without major renovation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide program available to all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government
Projects must partner with a housing developer or county must partner with a PHA or developer to acquire existing housing
Sponsor must have ownership interest in project's ownership entity as demonstrated by organizational chart and/or partnership agreement

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, OR at least 40% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing
Projects must be proposed in Maryland
Application fee of $2,500 required
Applications must be submitted electronically via Procorem WorkCenter
Application must include completed Application Submission Kit with CDA Form 202 dated March 2025, Form 203, and Form 209
Projects must adhere to DHCD Multifamily Policies regarding construction standards and individual unit health and safety requirements
Projects must comply with fair housing and equal opportunity laws
No tenant living in residential units has been forced to move without cause in the 12 months preceding application submission
Projects must be ready for occupancy within two years of award selection date
Must meet Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide threshold requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Request pre-application meeting using Pre-Application Meeting Request Form (optional). 2) Submit waiver requests if applicable using Waiver Request Form at least 15 days prior to deadline (by May 4, 2026). 3) Request electronic application folder using Electronic Submission Package Request Form in Multifamily Library. 4) Prepare and submit complete electronic Application Submission Package including: Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application, CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application (Excel Document dated February 2025), Certifications, Threshold Checklist, Applicant Self-Scoring, Organizational Chart, Developer/Owner qualifications (Form 203), General Contractor qualifications (AIA Document A305), Architect qualifications, Property Manager qualifications (Form 209), Development Team information with references, and other required exhibits. 5) Submit $2,500 application fee separately to Community Development Administration, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784 under separate cover with copy included in application submission. 6) Submit complete application electronically via Procorem WorkCenter with all sections, attachments, and exhibits clearly tabbed. 7) Applications received by DHCD staff will be reviewed for completeness - incomplete submissions will not be processed further. 8) Complete applications will be scored by DHCD scoring committee. 9) Proposals ranked according to score; highest-scored proposal recommended to CDA Director for approval, then submitted to Secretary for final approval and allocation. 10) DHCD may select only one project per jurisdiction. Virtual information session held March 11, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial assistance to eligible applicants for independent living modifications and improvements.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants who are approved receive a tax credit certificate issued by DHCD.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to make independent living modifications and improvements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent living modifications and improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (Maryland).
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and supporting documents online or via paper form by the June 1st deadline. DHCD will review applications by August 31st. If approved, applicants will be notified and issued a tax credit certificate. DHCD may request additional information if needed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help homeowners install or repair indoor plumbing in residential properties, including wells, septic systems, water and sewer connections, and plumbing fixtures.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay and household income. Interest rates range from 4.5% to 6.0% for households at 80% of median income, and 0% to 4.5% for households at 60% of median income. Households at 50% or below of median income may be eligible for deferred principal and interest with no repayment capability. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Deferred loans are available for families with incomes at or below 50% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. Deferred loan amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes below 30% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes who are income-eligible, and owners of rental residential properties whose units will be occupied by income-eligible households.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into buildings, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications to provide private space for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, percolation test costs, and alternative and innovative septic and water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Loan requests are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. Counties in the Washington, D.C. PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's) may have different income limits than the rest of the state.
requirements_list: Single-family, owner-occupied house with inoperative, unsafe, or non-functional plumbing
Property must be structurally sound
Owner-occupants must have income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
For rental properties, residents of assisted units must have income at or below 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Applicants must provide a work proposal with scope of work from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or other trade professional
Applicants must provide photos documenting the plumbing issues

Contractor must provide current MHIC License or appropriate trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form
Property must have valid homeowner's insurance
Funding requests should not exceed $50,000
Applicant must own the property (deed required as proof of ownership)
Lead-based paint disclosure requirements apply for homes built before 1978
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Applicants contact their local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs. 2. Applicants must complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application with full documentation of income, assets, liabilities, and property information. 3. Applicants must provide proof of home ownership (deed, current mortgage statement, and property tax bill). 4. Applicants must obtain bids from licensed Maryland contractors that include scope of work, photographs, contractor contact information, MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form. 5. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. Applications are reviewed for income eligibility based on household size and statewide or Washington D.C. MSA median income limits. 7. Loans are originated, packaged, and closed by the Special Loan Program's network of local administering agencies, which includes county housing and community development offices, nonprofit organizations, and local banks.

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant and loan program administered by DHCD to assist Maryland homeowners, landlords, and licensed childcare facilities lessen the risk of lead poisoning and preserve housing stock by reducing or eliminating lead-based paint hazards. DHCD provides grants of up to $25,000 per property for lead abatement services performed by licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors. The program applies to both single-family homes and multi-family properties. Funding is available statewide except in the City of Baltimore.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Three assistance options are available: (1) Grants: Up to $25,000 per eligible property with no repayment required. Annual sponsor maximum of $100,000. Match requirements vary: 20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median AMI, and no match for owner-occupants with limited incomes (below 80% of median AMI). Grants require property to be in target area or utilize innovative lead hazard reduction treatment, and underwriting must show no affordability to repay loan or insufficient property value to secure debt. (2) Amortizing Loans: Up to $25,000 per property at 0%-7% interest over 20 years with 100% debt-to-value. (3) Deferred Loans: Up to $25,000 per property at 0% interest over 20 years. Loan forgiveness may be considered if no equity is available to repay upon resale, transfer, or after 20 years. All assistance must be used for lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Clearance testing is required. Available statewide except in the City of Baltimore. Funding available until April 1, 2029.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, landlords, and licensed childcare facilities seeking to reduce lead-based paint hazards and prevent lead poisoning. Includes individuals and non-profit organizations that own residential properties or daycare centers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduction or elimination of lead-based paint hazards, including lead abatement services performed by a licensed and accredited lead abatement contractor. Clearance testing is required. Funds support the removal of lead paint in residential buildings and daycare centers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide except in the City of Baltimore.
requirements_list: Property must be owner-occupied single family home or rental property
For owner-occupants: must be Maryland resident, own and occupy dwelling as principal residence
Units must be in need of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be structurally sound upon completion of lead hazard reduction activity
Units must be registered with Maryland Department of the Environment Lead Poisoning Prevention Program
Licensed childcare facilities (including licensed day care centers) may also be eligible
For grants: property must be in target area or utilize innovative lead hazard reduction treatment
For grants: underwriting must show no affordability to repay loan or property does not have sufficient value to secure debt
Clearance testing is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Homeowners should start with a free, in-home comprehensive assessment to identify needed repairs and enroll in programs suited to their situation. Contact Special Loan Programs at the provided phone or email to begin the application process. Use the Application Form or Sponsor Application Form available on the website. For-profit sponsors must pay all fees and charges associated with application and closing. Nonprofit sponsors and owner-occupants of limited income may include fees in financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance community infrastructure projects. The program reduces financing costs through economies of scale by pooling local demand and provides expertise in managing bond issuance. It provides long-term capital financing for projects like streetscape improvements, transportation enhancements, water and sewer treatment facilities, and other public infrastructure. Local governments borrow the bond proceeds at market rates and repay the debt.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on local government loans is based on market conditions at the time of bond sale. Loan terms are set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less. Loan amounts can range from $150,000 to $10 million or more. Each participant pledges its full faith and credit to secure repayment. Local governments are responsible for repaying the debt and paying their pro-rata share of bond issuance costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies that have legal authority to construct, operate and maintain the proposed project, pledge security for and repay the loan, and pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system and may include: street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, and maintenance facilities; and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Legal authority to construct, operate and maintain the proposed project
Legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or 30 years, whichever is less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that requests information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate creditworthiness. Technical assistance is available through the Community Development Administration to help with the application. Interested parties may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions. When bonds are issued is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private investment in the construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis according to the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The tax credit equals the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the Internal Revenue Service. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return. Credits are allocated annually with amounts varying by year. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Typically announced annually; contact program for current deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit sponsors developing low-income rental housing projects. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties are eligible. A residential rental building must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made. Properties must meet Qualified Census Tract (QCT) or Difficult Development Area (DDA) requirements as defined by IRS.
requirements_list: Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes of 50 percent or less of area median income or 40 percent of units to households with incomes of 60 percent or less of area median income
Building must comply with requirements regarding tenant income, maximum rent levels, and percentage of low-income occupancy
Building must remain in compliance and is subject to covenant to enforce compliance for minimum of 40 years (Initial Compliance Period) followed by Extended Use Period of at least 15 additional years
Owner must submit annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Compliance (OCPC)
Owner must maintain tenant income certifications and supporting documentation for all low-income units
Building must meet physical inspections and pass management and file reviews
Owner must obtain and maintain annual tenant income verifications for Initial Compliance Period; less frequent verification allowed during Extended Use Period with exemption for 100% LIHTC buildings

For Initial Compliance Period: annual full tenant recertification required; during Extended Use Period: full recertification at least every five years with annual self-declarations in non-full-recertification years

Owner must maintain detailed project files including recorded covenant, management plan, tenant selection plan, management agreement, IRS Forms 8609/8586, regulatory documents, and utility allowance documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted competitively based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The QAP is updated periodically and published by DHCD. Potential applicants should review the current QAP for specific application requirements, scoring criteria, and submission procedures. Projects financed with tax-exempt bonds may be eligible outside of the competitive process. Interested parties should contact the program for details on current application cycles, required documentation, and specific submission deadlines. The Community Development Administration (CDA) reviews applications and makes allocation recommendations. Once allocated, property owners must work with CDA through project development, placement in service, and ongoing compliance monitoring throughout both the Initial Compliance Period (15 years) and Extended Use Period (at least 15 additional years).

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program to further Maryland's digital inclusion efforts by enabling access to high-speed internet and expanding digital literacy. The program funds local jurisdictions, 501(c) non-profit organizations, and community-based anchor institutions to advance digital inclusion efforts through both digital inclusion planning and implementation of digital inclusion programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Digital Inclusion Planning: grants cover up to 50% of planning costs with maximum grant of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. Digital Inclusion Implementation: grants cover up to 100% of implementation costs with maximum grant of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Total program funding is $2 million. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds administered by the US Treasury. Grant funds may be used for: developing digital inclusion plans; implementing digital inclusion activities; facilitating broadband adoption for covered populations for educational and employment opportunities; implementing training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; constructing, upgrading, expanding, or operating public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; and researching populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers. Grant funds may not be used for construction of broadband infrastructure. Only fully complete applications will be considered for funding. Grant amounts may be reduced based on impact and ability to deploy funds responsibly and quickly. Successful applicants will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining the obligations of the awardee and State to the Project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022 (REVISED)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties or municipalities), 501(c) non-profit organizations, community-based anchor institutions, and covered populations including individuals with low income, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers or low literacy, racial or ethnic minorities, and rural residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To develop digital inclusion plans and implement digital inclusion activities; to facilitate broadband adoption for covered populations for educational and employment opportunities; to implement training programs covering basic, advanced, and applied skills or workforce development programs; to construct, upgrade, expand, or operate public access computing centers for covered populations through community anchor institutions; to research and identify populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Services must be provided within the State of Maryland. Covered populations receiving priority include individuals with household income less than or equal to 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers (including English learners and individuals with low literacy levels), individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals who primarily reside in rural areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local government (county or municipality), a nonprofit IRS-approved 501(c) entity providing services within Maryland, or a community-based anchor institution
Digital Inclusion Planning: minimum grant request $5,000, maximum $30,000
Digital Inclusion Implementation: minimum grant request $10,000, maximum $75,000
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Only fully complete applications will be considered for funding

Applications must include completed and signed application form, executive summary with project overview, population needs, barriers, partners, intended outcomes and metrics, and statement of experience
Scope of work and simple budget must be provided with spending categories for operations, contracted services, travel, and other funding sources

Budget must identify spending: Operations (payroll, supplies, materials); Contracted services (payments to independent contractors, external organizations); Travel (related to program deployment); and any other funding necessary for the project including anticipated sources
IRS Determination Letter of nonprofit status required if applicable
Online verification of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation required
IRS W-9 Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification required
Dun & Bradstreet DUNS Number required for the organization
Applicants are encouraged to identify other funding sources to leverage the available grant funding

A list of community partners and their involvement in the planning process or support of digital inclusion must be included; if not a local jurisdictional agency, indicate whom you are working with from the local jurisdiction
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: NOFA issued February 9, 2022. Application submission opens February 15, 2022 and closes March 31, 2022. Submit all applications and supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov with subject line: 'MD-DIG: Name of Applying Organization'. Include the following attachments: (1) executive summary of the project, (2) project budget, (3) Federal Form W-9. Funding announcements to be made on or before April 15, 2022. It is the OSB's intent to award funds beginning in May 2022. Successful applicants will be chosen based on qualifications, evaluation of responses, and possible interview. The OSB reserves the right to conduct discussions or negotiations for maximum clarification and completeness of proposals.

structured_extraction.program_name: MEER: Maryland Emergency Education Relief Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to help K-12 students and school staff access the internet and devices needed to connect to classrooms. The program closes the gap for students lacking internet access or required technology for remote learning.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to eligible organizations for broadband access and device connectivity projects. Grant awards varied by project, ranging from approximately $34,000 to $250,000. Projects funded through this program were completed during the FY2022 period (September 1, 2021 through September 15, 2022). Total MEER program funding awarded was $4,999,251.80 across multiple jurisdictions including Baltimore, Baltimore City, Cecil, Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard, and Wicomico counties.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program period: September 1, 2021 to September 15, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: K-12 schools, libraries, anchor institutions, community organizations, government entities, and non-profit organizations serving K-12 students and low-income communities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Broadband access and device connectivity for K-12 students, including funding for qualified equipment and infrastructure projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - awards were distributed across Baltimore, Baltimore City, Cecil, Montgomery, Prince George's, Howard, and Wicomico counties
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include schools, libraries, anchor institutions, community organizations, and government entities
Projects must be completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
Projects must address broadband access and device connectivity for K-12 students and/or low-income communities
Applicants must demonstrate how the project serves vulnerable populations lacking internet access or technology
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application according to program guidelines and requirements through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Operating assistance grants for Main Street improvements. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation receive approximately $33,000 each. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive approximately $25,000 each. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Funds support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Grants can be used for staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives and other projects identified in the applicant's work plans as key to Main Street efforts. All projects and activities should be completed within one year; a funding match is not required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Funds support projects and activities that align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the transformation strategy of the community. Capital project costs are not supported.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated and Aspiring Main Street Maryland communities throughout the state. Designated Sustainable Community areas throughout Maryland, with additional consideration for projects in designated ENOUGH areas and Just Communities.
requirements_list: Only designated and aspiring Main Street Maryland communities are eligible
Projects and activities must align with the applicant's annual work plan
Projects and activities must contribute to the transformation strategy of the community
All projects and activities must be completed within one year
Operating expenses only; capital project costs are not supported
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing (Md. State Department of Assessments and Taxation), and evidence of charitable registration (Md. Secretary of State)
Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements
Awardees must meet all reporting deadlines and submit all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through the Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. Register as a new user if needed; approval may take up to 72 hours. New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting. Application period opens Friday, February 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM EDT and closes Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT. Late applications will not be accepted. All applications must be submitted online through the DHCD Project Portal. Training documents, including a program overview and step-by-step application guide, are available in the DHCD Project Portal. Virtual application training and individual technical assistance sessions are available. Applications must align with the Main Street annual work plan. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants. The Department may also contact applicants for follow-up discussions prior to award decisions. Successful applicants will receive official award letters through the Project Portal. Award recommendations are subject to review and approval by the Secretary of DHCD. Final authorization of award amounts is contingent upon approval by the General Assembly during the FY2027 legislative session.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency loan program that provides financial assistance to small businesses affected by disasters. The program is only activated by the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development for specific declared disasters.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans for small businesses to cover renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and certain other costs associated with business recovery. The program provides working capital and recovery funding for eligible businesses.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Colleen Cord-Malone, Business Lending Programs Manager II; Aisha K. Taylor, Business Lending Programs Loan Underwriter
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland-based small businesses and nonprofit organizations located in commercial spaces that have been affected by declared disasters.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and certain other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County and must show evidence of damage or loss associated with the May 2018 flooding events.
requirements_list: Maryland-based small business or nonprofit organization
Business must be located in a commercial space
Applicant must show proof of insurance status
Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Must show evidence of damage or loss associated with May 2018 flooding events
Cannot be residential or transient living businesses such as multifamily or single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living facilities, or homeless shelters
Cannot be public facilities such as community halls, fire stations, hospitals, colleges, or universities

Cannot be adult bookstores, adult video shops, gambling facilities, gun shops, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, or tattoo parlors unless the project includes another eligible business type
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Neighborhood BusinessWorks Program at 1-800-756-0119 or 301-429-7408 to inquire about program activation and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses access financing by enabling private lenders to establish a loan loss reserve fund. The program uses contributions from lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland to reduce lender risk on loans that fall slightly outside normal credit guidelines. The program supports businesses located in Priority Funding Areas across Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program works through participating lenders who enroll appropriate loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Lender, borrower, and the program each contribute to a reserve account (typically 1.5 percent from lender, 1.5 percent from borrower, and 3 percent match from the program for a total reserve of 6 percent of the original loan amount). In case of loan default, the reserve account covers losses up to 75 percent of the account balance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses in Priority Funding Areas, including nonprofit organizations, seeking financing that may fall slightly outside traditional lender credit guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business loans for small business growth and expansion. Cannot be used for passive real estate ownership, residential housing, facilities such as hospitals or universities, adult entertainment, check cashing, gambling, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, tattoo parlors, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas as approved by the Maryland Department of Planning.
requirements_list: Business must be a small business located in Maryland
Business must be located in a Priority Funding Areas
Loan amount must range from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential housing or transient living facilities
Project cannot be certain restricted business types
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Small business applies to a participating lender. Lender underwrites and enrolls the loan. Lender, borrower, and program contribute to a reserve account. Lender submits one-page enrollment form to the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provided a monthly subsidy to help lower-income households afford internet service. It offered up to $15 per month off internet costs, in addition to the $30 per month federal Affordable Connectivity Program subsidy.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $15 per month subsidy off internet service costs for lower-income households, provided in addition to the federal Affordable Connectivity Program subsidy of $30 per month. The program worked with a wide range of participating internet service providers offering both fixed broadband and mobile broadband services throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lower-income households seeking affordable broadband connectivity
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Internet service costs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Lower-income household status
Must be a resident of Maryland
Must enroll with a participating internet service provider

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Facade Improvement Program provides funding to local governments and community development organizations for programs to improve the exteriors of commercial properties located within Maryland's Sustainable Communities. The program supports communities seeking to create consistent, attractive designs for their commercial corridors in order to bolster economic vitality and stimulate new private investments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funds are provided as grants to local governments, municipalities, and community development organizations to capitalize their own local facade improvement programs. Local programs then award grants to businesses for capital improvements to the exterior facades of commercial properties. Individual businesses can receive between $1,000 and $50,000 in MFIP funding per award cycle. Eligible capital improvements include signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Projects should prioritize aesthetic improvements over routine maintenance and focus on primary elevations of commercial properties.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Counties, municipalities, and community development organizations located in Sustainable Communities. Final recipients of funding must be businesses located within the State's designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvements to exterior facades of commercial properties including signage, exterior painting, storefront reconstruction, siding, exterior lighting, window and door upgrades, public-facing masonry or cornices, murals, removal of unattractive exterior finishes, and roofs. Individual business improvements must range from $1,000 to $50,000 per award cycle. Ineligible uses include interior work, electric charging stations, solar panels, improvements banned by local building codes, and predevelopment or operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland Facade Improvement Program funding can only be used in areas known as Sustainable Communities, which are geographic areas targeted for revitalization by local governments. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.

Applicant must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Applicant is responsible for compliance with all building codes, building permits, zoning requirements, and Historic Preservation Commission requirements
Applicant must maintain valid and sufficient insurance coverage
Applicant must provide evidence of expenditures for all approved improvements
Applicant agrees to maintain the property and improvements and remove graffiti promptly
Applicant agrees to return pro-rated grant funds if improvements are removed within two years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible applicants (counties, municipalities, and community development organizations) submit applications to DHCD for funding to establish or enhance local facade improvement programs. Applications should include evidence of site control, photographs of existing conditions, written consent from landlord and lessee as applicable, project description with two cost estimates and detailed sketches, and proof of business good standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation. DHCD reviews applications annually, with priority given to applications demonstrating strong local design guidelines, dedicated staff, track record of successful revitalization, and alignment with local Sustainable Communities Action Plans. Awardees then develop their own application process for individual businesses to apply for facade improvement grants. All projects undergo historic preservation review before work begins. Applicants should not begin work prior to receiving written approval from the program.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides affordable funding through special loan programs to help homeowners preserve and improve their single-family homes. The goal is to bring properties up to current building codes and standards, while also addressing critical health and safety problems including mold remediation, roof repair, lead abatement, electrical hazards, plumbing issues, structural repairs, and accessibility improvements for seniors and disabled residents. To qualify, a household's income must not be more than 80% of the Adjusted Median Income (statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area) set by DHCD each year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
