structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest loans with rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and household income. Households with incomes at 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income qualify for interest rates of 4.5% to 6.0%. Households with incomes at 60% of median income qualify for interest rates of 0% to 4.5%. Households with incomes at or below 50% of median income may qualify for deferred principal and interest payments if necessary for project feasibility. Maximum loan is generally $50,000 or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. Minimum loan is $5,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans over $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a deed of trust mortgage on the property. Grants may also be available in certain circumstances.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - no specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household income not exceeding 80 percent of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income needing repairs for health, safety, and building code compliance.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs and rehabilitation including mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing and drainage, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, electrical service upgrades for future home electrification (100A to 200A), plumbing issues, water and well repair, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion, structural repairs, accessibility improvements for disabled and seniors, fall and injury prevention, ductwork upgrades and installations, building shell stabilization, and pest treatments. All work must bring the property up to applicable building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Loans are processed by a network of local administering agencies including county offices and nonprofit organizations. Applicants should contact their local housing office by county. For specific county contacts, visit https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Residents/Pages/mhrp-sf/contactlist.aspx.
requirements_list: Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (duplexes, townhomes, condos, and manufactured homes excluded).
Household income cannot exceed 80% of statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area Adjusted Median Income (specific income limits vary by household size and region).
Property must be primary residence.
Provide a work proposal from a licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractor or other trade professional.
Provide photos documenting the issues requiring repair.

Contractor must provide current MHIC license or trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.), Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits of $1 million or greater, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form.
Bid must be dated within the past 60 days.
No active bankruptcy or foreclosure; if either occurred, must be dismissed for a minimum of 2 years before assistance can be provided.
Applicant must authorize credit pull and verification of income information.
Applicants must provide homeowner insurance information and flood insurance if applicable.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local housing office by county or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Special Loan Programs office at (301) 429-7409 or (877) 218-8101. 2. Obtain at least one detailed estimate from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or trade professional for the work needed, dated within the past 60 days, with photographs documenting the issues. 3. Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program application and submit with required documentation including: income verification (2 months paystubs or 2 years tax returns), proof of home ownership (deed and mortgage statement), property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance if applicable, and personal identification. 4. Provide contractor bid with completed Bid Cover Page and contractor documentation (MHIC or trade license, certificate of liability insurance, letter of good standing, and W-9 form). 5. Submit complete application and supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. DHCD staff will review the estimate to verify the work meets health and safety requirements and that the contractor meets State of Maryland requirements. 7. Once approved, applicant must sign commitment letter, rehabilitation contract, construction agreement, and W-9 form. 8. Loans are processed, packaged, and closed by the network of local administering agencies.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative designed to help certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses reduce the interest rate on loans they obtain from participating banks. Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on their loans to help them access affordable capital for growing and expanding their business.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating lenders offer loans at an interest rate up to 2% lower than the standard rate for similar loans. The state treasurer deposits an amount equal to the loan with the lending bank at a reduced interest rate. The interest rate reduction benefit is available for the full term of the loan, up to 10 years, for term loans only or loans with fixed rates and one disbursement. Loans cannot exceed 10 years and points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount. The program leverages $50 million of state funds. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds must be used for projects located in Maryland. Funds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.

requirements_list: Must be a certified minority business enterprise in good standing with the Maryland Department of Transportation, or a small business in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining the qualifying loan
Must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to maintain the interest rate reduction benefit
Loan must be obtained from a participating bank designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years
Loan proceeds must be for a project or activity located in Maryland
Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. The department verifies eligibility and forwards the application to all enrolled banks, or notifies the lender of the borrower's eligibility if the lender applied on behalf of the borrower. The borrower receives a list of participating banks and contacts them to complete full application requirements. Banks underwrite the loan according to their standard process and offer an interest rate up to 2% less than the standard rate. Upon loan approval and acceptance, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program. The state treasurer then deposits an amount equal to the loan with the bank at a reduced interest rate. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank with multiple contact representatives available.

The program uses federal funds to provide loans and equity investments to support small businesses, micro-businesses, and socially and economically disadvantaged individual (SEDI) businesses with limited opportunities for growth. It partners with the Maryland Department of Commerce and the Maryland Technology Development Corporation, targeting communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and SEDI businesses.

The program works through partnerships with community-based microlenders (Community Development Financial Institutions/CDFIs) who originate and administer loans and provide training and technical assistance. The program also provides loans directly to local CDFIs, which then lend money to small businesses in Maryland communities to support local economies.

No prepayment penalties apply. The program also offers loans directly to local CDFIs, which then lend to small businesses and microenterprises.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides tax-exempt bonds and notes to increase the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes. The financing can be used for new construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing rental housing with at least five units, and can be combined with federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (4% LIHTC under the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan). The program offers multiple financing structures including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing, GNMA MBS, Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, and FNMA MBS collateral options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing through multiple credit enhancement structures: FHA-CDA Risk Sharing with 40-year terms, GNMA MBS loans, Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans with 17-year terms, cash collateral structures, and FNMA MBS collateral options. Interest rates vary by structure (ranging from approximately 4.3% to 5.9% all-in rates based on 4/2/2026 indicative rates). Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years with permanent amortization periods of 35-40 years. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. The program participates in the Federal Housing Administration and Housing Finance Agency Risk Sharing Program. Projects may use 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits if they comply with the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan. Construction periods typically range from 20-24 months. Projects can combine taxable GNMA loans with tax-exempt bonds (Tax/TE Financing) to optimize interest rates and reduce borrowing costs.

Loans may also refinance existing high interest rate private loans if the refinance is in conjunction with housing rehabilitation. Financing can support projects using HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or similar HUD programs.

All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Prospective borrowers should contact CDA Multifamily staff to discuss project financing structure and options. CDA staff can meet with prospective borrowers to answer questions and guide through the underwriting process. structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - EmPOWER
structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides grants or loans to reduce electric or gas consumption in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Funding can be used for energy efficiency measures and limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects that reduce energy consumption. All building sizes and configurations are eligible, including single family units as group projects, individually metered, or master metered buildings. The program also includes the MEEHA Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) for electrification of covered buildings. It aims to reduce greenhouse gases and keep housing affordable.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides funding through grants or loans with 0% interest and deferred payments. Funding is allocated at $134.9 million for calendar years 2024-2026. Projects must maintain a minimum of 20% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 5 years (Tier 1) or 15 years (Tier 2) of affordability compliance. Tier 1 projects receive standard funding amounts, while Tier 2 projects with 15+ years of affordability receive enhanced funding. Maximum funding amounts vary by measure type and tier level. For GHGRP, funding is limited to $15,000 per unit. All building sizes and configurations are eligible, including single family units as group projects, individually metered, or master metered buildings. Funding can cover energy audits (up to $4,000), energy efficiency measures, electrification measures, and limited health and safety or incidental repairs (not to exceed 10% of total energy efficiency funding). Electrification add-on costs cannot exceed 10% of total electrification measure costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners and operators of affordable multifamily rental housing developments seeking to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Eligible applicants include government bodies, for-profit companies, non-profit organizations, and individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including building shell improvements, HVAC and water heating systems, lighting, appliances, and fenestration. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs in projects completing measures that reduce electric or gas consumption. Electrification measures to replace fossil fuel systems with electric equipment. Gas reducing measures are allowed only if the customer is in the Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory. Energy audit costs may be requested on the first construction draw.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Gas reducing measures limited to BGE or WGL utility territories. Priority for affordable properties and low-income housing, including Priority Funding Areas.

Energy audit must identify eligible energy conservation and decarbonization measures (ECMs)
Qualified Energy Professional must submit the Funding Request (using DHCD's Rehab Funding Request Form or MINT when available) on behalf of the project owner with owner approval

For GHGRP projects, building must have gross floor area of 35,000 sq ft or more (single building) or two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000+ sq ft served by the same meter or heating/cooling system
For GHGRP projects, minimum of 51% of units must be at or below 80% AMI for a minimum of 15 years
Energy savings calculations must be submitted with actual contractor bids including materials, equipment, and installation costs
Energy audit sampling must include at least one representative unit from each unique unit type and a minimum of 10% of all units (minimum 5 units)
All insulation materials must not contain formaldehyde intentionally added or present above 0.1% by weight
Air sealing, insulation, duct sealing, and HVAC replacement are mandatory when existing conditions warrant
Mandatory measures are evaluated on a case-by-case basis with waivers available
Duct systems must be evaluated and accessible ducts sealed; Aeroseal may be used for full system sealing
HVAC equipment capacity cannot increase without written DHCD approval and detailed Manual J calculation
Ventilation requirements must meet ASHRAE 62.2 standards post-retrofit with calculations provided
At least one authentic photo uniquely identifying each recommended ECM and its location must be provided; additional photo showing model/serial number required where applicable
Regulatory agreement or tax covenant must be created by DHCD if one does not exist (minimum 20% of units at 80% AMI for 5 years minimum)

Required documents for commitment include application, utility bills, customer consent form, grantee signature block, deed with legal description, SDAT property ownership check, SDAT status checks, minority business enterprise plan, ACH direct deposit form, proof of affordability, and W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Owner or qualified representative completes the MEEHA Application Form with property and project information and submits to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov along with required documents including commercial utility bills, customer consent forms, proof of property ownership, and tax documentation. 2. Owner selects a Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's approved list to conduct comprehensive energy audit (for rehabilitation projects) or energy certification review (for new construction). 3. Qualified Energy Professional performs energy audit in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards, sampling at least 10% of units (minimum 5, maximum typically 20) representing each unique unit type, and evaluating all feasible energy saving opportunities. 4. Qualified Energy Professional performs ASHRAE 62.2 ventilation calculations and provides detailed photos of existing conditions with model/serial numbers where applicable. 5. Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD using the Rehab Funding Request Form (or MINT system when available) including recommended energy conservation and decarbonization measures (ECMs) with actual contractor bids, measure specifications, energy savings calculations, and required documentation. 6. DHCD reviews Funding Request and required documents for completeness and compliance with program guidelines. 7. DHCD may request additional information or clarification from the project or energy professional. 8. Upon approval, DHCD creates a funding agreement (grant or loan agreement) specifying terms to be executed by the project owner. 9. Project installs the funded energy efficiency measures according to the approved specifications. 10. DHCD inspects equipment after installation to verify compliance. 11. DHCD releases funding after inspection and verification of installed measures. 12. Project enters the affordability compliance period (5 or 15 years depending on funding tier) with ongoing DHCD monitoring.

structured_extraction.program_name: Multifamily Energy Efficiency and Housing Affordability (MEEHA) Program - Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP)
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that reduces direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment in affordable multifamily rental housing developments. Funding also supports building energy conservation and alternative energy generating systems.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: GHGRP provides grants only (loans available under separate MEEHA EmPower program). Funding is allocated at $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, $5 million each for fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Projects receive up to $15,000 per dwelling unit with a project cap of $1.25 million. Funds support measures that reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions including: replacing fossil fuel-fired equipment with electric equipment; incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure; energy efficiency and conservation improvements (excluding fossil fuel-fired equipment); and alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics. Projects must maintain a minimum of 51% of households at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years. Eligible projects must be existing buildings with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more (excluding parking garages), or two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more served by the same electric or gas meter or heating/cooling system.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more, or multiple buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more, housing at least 51% of tenants at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Replace fossil fuel-fired equipment with electric equipment. Incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure. Energy efficiency and conservation improvements. Alternative energy generating systems such as solar photovoltaics. Health and Safety measures necessary to prevent indoor air quality issues or mold. Incidental repairs required to allow installation of program-funded measures. Electrification add-on expenses needed to support electrification measures.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be an affordable multifamily rental housing development

Project must be an existing building with 35,000 gross square feet of floor area or more (excluding parking garages), OR two or more buildings with combined gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more that are served in whole or in part by the same electric or gas meter or are served by the same heating or cooling system(s) which is not a district energy system
A minimum of 51% of households must be at 80% Area Median Income (AMI) or less for a minimum of 15 years

Projects must have at least 15 years of affordability restrictions in place. If no initial regulatory agreement exists or current affordability restrictions have fewer than 15 years remaining, the property must accept regulatory restrictions for a period not less than 15 years
For rehabilitation projects, a Qualified Energy Professional must complete an energy audit in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards
Energy audit must identify eligible greenhouse gas reduction measures and provide benchmarking report through Energy Star Portfolio Manager
Qualified Energy Professional must submit the Funding Request on behalf of the project owner using DHCD's Rehab Funding Request Form or MINT (Hancock Mobile Intake Tool) when operational
Projects must set up an Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and follow MDE and/or EPA guidelines for creating benchmarking reports
Projects must provide annual energy use benchmarking reports to DHCD for a minimum of two years after construction completion
If renewable energy systems are installed, estimated greenhouse gas emissions reductions data must be calculated using DHCD-provided conversion factors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Set up an Energy Star Portfolio Manager account and follow MDE and/or EPA guidelines for creating a benchmarking report. 2. Submit completed MEEHA Application and required documents to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov, including Portfolio Manager baseline report, third-party verification report (sample), and other required application documents listed on the MEEHA website. (Note: Projects seeking funds through CDA Rental Lending using the 202 form do not need to submit the Application form or other required application documents). 3. Have a DHCD Qualified Energy Professional from the approved list complete an energy audit for rehabilitation projects or energy certification review for new construction projects in accordance with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards. 4. Qualified Energy Professional submits Funding Request to DHCD on behalf of the project owner, including the Energy Audit Report, recommended scope of work, and estimated costs with greenhouse gas emissions reduction data. 5. DHCD reviews and finalizes the Funding Request. 6. DHCD creates a funding agreement to be executed. 7. DHCD Project Manager conducts monthly meetings and visual inspections to track construction progress. 8. Project installs the funded greenhouse gas reduction measures. 9. DHCD releases funding on a reimbursement basis through a requisition process as work is completed and verified. 10. Project provides annual energy use benchmarking reports to DHCD for a minimum of two years after construction completion. 11. Project enters the affordability period after construction is completed.

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: The National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (NED) provides competitive funds to support commercial and residential revitalization activities in the National Capital region. The program focuses on neighborhoods where modest, planned investment and coordinated strategy will have significant impact, funding strategic economic development and revitalization projects through capital investments in areas targeted for revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant and loan funding provided for commercial and residential development projects including down payment assistance for homebuyers, property acquisition and rehabilitation, property improvements, energy efficiency upgrades through weatherization and energy retrofits, affordable housing development, mixed-use projects combining housing retail and office space, community open space or public infrastructure development, and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application period closed July 2, 2025; registration closed June 11, 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and community development organizations seeking to revitalize targeted neighborhoods in the National Capital region.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Down payment assistance for homebuyers, acquiring or rehabilitating vacant or dilapidated properties, improving existing residential and business properties, energy efficiency through weatherization and energy retrofits, developing affordable housing, creating mixed-use projects combining housing retail and office space, developing or enhancing community open space or public infrastructure, and strategic demolition. Funds can support projects listed in a Sustainable Communities Action Plan.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: In Prince George's County, projects must be at least in part within the boundary created by Interstate 495 and the District of Columbia. In Montgomery County, projects must be within an Enterprise Zone or within the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia. All projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in designated Sustainable Communities
Projects must support goals and objectives outlined in the targeted area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects must be in eligible geographic boundaries as defined for Prince George's or Montgomery County
Project must be located in the National Capital region
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit application through Project Portal after registering as a new user. For more information and application procedures, applicants should contact the regional project manager for their area or visit the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: An affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The National Housing Trust Fund provides federal funding to increase and preserve affordable housing supply for extremely low-income and very low-income households under guidelines established by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Extremely low-income and very low-income households
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Affordable housing production and preservation

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects. A business project qualifies if it is located in a priority funding area and is acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business, whether or not for profit. Some qualified business projects are also located in traditionally underserved areas defined as Sustainable Communities. The program, also known as Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW), has a history of over 20 years of financing small businesses in Maryland and has invested approximately $5 million per year in loans to small businesses. The current loan portfolio includes 158 loans with an aggregate outstanding principal balance in excess of $20 million.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration obtains legislative authority to issue bonds to fund loans for business projects. Project types include: (1) commercial real estate, including construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects; (2) commercial real estate, including acquisition or refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; and (3) non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy and/or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations. For-profit borrowers must contribute minimum 10% equity or total cost contribution, with maximum 90% CLTV financing based on senior loan(s) or maximum 100% CLTV with one senior loan of up to 70% LTV and one subordinate loan. Non-profit borrowers must contribute minimum 5% equity or total cost contribution, with maximum 95% CLTV financing based on senior loan(s) or maximum 100% CLTV with one senior loan of up to 70% LTV and one subordinate loan. All loans require minimum 1.50 DSCR throughout the life of the loan and a debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service. CDA earns interest override (minimum target of 0.60% for portfolio administration plus 0.40% for loan servicing and asset management fee) and upfront financing fees of 0.5% to 1%, plus $25,000 legal counsel fee and all normal real estate and loan closing fees.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and non-profit businesses seeking acquisition, construction, permanent financing, refinancing of commercial and mixed-use real estate, and qualified nonprofit organizations seeking facility financing for occupancy and/or use by 501(c)(3) organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition and permanent financing of commercial and mixed-use real estate; refinance of stabilized commercial and mixed-use projects; non-profit facility loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and new construction of facilities for occupancy and/or use by qualified 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations; construction and permanent financing for commercial and mixed-use projects
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas as defined in section 5-7B-02 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, or in Sustainable Communities as defined in section 6-205 of DHCD's Article, per Title 5, Subtitle 13 of the Economic Development Article, or per section 7-101 of the Transportation Article.
requirements_list: Project must be located in a Priority Funding Area or Sustainable Community
Project must be acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business
For-profit borrowers: minimum 10% equity or total cost contribution
Non-profit borrowers: minimum 5% equity or total cost contribution
Maximum 90% CLTV financing for for-profit borrowers (or 100% with two-loan structure)
Maximum 95% CLTV financing for non-profit borrowers (or 100% with two-loan structure)
Minimum pro-forma 1.50 DSCR throughout the life of the loan
Loan debt service reserve equal to 6 months of maximum annual debt service
Credit worthiness of borrower analysis required
Market position of assisted business assessment required
Adequacy of collateral evaluation required
Soundness of business plan and management team assessment required
Qualified professional and independent collateral valuation acceptable to CDA and MHF required
All CDA-funded business loans underwritten in anticipation of being offered as non-recourse-to-CDA collateral to private investors
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Program has an on-line application process to facilitate loan intake and underwriting. All NBW projects are evaluated based on their revitalization impact on the community including elimination of blight, catalytic redevelopment stimulus, and job retention/creation. NBW loans are originated using industry-standard underwriting criteria. All CDA business loans over $250,000 are reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the 5-member NBW Loan Review Committee. All NBLP CDA business loan underwriting is reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the 7-member Housing Finance Review Committee. All of CDA's debt issuance supported by business loans is reviewed and recommended for approval to the Secretary of DHCD by the 7-member Revenue Bond Advisory Board.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides financing options for small businesses and nonprofit organizations during all phases of business growth. The program helps finance new and expanding businesses whose efforts improve and revitalize existing commercial districts and town centers, including businesses located in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities across the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct, insured, or guaranteed loans to small businesses and nonprofit organizations. Financing is available through direct business loans and lending partners including banks and community development financial institutions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding small businesses and nonprofit organizations in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business growth and expansion, revitalization of commercial districts and town centers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available to businesses in Priority Funding Areas and Sustainable Communities throughout Maryland statewide.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can complete a pre-application consultation and then submit a financing application online. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to local jurisdictions and their internet service provider partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The program covers a significant portion of capital construction costs with a required local match. Funded through American Rescue Plan Act (ARP) federal funds, the program aims to address broadband deficits in Maryland communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $50,000 to $500,000 per application covering 70% to 90% of eligible capital construction costs for extending broadband service to unserved areas. Required cash or in-kind match of 10% to 30% of capital construction costs determined by project density (households per mile for wired projects or households per tower for wireless projects). Wired Infrastructure: Fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match; 8-14 households per mile requires 20% match; 15+ households per mile requires 30% match. Wireless Infrastructure: Fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match; 40-69 households per tower requires 20% match; 70+ households per tower requires 30% match. Match from applicant or non-ISP sources must be in cash; ISP Partner match may be cash or in-kind capital construction costs. All equipment must be new and non-depreciated.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 23, 2021
structured_extraction.program_audience: County or Municipal local jurisdictions in partnership with Internet Service Providers (ISPs) seeking to expand broadband service to unserved residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for extending broadband service to unserved areas, including: construction of facilities to deploy service at minimum broadband speeds to all end users; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service to end users; electronics necessary to deliver service such as Optical Line Terminals (OLTs), Optical Network Terminals (ONTs), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Tower construction costs owned by applicant may be included as match. Engineering design services for tower structural studies may be included as match using direct labor costs only.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland; areas must be unserved (lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds). Areas having received state grant funding in the past are ineligible for additional funding. All projects must conform to ARP federal requirements.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a County or Municipality listed on the Maryland Manual On-Line website
Must have a partnership agreement with an ISP Partner prior to funding
Project area must be unserved: lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds

Minimum network capability of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency to all end users (exceptions allowed for geographic, topographic, or cost limitations with ISP certification; in such cases, minimum 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload required with scalability to symmetric 100 Mbps)
Required local match between 10-30% depending on project density
Grant funding between $50,000 and $500,000 per application
Minimum $13 million available for program in FY22
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Costs incurred prior to application submission are not eligible
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Applicant and/or ISP Partner will own constructed facilities
Program closed and not accepting new applications
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Program is closed and not accepting applications. Historically, applicants were required to submit one electronic PDF copy of response to osb.md@maryland.gov by application deadline with subject line including 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and project name. Application package required: completed Grant Application Form (fillable PDF available); Executive Summary describing unserved area, community problems, and project benefits; Application Partnership naming ISP Partner; Statement of Experience for senior team from both applicant and ISP Partner; Network Design and Construction description including speed, latency, backhaul methods, pole attachment vs. underground, tower specifications, construction personnel; Subscriber Profile with demographic data and projected take rate; Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing ISP service options and costs; Line item Capital Budget on provided form; Project implementation schedule with key milestones. Supporting files required: GIS shapefiles (.shp, .kmz, .kml) showing properties to receive service; separate GIS file showing proposed infrastructure; all documents combined in single ZIP file with clearly identified file names. Applications evaluated on scoring criteria including Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points), with maximum score of 25 points.

structured_extraction.program_description: The state provides matching grants to support operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations that stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. These organizations partner with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the State to provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling services, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible Neighborhood Housing Services corporation may apply for a grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Umbrella corporations may apply for grants for each program under their supervision, also up to $50,000 per program without exceeding one-third of the annual operating budget for that program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Neighborhood Housing Services (NHS) corporations approved and certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation that serve low- and moderate-income households in targeted neighborhoods.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations, which support homeownership programs, home rehabilitation, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling services, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Neighborhoods served by certified NHS corporations in Maryland, including multiple neighborhoods in Baltimore City and Baltimore County served by NHS of Baltimore and St. Ambrose Housing Aid Center, and the West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods of Salisbury served by Salisbury NHS.
requirements_list: Must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local NHS corporation
Local political subdivision must participate on the NHS corporation's board of directors
State grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions
Grant amount cannot exceed $50,000
Grant amount cannot exceed one-third of the NHS corporation's annual operating budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible NHS corporations apply for grants. Contact the Poverty Solutions Team at the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for application instructions and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: The NourishMD Grant Program is a strategic and targeted investment designed to expand access to fresh foods in food-insecure communities across Maryland. It supports the development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets that provide fresh food in areas where residents have limited or no access to nutritious food options, providing grants to eligible food retailers for capital improvements, equipment, and operations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants range from $25,000 to $150,000 with up to $2 million in total funding available. A $250 processing fee is deducted from the awarded grant amount. Funds support equipment purchases (such as refrigeration and shelving), facility renovations and build-outs, facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion (non-prepared foods), working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT acceptance. Applicants may also request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks program, which will undergo financial review to assess the applicant's capacity to manage debt.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit food retailers including grocery stores, corner stores, farm stands, farmers' markets, food co-ops, delivery retailers, and small retail stores where the majority of inventory or sales are food-related (no more than 25% of gross sales from alcohol/tobacco) serving communities with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of furniture, fixtures, and equipment (e.g., refrigeration, shelving); renovation and build-out; facility upgrades; capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods); working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction; and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher, defined as any area with a score of 60% or higher pursuant to Annotated Code of Maryland - Housing and Community Development Article §6-308. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis. Note: Your business does not need to be listed on the Maryland Community Business Compass to be eligible. If you don't see your business on the Maryland Community Business Compass and would like to add it, please email compass@maryland.gov.
requirements_list: Serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Operate at least 5 days per week year-round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year-round)
Employ a maximum of 500 workers
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)

Currently or plan to offer a variety of high-quality fresh produce, or a mix of fresh, frozen, and preserved produce, as well as other healthy grocery items (e.g., whole grains, dairy products, fresh meats/proteins)
Dedicate at least 20% of retail inventory or floor space dedicated to food sales to healthy food items (may be based on square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory for sale)
Must meet SNAP eligibility or plan to adopt SNAP functionality
A $250 processing fee is sourced from the award amount
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications opened January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closed February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST through an online application portal. All required documentation must be submitted at the time of application. Complete applications are reviewed on a competitive basis for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities. DHCD staff evaluates eligible applications during February-March 2026, referring the final list of eligible applications to the NourishMD Grant Review Committee for determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April 2026. Award notifications are made in May 2026, with award agreements beginning processing. The Board of Public Works approves grants and disbursements are made in June 2026. Required documentation includes: (1) a detailed written plan describing how grant funds will be used (not to exceed 2 pages); (2) information demonstrating how the business currently meets or will meet the healthy and fresh food criteria to dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items; (3) one year of business tax returns or audited financial statements (or alternative documentation for businesses operating less than one year); and (4) supporting documentation for relocation or expansion projects, such as a lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: The Technical Assistance Grant (TAG) program assists nonprofit organizations and local governments with operating costs associated with community and economic revitalization efforts throughout Maryland. The program provides support for organizations engaged in community development activities, offering grants of up to $50,000 with no required matching funds. Funds help cover operating expenses such as salaries, professional services contracts, and technology costs for local housing and community revitalization projects.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for operating costs related to administering community and economic revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Maximum grant request is $50,000. No funding match is required. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, and other costs directly related to administering the Technical Assistance Grant program. Funds cannot be used for capital project costs, alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal items, fines, or travel companion costs. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required; subsequent payment requests must include evidence of expenditures such as paid invoices, contracts, or other documentation. Minimum request for reimbursement is $1,000. Funds must be drawn down at a rate of at least 50% within six months of award execution date, with all funds drawn down by the award agreement expiration date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland involved in community and economic revitalization activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community and economic revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services and general operating expenses that support community revitalization initiatives. Capital project costs are not supported. Funds cannot be used for alcohol, controlled substances, entertainment, personal items, fines, or travel companion costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Additional consideration given to projects in designated ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas and Just Communities. The Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool can be used to verify PFA eligibility.
requirements_list: Must be a nonprofit organization or local government entity in Maryland
Must be engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Projects or initiatives should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans and/or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
Maximum grant request is $50,000
No matching funds required
Current awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements and reporting requirements before applying

Nonprofit applicants must submit evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from MD State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from MD Secretary of State
Awardees must maintain all project-related records for a minimum of three years after official close-out of the award
At least 50% of awarded funds must be drawn down within six months of award execution date
Funds cannot be used for capital project costs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1) Register on the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/IGXLogin by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form (approval may take up to 72 hours). 2) New organizations should request access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. First-time applicants must contact the project manager for eligibility verification and system access. 3) Complete the online application through the Project Portal, ensuring all required organizational documents are included in your profile before submission. Applications missing required documents may be disqualified. 4) Submit the completed application through the Project Portal by the deadline. Late applications will not be accepted. 5) Applications are evaluated using a single 5-point scoring scale assessing alignment with funding priorities and organizational capacity. Projects in ENOUGH areas may receive up to 10 bonus points; projects in Just Communities will receive 10 bonus points. 6) Review teams may conduct site visits and/or follow-up discussions with applicants prior to award decisions. 7) Upon approval by the DHCD Secretary and General Assembly during the legislative session, successful applicants are notified through the Project Portal with official award letters. 8) Awardees execute the Award Agreement (a legally binding contract) through DocuSign, with authorized signatories required to sign within five business days of receipt. 9) Following execution, the award moves to 'active' status and all award management activities (progress reports, payment requests, final reports) are conducted through the Project Portal. 10) Progress reports are due either 6 months from grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted. 11) Final reports are due within 30 days of the award agreement expiration date and must include certification of completion, visual documentation (before/after photos preferred), financial reconciliation, compliance verification, and detailed results documentation. Training documents and application guides are available in the Project Portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that allows businesses to source additional capital and receive federal tax incentives by locating or expanding in designated Opportunity Zones.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program enables businesses starting or expanding in Opportunity Zones to source additional capital and receive federal tax incentives.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses starting or expanding in designated Opportunity Zones
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business startup or expansion in Opportunity Zones
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Opportunity Zones in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: Own Your Future provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy property they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program is funded by the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) and supports property acquisition and renovation for eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers loans with flexible terms of up to 30 years for purchasing, constructing, or renovating commercial real estate. Loan amounts range from a minimum of $500,000 to a maximum of $5 million. Loans can be offered in senior or subordinate positions with interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. Borrowers must provide a minimum of 1:1 private capital match (one dollar of private funding for every dollar of DHCD loan), provide personal guarantees from owners with greater than 20% equity interest, provide adequate collateral, and maintain total project costs not exceeding $20 million. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion and new construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees seeking to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used to purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate, including buying the space where you currently operate, moving to a new location, buying property for the first time if you do not have a storefront such as an e-commerce business or food truck, or buying property as part of an expansion.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Minimum 1:1 private capital match required
Loan amount must be at least $500,000 and no more than $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with greater than 20% equity interest
Adequate collateral must be provided
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion
New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion
Business cannot be an adult entertainment facility, check cashing facility, gambling facility, gun shop, liquor store, massage parlor, pawn shop, tanning salon, tattoo parlor, or cannabis business
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Applicants can schedule a consultation before applying by visiting dhcd.maryland.gov/Business/Pages/Own-Your-Future.aspx or emailing dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program expands the supply of affordable rental housing for low-income households by providing loans for development and preservation of rental housing. It typically involves partnerships between State and local governments. The program also allows non-governmental entities to create housing for people with disabilities or special needs integrated within traditional rental housing developments. Rental units must be occupied by households earning below 50% of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides direct loans for the development of rental housing. Loan amounts are limited to $75,000 per unit for large projects and up to $2 million without a per unit cap for small projects (defined as 40 units or fewer). Repayment is generally deferred for up to 40 years as long as the local government entity continues to own the housing and rents it to income-eligible households. Failure to comply with income and use restrictions may result in loan acceleration. Any profits from the sale of the project must be used by the borrower for other low-income housing purposes.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, housing authorities, entities owned in part by a local government or housing authority, non-governmental entities creating housing for individuals with disabilities or special needs, for-profit and non-profit rental housing developers, county governments, and municipalities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings and shared housing facilities. Funds are for developing and preserving affordable rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. Statewide.
requirements_list: Rental units must be occupied by households with incomes below 50% of the statewide median
Local governments must make a contribution of the land or a contribution of equal value from non-state resources
The local participant must manage the project or arrange for another party to manage the project
Resident households must have gross income not exceeding 50 percent of statewide median income adjusted for family size
Residents must contribute maintenance or other services to the facility, grounds or neighborhood
Occupants of Partnership Rental Housing Program-assisted units must provide tenant contributed services as detailed in the program statute and regulations
For individuals with disabilities or special needs units, resident households must have gross income not exceeding 30 percent of Area Median Income adjusted for household size
Projects must be evaluated based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests for funding are accepted on an ongoing basis. Applications are evaluated and processed based on meeting the program purpose, readiness to proceed, and availability of funding. If Partnership Rental Housing Program funding is requested with other department funds, the application requirements and applicable deadlines of the other funding must be met. Applicants can find application documents in the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that activates vacant buildings, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing financial support to place-based economic development organizations working to improve the vitality of Maryland's commercial corridors. Specifically, the program provides grants of up to $300,000 to designated Main Streets, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other place-based economic development organizations in Sustainable Communities. These organizations identify priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts and then sub-grant the funding to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, and equipment to activate vacant spaces. Businesses receiving sub-granted funds must open and be operational by December 2025.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to $300,000 per applicant organization are provided. The FY2024 round made $13,193,363 in total awards available. Funds are sub-granted to businesses for rental assistance (capped at reasonable local market rental rates), renovation, interior/exterior renovation, and furniture, fixtures, and equipment (FFE) costs to activate vacant storefronts and buildings in business districts. Funds cannot be used for acquisition, new construction, vehicles, or operating costs for sub-grantees. Up to 15% of the grant request can be used for organizational operating costs such as staff, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0. Grants are not reimbursement-based; funding is provided after the award agreement is executed. Payments are strongly encouraged via ACH (direct deposit) rather than paper check. All funds must be expended and businesses must be operational by December 31, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Closed - FY2024 round application deadline was Wednesday, April 24, 2024 at 5:00 PM EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations such as designated Main Street organizations, Arts and Entertainment Districts, and other place-based economic development organizations located in Sustainable Communities. Local governments (towns, cities, counties) are also eligible to apply. Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but can receive sub-granted funds through awarded place-based organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supporting place-based economic development organizations to activate vacant buildings, support economic activity, improve commercial corridors, and create jobs. Sub-grants to businesses for rental assistance, renovation, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment. Operating funds for awarded organizations may support staff costs, professional services, marketing, and promotion directly related to administering Project Restore 2.0.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide; all counties eligible. Organizations and all vacant properties must be located in designated Sustainable Communities. All awarded organizations in FY2024 represent counties including Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Calvert, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, Somerset, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization (e.g., designated Main Street, Arts and Entertainment District) or local government entity (town, city, county)
Must be located in a designated Sustainable Community
Organization must have IRS-determined non-profit status at time of application (501(c)(3) status not specifically required)
Organization must have been in existence for a demonstrable period (no specific minimum time requirement, but ability to complete similar projects within grant timeline will be evaluated)
Must have at least 0.5 FTE staff at time of application if requesting operating funds
Must identify priority vacant storefronts or buildings in local business districts that are vacant at time of application
Each eligible entity can only submit one application
Vacant properties must be vacant at time of application (no minimum vacancy period required; means no executed lease with tenant at application)
Applicant must provide list of specific vacant property addresses (1-3 properties recommended)
Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly
Properties must be in commercial corridors with commercial character, including downtown and historic commercial corridors; focus on street-level retail
Properties cannot include indoor shopping malls, industrial parks, office parks, or new construction lots
Property owner letter must confirm building was vacant at time of application
If awarded, executed sub-grant agreements required with sub-grantees
If awarded, open and inclusive process for determining sub-grantees must be demonstrated
Past Project Restore awardees from FY22 and FY23 cannot be awarded funds for same property location as previously awarded
All grant funds must be expended by December 31, 2025
All tenant businesses must be open and operational by December 31, 2025
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Place-based economic development organizations submit applications through Maryland OneStop portal identifying priority vacant storefronts or buildings in their local business districts. Applications must provide specific property addresses and demonstrate organizational readiness, equitable processes for determining sub-grantees, project alignment with strategy, and advancement of program goals. Applications are reviewed for threshold eligibility, then scored by DHCD staff on a 100-point scale. All applications are reviewed after the deadline; no rolling reviews. Selected organizations receive funding and execute grant agreements. Organizations then develop their own policies and practices for sub-granting to eligible businesses, with requirements for open and inclusive processes. Regional training sessions were offered across the state. After award, grantees submit a Request for Payment (RFP) for each property before costs are incurred. An executed lease and sub-grant agreement are required with the RFP. Following project completion and business opening, grantees submit a Completion Report per property (including Use & Occupancy permit, photos, receipts, MHT determination). A single Final Report is submitted per organization within 30 days of end of grant term or after all Completion Reports are approved. FY2024 application closed April 24, 2024. Future rounds uncertain; interested parties can sign up for DHCD news and alerts.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Rental Housing Program provides financing to rehabilitate or create affordable multifamily rental housing. The program allocates funds through a competitive process and may be combined with federal HOME funds, tax-exempt or taxable bond financing, low-income housing tax credits, and other public or private funds. It supports both the development and preservation of affordable rental housing for low-income residents.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with a term of up to 40 years, bearing interest at 2 percent per annum and repayable from cash flow. The maximum loan amount should not exceed $2 million. Loans may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, legal fees, and other development-related costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted at designated times during the year; contact for additional detail
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs, Community Development Administration (also: Alvin Lawson)
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit, limited profit, or nonprofit developers, nonprofit organizations, county governments, municipalities, or local housing authorities developing or preserving rental housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Newly constructed or rehabilitated rental housing including congregate housing, single-room occupancy, emergency shelters and shared living facilities. Projects may be restricted to elderly residents. In some cases, small commercial rehabilitation housing projects may be considered. Funds may be used for acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, and development costs, including lender fees, architectural and engineering fees, market studies, appraisals, and legal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All new construction projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (new construction).
Eligible residents must have incomes of no more than 60 percent of the area median income.
Owner must reserve the same proportion of units for these tenants as the Rental Housing Program Funds are to the total financing.
Priority given to projects that restrict units to tenants with incomes below 60 percent of median income.
Priority given to projects that restrict units to low-income tenants for more than 40 years.
Priority given to projects that provide tenant service packages.
Priority given to projects that use non-State funds in addition to State funds.
Priority given to projects that provide quality housing in a good location.
Priority given to projects sponsored by teams with demonstrated development and management ability.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program awards funding through competitions held one or two times a year. Applications are accepted at designated times during the year and are evaluated against criteria established by the Department. Applicants can download application documents from the agency's Multifamily Document Library.

structured_extraction.program_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate gap financing to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by supporting the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The financing is used in conjunction with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental Housing Works provides subordinate loans as gap financing with a maximum of $2.5 million per project (though this limit may be waived in certain circumstances; in no event shall RHW funding be provided in excess of an amount necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department). Loans are offered with a 40-year term at 2% simple interest for the permanent loan period, with no regular interest during the construction period. Principal payments are based on surplus cash, calculated annually and limited to a percentage of annual cash flow. Upon occurrence of a capital event (sale, transfer, refinancing, or transfer of property interest), contingent interest payments may be required. Loans are secured by a Deed of Trust and are non-recourse except as otherwise provided in loan documents.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers, for-profit businesses, non-profit organizations, county governments, and municipalities creating or preserving affordable rental housing projects that also qualify for the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. Funds must be used in conjunction with Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Required zoning for use and density must be in place at time of application with proper documentation (letter from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution)
Award of any necessary competitive public and private sources of funding must have been made at time of application
Project's projected Full Time Equivalent (FTE) jobs must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all funding awards
Projects must meet threshold and scoring criteria outlined in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
Development or site plan approval is not required at application, but conditional use or special exception approval must be obtained before closing
RHW loan amount may not exceed $2.5 million per project unless waived, and in no case shall exceed amount necessary for financial feasibility and viability per Section 42 of Internal Revenue Code
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed RHW Application Submission Package (CDA Form 202) in conjunction with a Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits application using the Department's standard Application Submission Package. Required documentation includes: completed CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds; written zoning documentation; certification that competitive funding awards have been made; completed FTE Job Calculator; and certification to the RHW Application Submission Package including Access to Public Records Act waiver. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed alongside Multifamily Bond Program applications. Projects passing threshold are scored using evaluation criteria in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide. Kick-off meetings are scheduled after scoring is complete. Projects must proceed according to agreed-upon timelines and are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners to cover costs associated with preparing federal funding applications for broadband projects. The Office of Statewide Broadband assists applicants in developing competitive applications for federal funding opportunities by reimbursing for properly contracted services such as engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved services needed to prepare federal funding applications.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants covering up to a maximum of $125,000 to reimburse for properly contracted services required for federal funding applications, including: engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other costs considered on a case-by-case basis. Reimbursement is only available for projects that submit a completed application for a federal funding program and meet the terms and conditions of that federal program. The OSB will offer partnerships on a rolling basis depending on the federal funding opportunity and available state funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis; no fixed deadline. Partnerships offered depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding.
