structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions or their internet service provider partners seeking to develop broadband expansion projects for unserved rural residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Costs associated with preparing federal funding applications, including engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved consulting services. Funds can also be used for coordination with other State Agencies on the use of State assets where they will feasibly benefit the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; project areas must comply with federal program requirements and serve unserved areas where broadband is not available at minimum 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up, unless the federal funding program defines unserved areas differently.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local jurisdiction or internet service provider partner of a local jurisdiction
Projects must be designed to serve unserved areas as defined by federal program or by OSB standards (25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up minimum)
Projects must be able to provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds, unless federal funding program is more restrictive
Applicant must submit a completed application for a federal funding program
Project must meet the terms and conditions of the applicable federal funding program
Technology must be capable of meeting speed and latency requirements; OSB is technology neutral
Applicant must complete the application form signed by both the local jurisdiction and ISP partner
Applicant must provide business model summary, experience statement, network design description, customer profile, and implementation schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Prepare a response to the Request for Proposals (RFP) including: cover letter with authorized representative contact information, completed and signed application form, business model summary, experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule. 2. Submit one electronic copy of the response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in the subject line. 3. Identify any proprietary or confidential information in the response. 4. Submit written questions related to the RFP to OSB.MD@maryland.gov. 5. OSB will evaluate responses based on qualifications, submittals, and may conduct interviews. 6. OSB will select the proposal that best meets requirements and public interest. Contact the Office of Statewide Broadband to discuss the project and determine if an application can be funded.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program exclusively designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to access capital for relending to small businesses, with a focus on businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses (VSB), and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas. Part of the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) administered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) platform. Targeted loans to small businesses up to $250,000 (individual SBL borrowers; DHCD may approve up to $500,000 with prior written approval).
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) for relenting to small businesses. SSBCI loans to lenders bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options. Lenders must match SSBCI funds with private capital: 20% SSBCI/80% private match for non-SEDI and non-VSB businesses, and 30% SSBCI/70% private match for SEDI and VSB businesses. Individual SBL borrowers receive loans up to $250,000 (DHCD may approve up to $500,000 with prior written approval) at interest rates not exceeding 18%, with terms up to 5 years unless financing longer-lived assets. SBL origination fees and points combined cannot exceed 1%, application fees capped at $100. No prepayment penalties allowed. Lenders maintain 20% capital at risk with minimum 1:1 private capital match.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) seeking capital to relend to small businesses, particularly those owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI), very small businesses (VSB), and businesses in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relending to small businesses for working capital, marketing, feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business. Ineligible uses include residential or transient living businesses, multifamily or single-family housing, nursing homes, assisted living, adult entertainment facilities, gambling facilities, gun shops, liquor stores, massage parlors, pawn shops, tanning salons, and tattoo parlors.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. CDFIs must serve Maryland counties/cities and give priority to CDFI Investment Areas.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) certified and in good standing with the State and Internal Revenue Service

Demonstrated experience in administering small business loan programs including origination, credit and compliance underwriting, loan servicing, post-closing asset management, and compliance reporting
Ability to leverage eligible required private capital as match to SSBCI funding (minimum 1:1 match; initial target 70% private/30% SSBCI for SEDI and VSB; 80% private/20% SSBCI for other businesses)
Capacity to comply with SSBCI statutes, regulations, and policies as well as DHCD requirements
Financial stability with minimum 20% lender capital at risk
Readiness to originate and fund SBLs within 90 days of SSBCI Loan closing
Ability to provide technical assistance to SBL borrowers
Outreach capabilities to very small businesses (VSBs) and socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led businesses (SEDIs)
SBL borrowers must be small businesses (fewer than 500 employees) or nonprofit organizations as defined by U.S. Small Business Administration
Individual SBLs cannot exceed $250,000 unless DHCD grants prior written approval
SBL interest rates cannot exceed 18%
SBL terms cannot exceed 5 years unless financing assets with longer useful lives
Combined origination fees and points not to exceed 1% of SBL amount
Application fee maximum $100 per SBL borrower
Must submit monthly, quarterly, and annual reports including SSBCI loan balance, private match fund balance, SBLs made, and leveraged follow-on capital
Must maintain audited financial statements and allow DHCD and federal auditors post-closing file access
Must provide technical assistance to each SBL borrower
Cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap, familial status, or national origin
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs submit a completed SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application form (Appendix A) to DHCD at 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706 or dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov. Application must include: organization information and CDFI certification documentation; explanation of capacity and experience originating and servicing small business loans with 6-year projected loan production; description of leverage strategy and private capital terms (targeting 10:1 leverage with 70-30 or 80-20 split); verification of financial stability and resources to begin relending within 90 days of loan closing; detailed lending program description including demographic, geographic, and industry targets; outreach capabilities to VSBs and SEDIs; loan product details (size, interest rates, terms, uses, fees); reporting and audit capabilities; technical assistance approach; and attestation of no outstanding state liabilities. Applicants must attach most recent Annual Report, Annual Financial Statement, 501(c)(3) organizational documents, and last 3 years of tax returns. Upon approval, Lender receives commitment letter from DHCD specifying SSBCI loan amount, required private capital match, and funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must close according to terms and documentation provided by Maryland Office of the Attorney General. Lender then originates and underwriters SBLs according to SSBCI guidelines and DHCD requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program dedicated to funding and growing the next generation of early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. The program provides bridge financing to help companies that have already raised equity from early-stage investors reach their next equity raise and scale their operations. Typical bridge rounds are over $2,000,000.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Venture debt or convertible notes ranging from $500,000 to $2,500,000 per company with aggregate funding rounds under $20,000,000. SSBCI must be on at least a pari passu basis (equal footing) with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Repayment in principal and interest or convertible note terms available. Equity investments also available to support early-stage businesses seeking bridge financing to achieve milestones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking additional investors. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals who own and operate businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to help early-stage businesses achieve milestones and reach their next equity raise.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses operating in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fewer than 500 employees
Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing Paid-In-Capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
Companies typically positioned to scale and bridge financing needed to achieve milestones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested businesses should email dhcd.ssbci@maryland.gov to inquire and apply.

structured_extraction.program_name: SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) Loan Participation Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that helps small businesses acquire or expand their owner-occupied real estate or working capital needs. The program offers below-market interest rates and can lend up to $5 million with flexible terms up to 30 years. It is part of the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) and administered through the Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) platform.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Senior or Junior Debt ranging from $350,000 to $5,000,000. The SSBCI portion covers up to 30% of the total loan. Interest rates are based on underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms available up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Personal guarantees and collateral are required. A prepayment lockout period may apply. Private capital match required: 4:1 target (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB businesses or 2.3:1 target (70-30) for SEDI/VSB, with minimum 1:1 match required.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with fewer than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and socially and economically disadvantaged individuals (SEDI) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses in the same building, machinery and equipment, working capital, and certain other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area in Maryland.
requirements_list: Fewer than 500 employees
Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area
Proof of private capital match: 4:1 target for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 target for SEDI/VSB with minimum 1:1 match required
Business viability and potential impact on the neighborhood
Readiness to proceed
Acceptable cash flow and collateral
Must be Maryland-based
Local governments are not eligible
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package and submit through the online application system at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Upon loan approval, applicants receive a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires that applicants meet underwriting guidelines. Applicants must have executed necessary legal documents prior to disbursement of loan proceeds. Application fee is $250 and closing fee is $250.

structured_extraction.program_description: This federally funded program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing project-based rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. The program is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health, and helps eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services. It is available to for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Section 811 provides project-based rental assistance that subsidizes the contract rent of eligible participants. Funds are awarded to eligible rental projects that receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds. The program does not provide loans. Eligible properties receive assistance to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.program_audience: Rental housing projects and low-income adults with disabilities aged 18 to 61 who receive Medicaid and have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income. Also targets for-profit and non-profit sponsors of affordable rental housing developments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental assistance to subsidize the contract rent of eligible participants with disabilities in approved rental housing units.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in priority funding areas. The program is available statewide. Funding has been distributed to support units in Baltimore, Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Areas, the Eastern Shore, and Western Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicants must be adults aged 18 to 61
Applicants must have a qualifying disability and receive Medicaid
Applicants must have household income at or below 30% of the Area Median Income (AMI)
Applicants must be referred by the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD)
Housing must be a rental property
Housing must receive financing from DHCD
Housing must receive federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits or State Rental Housing Funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: DHCD meets with an Interagency Committee including representatives from the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to review and select projects that align with program goals. Once a project is selected, DHCD issues a Reservation Award Letter to the developer confirming the property is eligible for funding to support unit subsidies. Eligible residents are referred by MDOD and selected according to tenant selection plans.

Projects include adaptive reuse of vacant schools and other buildings for community centers, health care facilities, day care facilities, and other community amenities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grants and loans for capital improvement projects. Anchor institutions must provide matching funds equal to 100 percent of the financial assistance received from the fund (1:1 match requirement).

structured_extraction.program_audience: Anchor institutions defined as institutions of higher education in Maryland or hospital institutions in Maryland with organized medical staff, diagnostic and treatment facilities, and overnight care capacity. Also includes Maryland hospital and higher education institution departments, foundations, and other related entities, as well as nonprofit organizations seeking to catalyze neighborhood revitalization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital improvement projects at anchor institutions in eligible geographic areas. Projects must generate jobs, strengthen community partnerships, and lead to safer, healthier, and more attractive communities. Includes adaptive reuse of vacant schools and other buildings for community centers, health care facilities, day care facilities, and other community amenities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within the boundaries of a Sustainable Community or areas of the state that have not been invested in. Applicants should use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to nonprofits and local governments to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters, including supportive services for residents experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness. The program uses a Harm Reduction approach for supportive services and aims to prevent homelessness and assist households to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Grant funds may cover up to one-half of total project costs generally, or up to 75 percent under certain conditions. Eligible expenditures include real property acquisition, architectural/engineering services, construction, relocation, renovation, replacement, restoration, site development and improvements, utilities, and equipment and furnishings meeting specified criteria (minimum 15-year life expectancy, durability requirements, and not elaborate or extravagant). Recipients must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or the grant becomes repayable. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, feasibility studies, salaries/wages, administrative or legal costs, maintenance, and non-capital furnishings and equipment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments seeking to create or improve transitional housing and emergency shelters for homeless individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Funds may also support architectural/engineering services, site preparation, site development and improvements, utilities installation, and necessary studies and surveys. Funds cannot be used for refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, administrative costs, maintenance, or non-capital furnishings and equipment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Local government letters of support are required for all projects. Projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore and Washington beltways, Sustainable Communities, federal and state enterprise zones, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. All new construction applications must include a letter from local government certifying PFA location.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Project must provide transitional housing or emergency shelter with supportive services
Residents must be homeless households and individuals without permanent housing, lacking resources to obtain permanent housing, and in imminent danger of homelessness
Recipient must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years or grant becomes repayable
Local government letter of support required for all projects
Grant funds may not exceed one-half of total project costs generally, or 75 percent under certain conditions

Applicants must identify the homeless target population to be served (families, women and children, single males, victims of domestic violence, etc.) and continue serving that population throughout the 15-year funding term
Supportive services must be clearly defined with identified service providers and committed funding sources documented through commitment letters or agreements
Applicants must submit a plan outlining funding sources for services and operating expenses during project term
Department will consider applicant's experience operating facilities for homeless and previous success providing services

Equipment and furnishings must have at least 15-year life expectancy with normal maintenance, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, be heavy enough to prevent easy removal (except chairs), not replace adequate existing items, be necessary for intended functions, and not be elaborate or extravagant
Projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation subject to thorough construction management review
Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation encouraged with state goal of 29% certified MBE participation
Maryland resident businesses encouraged for design and construction
Green building technologies and LEED standards encouraged
Maryland Historical Trust consultation required with approval letter needed before fund disbursement for projects affecting historic properties
Roofs purchased with state funds must have minimum 20-year no-dollar-limit warranty; new construction roof systems determined by 60-year life cycle cost analysis
Forest Conservation Program applies to construction on land greater than 40,000 square feet
All prospective contractors must be checked against state debarment list; suspended or debarred individuals/firms cannot receive state funds
Project funds cannot be used for sectarian religious instruction or sectarian religious buildings or programs; Affidavit Not to Use Funds for Religious Purposes may be required

Eligible projects include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family detached homes, single room occupancy facilities, and group or shared housing providing housing for homeless and support services; projects may include other uses if program funds only cover homeless units and necessary operational space
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office at (301) 429-7854 or (800) 543-4505 for application instructions and deadlines. Threshold requirements must be met for acceptance of applications. The Department processes applications through underwriting and construction review phases. Viability review assesses the project's financial feasibility and long-term sustainability. Commitment review ensures all required commitments and documentation are in place. For new construction projects, a letter from local government certifying Priority Funding Area location must be submitted. Maryland Historical Trust review must be completed and approved with issued letter before state fund disbursement. Projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation undergo thorough construction management review.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides loans to preserve and improve single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or minimum housing quality standards. The Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program assists owner-occupants with critical health and safety repairs on their primary residence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Zero percent to six percent interest loans that may be fully deferred for households at or below 50 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income. The maximum loan is generally $50,000. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans are processed directly by local governments. Interest rates are based on the applicant's ability to pay.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes with household incomes at or below 80 percent of the HUD Income Limits or statewide/Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical health and safety repairs on owner-occupied single-family homes, including but not limited to: mold remediation, gas leaks, roof repair and replacement, asbestos abatement, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation waterproofing, radon mitigation, electrical hazards and upgrades, plumbing issues, water and well issues, septic and sewer, windows and doors for health and safety concerns, structural repairs, accessibility modifications for disabled and seniors, fall prevention, pest treatments, and other repairs to bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes and standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Generally not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, or Montgomery County. Available in other Maryland jurisdictions. Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income, or 50 percent for fully deferred loan consideration.
requirements_list: Owner must occupy the single-family home as primary residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (50 percent for fully deferred loans)
Property must be a single-family home, duplex, townhome, condo, or manufactured home
Funding requests should not exceed $50,000
Applicants must provide bids from licensed and insured Maryland Home Improvement contractors or trade professionals documenting critical repairs with photographs
Bids should not be more than 60 days old
Applicants must provide complete income verification documentation including paystubs and/or tax returns
Applicants must provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Applicants must provide homeowners insurance information
Applicants must meet eligibility criteria set by local governments processing the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Applicants identify critical repairs needed on their primary residence. 2. Obtain bids from licensed and insured Maryland contractors including photographs documenting the repairs, contractor contact information, MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9 form. 3. Complete the Maryland Home Rehabilitation Program Application with detailed financial and personal information. 4. Gather required supporting documentation including income verification (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements), proof of home ownership (deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill), homeowners insurance documentation, photo ID, and contractor bids. 5. Submit completed application and all supporting documentation via email to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 6. Application is reviewed by DHCD and local administrators for income eligibility and loan feasibility. 7. Loan is processed directly by local government for the applicant's jurisdiction. Applicants can contact local government housing rehabilitation offices or Special Loan Programs for status.

The fund focuses on projects with high economic and revitalization impact, specifically supporting demolition of vacant and underutilized structures as part of community revitalization efforts statewide. It helps make development on previously used land more financially possible.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state designation program that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It gives local governments resources to improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible. The program combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development under a single designation, focusing on infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that enables local governments to access state resources and funding from multiple state programs including Community Legacy Program (providing capital funding for projects such as mixed-use development and streetscape improvements), Strategic Demolition Fund (providing grants and loans for predevelopment activities, demolition, and land assembly), Neighborhood BusinessWorks (subordinate financing for small businesses and nonprofits), Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance and training for main streets revitalization), Maryland Facade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements), Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund (below-market rate loans for water infrastructure), Job Creation Tax Credit (enhanced from $3,000 to $5,000 per job in Sustainable Communities), Low Income Housing Tax Credit (additional points in application review), Tax Increment Financing (expanded uses for historic preservation, environmental remediation, affordable housing), Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (BRNI) grants, and Operating Assistance Grants. The designation coordinates and prioritizes state investment in designated communities and enables access to federal, state, and foundation funding for revitalization initiatives. Communities receive preference or additional points for programs from MDOT (Transportation Alternatives Program, Safe Routes to School, Kim Lamphier Bikeways Program, Sidewalk Retrofit Program), Maryland Department of Environment (Water Quality financing programs, Stormwater grants), and other state agencies.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted on or before the expiration date of existing Sustainable Communities designation. New designations have rolling application rounds with deadlines approximately every three months.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to revitalize and develop their communities through coordinated state investment and resources. Communities must be within or near town centers or transportation centers and within Priority Funding Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The designation enables access to state and federal funding for historic preservation, housing development and rehabilitation, economic development, infrastructure improvements (water, sewer, stormwater), multimodal transportation (pedestrian and bicycle networks, transit improvements), commercial revitalization (facade improvements, streetscape enhancements, business assistance), environmental improvements (green infrastructure, parks, trails), demolition and land assembly, and other revitalization initiatives within the designated area. Funds can support both public and private projects that strengthen existing communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Entire designated area must be entirely within a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center. Various designated Sustainable Communities exist across all Maryland counties. Applicants can verify PFA boundaries at the Maryland Department of Planning website.
requirements_list: Entire designated area must be entirely within a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Proposed community must be within or near a town center or transportation center, or there is a need for financing assistance for small businesses, nonprofit organizations or microenterprises
Area must demonstrate need for renewal and reinvestment that would benefit from a targeted long-term strategy
For new designations, must obtain a local government resolution supporting both boundary designation and Action Plan before or concurrent with application
Must provide support for nonprofit organizations, strengthen older commercial districts and residential communities, and improve public amenities

Must include a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects addressing Environment, Economy, Transportation, Housing, Community Health & Quality of Life, and Local Planning & Staffing Capacity
Must establish and maintain a Sustainable Communities Workgroup with representatives from local government agencies and community stakeholders
Updated Action Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
The Action Plan must be multi-year investment strategy flexible enough to be updated regularly
For renewal applications, must reconvene Sustainable Communities Workgroup to discuss accomplishments and challenges
For new designations, must have a meeting with Sustainable Communities Program staff before applying
Action Plan must address strategies for revitalization across the six plan elements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For New Designations: 1. Request an application template by contacting program staff or regional project manager. 2. Establish a Sustainable Communities Workgroup with representatives from local government and community stakeholders. 3. Conduct community engagement to gather input on strengths, weaknesses, and revitalization priorities. 4. Develop or update a comprehensive Sustainable Community Action Plan addressing six elements: Environment, Economy, Transportation, Housing, Community Health & Quality of Life, and Local Planning & Staffing Capacity. 5. Obtain a local government resolution supporting the boundary designation and Action Plan. 6. Schedule a meeting with Sustainable Communities Program staff before submitting application. 7. Submit complete application including: defined geographic area map (PDF/JPEG and GIS shapefiles), Sustainable Community Action Plan, local government resolution, workgroup roster, and supporting documentation. 8. Application is evaluated by inter-agency review team based on assessment of strengths and weaknesses and connection of desired outcomes to local conditions. 9. Recommendation is presented to the Governor's Smart Growth Coordinating Committee or Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. For Renewal Applications (every five years): 1. Reconvene the Sustainable Communities Workgroup. 2. Report on accomplishments over past five years. 3. Update the Sustainable Community Action Plan based on current community needs and strengths/weaknesses. 4. Submit renewal application with updated contact information, accomplishments report, and revised Action Plan. 5. Application is reviewed and approved by Governor's Smart Growth Coordinating Committee on recommendation of inter-agency review team.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: UPLIFT is a public-private partnership program designed to increase homeownership opportunities and property values in historically redlined and underserved communities by closing the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to develop or renovate a property and its market sale price. The program provides funding to cover this gap, enabling qualified development teams to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted low-income neighborhoods. Selected qualified development teams use a combination of public and private financing to acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in strategically sized and located assemblages in targeted neighborhoods. The program aims to increase property values, create homeownership opportunities, and build wealth for families.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: UPLIFT provides funding to qualified development teams to cover the appraisal gap—the difference between the total cost to develop a property and the price it can sell for on the market. The State covers this gap through a combination of public and private financing, structured as both grant and loan components. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using a combination of: (1) a down payment; (2) down payment assistance; (3) a first mortgage loan offered by the Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP) or other source; (4) any other acceptable subsidy support; and (5) a 'soft' promissory note with the Department. The developer loan is used to finance the construction phase and the developer requisitions funds as construction progresses and repays upon approved sales. The appraisal gap is reflected in a Promissory Note from the State which the homebuyer includes as part of consideration in acquiring fee simple title. The program charges a one-time non-refundable fee of $1,000 per project. Additional fees may include an origination fee and a closing fee as the project progresses.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis - applications accepted ongoing dependent upon funding availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit and for-profit developers and builders working with local jurisdictions and community-based organizations to develop affordable housing in historically redlined and low-income communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding is used to cover the difference between the cost to construct or renovate quality affordable housing and the price the property can sell for on the market. This enables development teams to build or rehabilitate homes in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities affected by historic redlining and disinvestment. Projects must involve newly constructed or formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in low-income census tracts (where 50 percent of households have incomes below 60 percent of the Area Median Income or have a poverty rate of 25 percent or more) and designated Sustainable Communities. New Construction projects are not to be located in FEMA Flood Zone A or AE. Projects in FEMA Flood Zone C, X, or within floodplains may submit waiver requests with appropriate documentation. Applicants should refer to the UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map for eligible locations.
requirements_list: Project must be composed of properties which are newly constructed or are formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated
Project must be located in both a Low-Income Census Tract and an area designated as a Maryland Sustainable Community
Development team must consist of qualified nonprofit or for-profit developers and builders

Each developer team member (developer, builder/general contractor, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, and marketing/sales entity) must have experience as a significant participant or developer in comparably scaled projects

All corporations, limited liability companies, or limited partnerships that make up the Developer, Project Owner, or that will provide guarantees must submit audited, reviewed, or compiled financial statements as well as interim statements acceptable to DHCD
Any individual providing guarantees or who will be a managing member or general partner in the Developer must submit personal financial statements including certifications acceptable to DHCD
Projects must align with program standards for design, construction, and quality per UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards
Developer entities and guarantors must be determined by the Department to have an acceptable credit history and current financial capacity to successfully undertake the project
Applicants must complete pre-application meeting before formal application submission
Non-refundable $1,000 application fee per project required
Both electronic and hard copy application submissions required
Two complete copies of application form including all attachments and exhibits must be submitted
All information on application must be completed or marked as not applicable; all required exhibits must be included
All documents submitted with applications, including environmental assessments, must be current (usually less than 12 months old)
Appropriate documentation regarding flood risk must be provided if project is in or near FEMA Flood Zones
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Review program guide and schedule a pre-application meeting by submitting the Pre-Application Meeting Request Form at least two business days in advance. Pre-application meetings are required for all applicants and provide preliminary feedback regarding project specifics. Step 1: After the pre-application meeting, submit the Electronic Application Submission Request Form to receive a private Dropbox link and access to the Application Documents Package. Step 2: Download the Application Submission Package (consisting of seven parts: Application Portfolio General Elements, Development Team, Project Economics, Project Location, Design and Construction, Marketing and Sales, and Neighborhood Engagement), complete all sections using the Detailed Application Instructions, and prepare two copies (one electronic, one hard copy). Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable fee by either ACH transfer or check and include documentation of payment with the application. Step 4: Upload all files to the Dropbox in correct subfolders, sign and upload the Final Submission Checklist, and deliver the hard copy to DHCD's Lanham office at 7800 Harkins Rd, Lanham, MD 20706. Hard copy applications should be addressed to Brien O'Toole. Step 5: Applications are evaluated for compliance with UPLIFT's Threshold Criteria and scored against Evaluative Criteria (Capacity of Development Team, Project Impact, Leveraging and Cost Effectiveness, Readiness to Proceed, Development Quality, and State Bonus Points). If materially incomplete or unable to meet Threshold Criteria, DHCD will contact applicant to discuss non-complying issues. If rejected, applicant will be notified in writing with reasons for rejection and may request reconsideration within 7 calendar days. Step 6: Applications passing Threshold Review and scoring adequately enter the UPLIFT underwriting pipeline and are processed for feasibility. A Project Kick-off Meeting is generally held 45 to 60 days after complete application submission to determine underwriting schedule. Step 7: Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) using prescribed packages updates financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 8: DHCD reviews and scores eligible projects; recommendations are made by the UPLIFT Loan Committee to the Secretary of the Department. Step 9: Approved applicants receive a commitment letter from the Secretary's determination authorizing commitment and investment of resources. Step 10: After a Secretary's determination and closing, a Notice to Proceed is issued to the builder. Shortly after, a Construction Kick-off Meeting is held to coordinate construction phase processes and marketing and occupancy requirements.
