structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program funded by the American Rescue Plan Act (ARP) that provides stabilization funding to eligible child care providers to help keep their doors open and support early childhood educators. The program addresses the hardships faced by child care providers and instability in the child care market caused by COVID-19, supporting operational stability and continuity of care during the pandemic recovery period.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a base award of $10,000 plus additional per-slot funding of $126 for licensed child care slots serving infants, toddlers, or children in the Child Care Scholarship program, as well as additional funding for providers participating in Maryland EXCELS (rating 1-5) and providers located in census tracts with a Social Vulnerability Index greater than 0.6. Any unutilized funds from non-participating providers are distributed evenly to grant-awarded providers per licensed slot. Funding does not need to be repaid if recipients meet all required certifications. Eligible uses include: personnel costs (wages, benefits, premium pay, bonuses, vaccine-related costs, professional development); facility costs (rent, mortgage, utilities, maintenance, COVID-related facility improvements); PPE and cleaning supplies (sanitizing materials, personal protective equipment, cleaning services, health and safety trainings); equipment and supplies (accounting/payroll software, health monitoring equipment, computers/devices for remote communication); goods and services (food, diapers, toys, cribs, bedding, books, craft materials, licensing fees); behavioral health supports; and past expenses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 23, 2022 by 6:00pm (EST) CLOSED
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible child care providers including family child care homes, large family child care homes, child care centers, and education programs under a Letter of Compliance operating in Maryland. Licensed child care providers and programs in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Personnel costs including wages, benefits, premium pay, bonuses, recruitment and retention expenses, vaccine-related costs, and professional development; facility costs including rent, mortgage, utilities, maintenance and improvements, and insurance; personal protective equipment, cleaning and sanitation supplies and services, and health and safety trainings; equipment and supplies to respond to COVID-19 including software, computers, and monitoring equipment; goods and services necessary to maintain or resume child care services including food, diapers, toys, bedding, books, and licensing fees; behavioral health supports for children and employees; and past expenses incurred during the pandemic.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. All counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be an operating child care provider (family child care home, large family child care home, child care center, or education program under a Letter of Compliance)
Must meet one criteria from each eligibility column as specified in the program eligibility chart
Must have been licensed as a child care provider in Maryland
Must comply with all required certifications throughout the grant term
Head Start and Early Head Start programs are not eligible
Providers who own or operate more than one child care location must submit separate applications for each site
Must implement policies in line with Maryland guidance and CDC guidance to the greatest extent possible when open and providing services

Must continue paying employees at least the same weekly wages and maintain the same benefits throughout the grant period and not furlough employees from the date of application submission through the duration of the grant period
Must provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for families enrolled in the child care program to the extent possible, prioritizing relief for families struggling to make payments

Must keep all documents and records related to the child care business stabilization grant, including health and safety protocols shared with families, employee payment and benefits records, and family payment records
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted online only through a survey link. Providers cannot submit scanned copies, faxes, or written applications. Applicants can access the application via computer or mobile device. The MSDE provides virtual customer service support sessions including documentation needed webinars, application form walkthroughs, and questions and answers sessions. All session recordings are posted on the website. Providers without questions can contact MSDE staff via email or inquiry form, with responses provided within 24 hours or the next business day. An expense tracking tool is available to help providers organize and document their eligible expenses by category and month.

structured_extraction.program_name: 2022 Equipment Assistance Grants for National School Lunch Program (NSLP) Operator
structured_extraction.program_description: This grant provides funds for National School Lunch Program operators to purchase equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals. Equipment requests may include new equipment, renovation of equipment, or replacement of equipment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants fund the purchase of equipment for school food service operations. The 2022 funding amount is $954,126. Equipment must have a value greater than $1,000 per item. All costs must be incurred after grant approval. The grant operates in two phases: Phase 1 (October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024) and Phase 2 reallocation (July 1, 2024 through September 30, 2024). If you receive a Phase 1 award, all spending must be completed and a final report submitted no later than June 30, 2024. Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline. Priority is given to high-needs schools where 50 percent or more of enrolled students are eligible for free or reduced-price meals, schools demonstrating meaningful nutrition impacts, those adopting lunchroom changes, those with aging equipment, schools with limited existing funding sources, and schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, February 1, 2023. No later than 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: National School Lunch Program operators in Maryland schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of new food service equipment, renovation of existing equipment, or replacement of equipment to serve healthier school meals, improve food safety, and expand access to school meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Each individual equipment item requested must have a value greater than $1,000
Costs incurred prior to grant approval cannot be funded
Priority given to high-needs schools with 50 percent or more of enrolled students eligible for free or reduced-price meals
Priority given to schools demonstrating opportunities for meaningful nutrition impacts
Priority given to schools adopting lunchroom changes providing convenience and appeal to students
Priority given to schools with aging food service equipment or lack of appropriate items
Priority given to schools with limited existing state and local funding for equipment purchases
Priority given to schools that have not previously received an NSLP Equipment Grant

Grantees must comply with state and federal statutes and regulations including the 1964 Civil Rights Act, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 34, Elementary and Secondary Education Act, Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR), General Education Provisions Act (GEPA), and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
Grantees must ensure facilities are accessible to individuals with disabilities as required by the ADA

Grantees must comply with Federal Executive Order 12549 on Debarment and Suspension and file a signed Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility and Voluntary Exclusion form with MSDE
Grantees must establish and maintain fiscal control and fund accounting procedures as set forth in 2 CFR §200
Grantees must retain all records of financial transactions and accounts relating to the grant for a period of five years or longer if required by federal regulation
Entities expending federal funds of $750,000 or more in a single fiscal year must have an annual financial and compliance audit in accordance with 2 CFR Subpart F 200.500 et. seq.
Grantees must receive prior written approval from the MSDE Program Monitor before implementing any programmatic changes

Grantees must receive prior written approval from the MSDE Program Monitor for any budgetary realignment of $1,000 or 15% of total object, program or category of expenditure, whichever is greater, with at least 45 days prior notice before the end of the grant period

Grantees must ensure programs and projects offering web-based or technology-based instructional products funded through this grant comply with Section 508 of the Federal Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and Section 7-910 of the Education Article, Annotated Code of Maryland
Grantees must submit all required reports including complete, accurate, and timely progress and final reports
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application was released on December 26, 2022 on the MSDE Grants webpage. Complete the grant application with required components including Goal(s), Measurable Outcome(s), Evidence of Impact, Plan of Operation, Key Personnel, and Project Timeline. Access the Budget Template from the Maryland Accountability Reporting System (MARS) or contact Sara Brandt. Submit the completed grant application by February 1, 2023, at 5:00 p.m. EST. MSDE provided customer service support sessions on January 9, 2023, and January 18, 2023, to review requirements and answer questions. Awards are made within 30 days of the application deadline, with NOGAs to follow the notification of the grant award.

structured_extraction.program_name: APPS (Autism Program Planning Success for Employment)
structured_extraction.program_description: APPS assists job seekers with Autism develop self-determination and employment readiness skills through small group, interactive learning sessions covering self-advocacy, career interests, job exploration, work expectations, and employer expectations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: APPS provides free training and employment readiness instruction through small group, interactive learning sessions at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center. Sessions focus on self-determination, self-advocacy, decision making, career interests and skills, job exploration, work expectations and responsibilities, and employer and employee expectations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with a documented diagnosis of Autism who can participate in program activities with little supervision.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development in employment readiness, self-advocacy, career exploration, and work expectations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered at DORS Workforce & Technology Center in Maryland.
requirements_list: Documentation of Autism
An interview with program staff
Ability to participate in all APPS programs and community activities with little supervision
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals apply by contacting DORS, providing documentation of Autism diagnosis, and completing an interview with program staff.

structured_extraction.program_description: Project ACT provides on-site training for child care staff, individualized child observations and support planning, center-wide coaching and mentoring to increase staff knowledge and skills, family support, resource and referral services, and access to individualized services to facilitate the optimal growth and development of children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides on-site training for child care staff, individualized child observations and support planning, center-wide coaching and mentoring, family support, and resource and referral services to help child care centers improve staff knowledge and skills and support children's growth and development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care centers, programs participating in Maryland EXCELS, and their staff
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff training, coaching, mentoring, individualized child observations and support planning, family support, resource and referral services, and individualized services for optimal child growth and development

structured_extraction.program_name: Accreditation Support Fund - Maryland Program Accreditation
structured_extraction.program_description: Assists licensed child care centers and school-age only programs with reimbursement for non-consumable instructional materials and learning materials needed to pursue Maryland Accreditation, supporting quality improvement efforts through the state accreditation process. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, accreditation fees, costs already covered by other funding sources, or costs exceeding the fee charged by the accrediting organization.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund provides reimbursement for non-consumable instructional and learning materials purchased in pursuit of Maryland Accreditation. Maximum reimbursement: $2,500 for programs serving 100 or fewer children, or $3,000 for programs serving more than 100 children per accreditation cycle. Eligible materials include curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities. Reimbursement covers items purchased within 12 months before the date of application. Funds cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, accreditation fees, costs already covered by other funding sources, or costs exceeding the fee charged by the accrediting organization.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling applications
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and school-age only programs in Maryland pursuing or having completed initial self-appraisal as part of Maryland Accreditation process
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Non-consumable instructional and learning materials associated with pursuing Maryland Accreditation, including curricula, classroom technology, outdoor play equipment, science and sensory materials, books, and literacy activities. Cannot be used for facility improvements, association membership fees, staff training, accreditation fees, costs covered through another funding source, or costs exceeding the fee charged by the accrediting organization.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center or school-age only program
Must be pursuing Maryland Accreditation or have completed the Initial Self-Appraisal as part of the Maryland Accreditation process
Purchases must have been made within 12 months before the date of application
Each child care center site with an individual license number can submit a separate application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process involves three steps: (1) Gather receipts for learning materials purchased during the accreditation process or during accredited status, dating back up to 12 months before application date; (2) Complete the Infants and Toddlers Learning Materials Checklist and/or Preschool and School-Age Learning Materials Checklist, ensuring information matches receipts; (3) Complete the Application for Maryland Accreditation Support in Maryland OneStop portal and upload documentation. Applications are reviewed within 30 business days. Approvals and requests for further information are sent through the Maryland OneStop portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs with the costs of pursuing national accreditation. The fund covers required application fees for national accreditation, including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees charged by recognized accrediting organizations. Assistance cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization and cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or costs paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The fund covers required application fees for national accreditation, including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees charged by recognized accrediting organizations. Support funds are paid directly to the accrediting organization on behalf of the program. Assistance cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization. Funds may not be applied to membership fees, program improvements, staff training, or other accreditation expenses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed family child care providers, child care centers, and school-age only programs in Maryland seeking national accreditation from a recognized accrediting organization.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Required application fees for national accreditation, including initial application fees, renewal application fees, and annual update fees. Cannot be used for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, membership fees, program improvements, or costs paid through another funding source.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All licensed child care centers, registered family child care providers, and school-age only programs in Maryland (statewide).
requirements_list: Must be a licensed child care center, registered family child care provider, or school-age only program

Must be pursuing accreditation from a recognized national accrediting organization recognized by MSDE (AMS, AMI/USA, AIMS, AWSNA, Cognia Early Learning Accreditation, COA/ASA, Lumen Accreditation, Maryland Accreditation, MSA-CESS, NAC, NAEYC, NAFCC, or NECPA)
Program must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Cannot use funds for costs paid through another funding source
Cannot use funds for facility improvement, association membership fees, staff training, or membership fees
Costs cannot exceed the fee charged by the accreditation organization
Must submit copy of completed application submitted to the accrediting organization
Must submit completed Accreditation Work Plan
Must submit copy of the accrediting organization's fee page
Must submit copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Visit earlychildhood.marylandpublicschools.org and search for 'accreditation support fund.' 2. Select the Accreditation Support Fund link and choose 'Apply Online.' 3. Collect all required documents: copy of accreditation application submitted to the accrediting organization, completed Accreditation Work Plan, copy of the accrediting organization's fee page, and copy of current accreditation certificate if currently accredited. 4. Complete the Application for National Accreditation Support on the OneStop Portal. 5. Upload all required documentation. 6. Submit the application. 7. MSDE will review and approve the application within 30 days. 8. The MSDE Accreditation Manager will notify you via email and OneStop messages on the status of your application. 9. The award will be paid directly to the accrediting organization on your behalf.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial reimbursement to help school-based programs and organizations serve snacks or suppers to children in afterschool care. The program operates through either the National School Lunch Program or the Child and Adult Care Food Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement to help programs serve snacks or suppers to children in afterschool programs. Programs can participate through either the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) for snacks or the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) for snacks and suppers. Requirements include being area eligible and providing educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment. Snacks must meet USDA nutritional requirements. Children participating in approved afterschool care programs age 18 and under are eligible to receive reimbursable snacks. The amount of reimbursement is set federally and covers the cost of snacks served in accordance with program meal patterns.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, non-profit organizations, and school-based or non-school-based organizations offering afterschool programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for serving healthy snacks and suppers to children in afterschool programs that meet USDA nutritional requirements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Area eligible programs as determined by USDA
requirements_list: Program must be school-based or a non-profit or non-school-based organization
Must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment
For NSLP component: school district must be participating in the National School Lunch Program
For CACFP component: program must be area eligible
Afterschool care program must primarily provide care for children after school
Must have organized, regularly scheduled activities in a structured and supervised environment
Must include education or enrichment activities distinct from extracurricular programs organized for scholastic, cultural or athletic purposes
Eligible education or enrichment activities include homework assistance, tutoring, supervised drop-in athletic programs, extended day programs, drama activities, and arts and crafts programs
Organized interscholastic programs or community-level competitive sports are not eligible
Children served must be age 18 and under (or turn 19 during the school year)
Snacks must meet USDA nutritional requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Programs must contact their school district or local food service administrator to participate. The SFA (School Food Authority) must participate in the NSLP lunch component for a site to operate the NSLP Afterschool Snack Service. Sites must sponsor or operate an approved afterschool care program to be eligible. State agencies can provide further information regarding afterschool care program eligibility and the application process. For more information, visit the USDA Afterschool website or contact your state agency administrator.

structured_extraction.program_description: Registered apprenticeship program offering students paid opportunities to join the workforce while in school through a combination of on-the-job training and related technical instruction. Students earn while learning in their area of interest, with flexibility to participate during school, after school, over summer, or on weekends.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Students receive 450 hours of paid on-the-job training and 144 hours of related technical instruction. Placements and schedules are set by employers and students to meet individual needs. Adult apprentice programs may help with college tuition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: High school and adult students seeking career-connected learning opportunities in registered apprenticeships across Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Paid on-the-job training in various industries and occupations. For adult apprentices, potential assistance with college tuition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide across Maryland through local school districts and employers.
requirements_list: Approved by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council
Delivered in partnership with local school districts
Must be matched with an employer through school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students and families should talk to their school's apprenticeship or career-connected learning coordinator to explore opportunities, eligibility, and scheduling. Bring your career interests and availability to your coordinator, who will help match you with employers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assistive Technology (AT) provides customized assessments, equipment, and training to help job seekers with disabilities improve their capabilities and achieve employment goals. The program includes items such as video magnifiers, note-taking devices, specialized software for reading and writing, and mobile devices for organization and time management.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS RTS staff provides customized assessments to find appropriate assistive technology, training on how to use the equipment and software, and technical support. Assessments and training can be held at the Workforce Technology Center (WTC) or in the individual's community. Equipment and software provided may include video magnifiers, note-taking devices, voice recognition software, screen reading software like JAWS or ZoomText, and mobile devices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who are DORS consumers with an employment goal
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistive technology equipment, software, training, and technical support to assist with employment goals and workplace accommodations
requirements_list: Must be a DORS consumer with an employment goal
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals contact DORS to be assessed for appropriate assistive technology to meet their employment needs. DORS RTS staff conducts customized assessments and provides training and support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A 12-week training course that prepares individuals with disabilities for entry-level automotive detailing jobs, including classroom instruction and hands-on experience in car exterior and interior cleaning, restoration, and maintenance techniques.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a 12-week training course with classroom instruction, videos, lectures, product demonstrations, and extensive hands-on experience in automotive detailing techniques. Training is delivered at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities seeking entry-level automotive detailing employment
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development in automotive detailing, including customer service, cleaning techniques, equipment and chemical safety, and quality detailing work.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Training is provided at the DORS Workforce & Technology Center campus in Baltimore.
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than two points
3rd grade or higher reading comprehension level and basic math skills
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop and kneel
Certain criminal backgrounds may disqualify an individual from the program

structured_extraction.program_description: A 16-week training course that prepares job seekers with disabilities to work in the automotive industry as entry-level General Service Technicians, teaching skills in vehicle diagnosis, repair, maintenance, inspection, and lubrication services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A 16-week training program provided at the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore that teaches automotive maintenance and repair skills, customer service, shop safety, and operation of equipment such as tire balancing machines, 4-wheel alignment lifts, and hand tools.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities seeking entry-level positions in the automotive repair industry
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in automotive general service technician skills including lubrication, fluid changes, tire services, battery replacement, tune-ups, vehicle inspections, brake repair, customer service, shop safety, and equipment operation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is provided at the WTC campus in northeast Baltimore
requirements_list: Valid driver's license with no more than 2 points
Ability to lift 50 pounds
Ability to squat, stoop and kneel
3rd grade reading level and basic math skills
No disqualifying criminal background

structured_extraction.program_description: A free online training course required by state and federal law for all child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program. The training covers health, safety, and nutrition topics required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant regulations, as well as recommended best practices related to health and safety in child care settings, connecting to Maryland regulations for child care. Participants must complete four modules, pass with a minimum score of 80%, and receive a certificate of completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free online training consisting of four modules covering health, safety, and nutrition. Training takes approximately three hours to complete. Participants must score at least 80% on all topic reviews and a final review and survey to receive a certificate of completion. Participants are allowed up to four attempts to achieve the passing score. The training is offered in monthly cohorts with a 21-day course window. Registration opens for one week each month according to a published schedule. Course is accessed at https://msde.instructure.com. New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance. Child care staff and family providers must complete the annual update by December 31 each year.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Registration opens one week per month. May cohort registration closes April 23 at 12:00 pm (training completed by May 22); June cohort registration closes May 23 at 12:00 pm (training completed by June 22). Ongoing monthly cohorts. New employees have 90 days from hire date to complete training for compliance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All child care providers, staff, substitutes, and adults responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program in Maryland. This includes newly approved family child care providers and newly hired staff. Also recommended for child care substitutes and volunteers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: This is a training program, not a financial assistance program. The training covers health, safety, and nutrition topics required by the Child Care and Development Block Grant to maintain compliance with state and federal regulations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide availability. Training is available online for all Maryland child care providers at https://msde.instructure.com, as well as through approved face-to-face trainers throughout the state.
requirements_list: Must be a child care provider, staff member, substitute, or adult responsible for the care and safety of children in a licensed child care program
Valid email address required to register
Must have basic computer skills including using a mouse, typing, email, viewing videos, navigating the internet, and printing web pages
Must complete all four training modules in order
Must score at least 80% on all topic reviews and final review and survey
Must complete final review and survey in one sitting
Certificate must be printed before course end date
Child care staff and family providers must complete the annual update by December 31 each year (for staff employed before October of that year)
Newly hired staff or approved family child care providers hired October through December must complete training by March 31 of the following year
New employees have 90 days after hire to complete the course to be in compliance
Each registrant is allowed only two attempts to pass the Final Assessment overall (system allows completion within four attempts during one cohort period)
Only one email address per registrant; multiple participants cannot use the same email address
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register during the one-week monthly registration window by completing the online registration form at https://msde.instructure.com with a valid email address. Upon successful registration, receive login instructions via email. Verify email address is correct and check spam/junk mail folders. Log into the course platform at https://msde.instructure.com/login/canvas using the email address as username and your created password. Start with the Introduction to Basic Health and Safety module; other modules unlock as you progress. Complete all four modules in sequential order at your own pace (no need to complete in one sitting). Click EXIT COURSE button before leaving to ensure progress is saved. Take notes as needed for the final assessment. Once all modules are complete, the Final Review module becomes available. Complete the final review and survey in one sitting. Submit the final assessment to receive an immediate score. If the score is 80% or higher, a certificate of completion is immediately available in the Modules section or My Achievements section. Print and save the certificate before the course end date. If the score is below 80%, you can retake the final review and survey up to one additional time (two total attempts overall per registrant). If account expires at end of course period without completion of any sections, you may register again in a future cohort. Submit certificate to licensing specialist or keep in personnel file. MSDE does not email grades or provide copies of certificates. To check your grade, access the Grades module within your Canvas course account.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The BOOST Scholarship Program provides scholarship awards to eligible students who qualify for free or reduced-price school meals and want to attend a participating nonpublic school. Priority is given to students who received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year and their siblings.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided to cover tuition costs at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board and vary based on household income (as a percentage of federal poverty levels), academic level of the student, whether the student receives special education services, and any financial assistance or discounts the school provides. The estimated funding available is approximately $9,000,000 for approximately 2,500 scholarship awards distributed among approximately 175 participating nonpublic schools. The scholarship check is sent directly to the school, which the parent or guardian must endorse on the back. The scholarship award is reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school, and may be prorated if the student withdraws or is expelled before April 30, 2027.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.contact_name: Allison Sanborn (Program Manager) / James Clark (Administrative Support)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students who qualify for free and reduced-price school meals (FARMS) and are entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year. Enrollment in a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year is required.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools. Funds may not be used for transportation, meals, or other expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland for nonpublic schools registered to operate in the state and approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program. During the 2025-2026 school year, scholarship awards were granted to students in 19 jurisdictions across Maryland.
requirements_list: Qualify for Free and Reduced-Price Meals (FARMS) - determined through Federal 1040 tax form review
Be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade for the 2026-2027 school year (Pre-K students not eligible)
Upload 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size
Nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval from or be registered with the State Board of Education
Nonpublic schools must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Nonpublic schools must provide more than only prekindergarten and kindergarten programs
Participating nonpublic schools must comply with all BOOST reporting requirements by specified dates
Participating nonpublic schools must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or gender identity/expression
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable beginning March 9, 2026. The application deadline is May 8, 2026. As part of the application, parents upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis but are not awarded on a first-come-first-serve basis. The BOOST program uses FARMS income guidelines posted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture each year. After May 8, 2026, all application data is collected and ranked by the MSDE as a percentage of the federal poverty index. The BOOST Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine the base scholarship award amounts, additional award amounts for students receiving special education services, and any other award criteria. Parents/guardians are notified by August 2026 of award eligibility and must accept or decline the award by the deadline specified in their notification. Participating nonpublic schools must confirm student enrollment. For students whose parents indicated special education services, schools must upload a copy of the student's IEP, IFSP, or 504 Plan. MSDE prepares scholarship checks at the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland, which are then packaged and sent via FedEx to participating schools. Award offers continue as parents decline awards and funds become available, with no new awards offered after December 11, 2026. Customer service support sessions are held on March 10, March 12, and weekly Wednesdays from March 18-May 6, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA training grant that expands menu planning training to address meal pattern requirements, creditable and non-creditable foods, standardized recipes, healthy food preparation methods, culturally appropriate CACFP recipes, infant feeding, breastfeeding, formula use, and safe food handling.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A USDA grant providing free training on CACFP meal planning, including menu planning principles, meal pattern requirements, creditable and non-creditable foods, standardized recipes, healthy food preparation methods, and culturally appropriate recipes. structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund (CCCPDF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A tuition assistance/scholarship program that helps child care providers and staff earn a college degree in early childhood education, child development, elementary education, or special education at participating accredited colleges and universities in Maryland. Funding is paid directly to the college or university rather than reimbursing participants. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis for first-time applicants, with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship/tuition assistance funding that covers tuition, fees, and required textbooks for associate or bachelor's degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at accredited Maryland colleges and universities. Payments are made directly to the institution rather than reimbursed to participants. Awards are made on a first-come, first-served basis. Funds are distributed on an annual basis as long as funding is available. Recipients must maintain a 2.50 cumulative GPA to continue receiving funds. Upon completion of an associate degree, recipients must work in child care at least 20 hours per week for two years; upon completion of a bachelor's degree, four years; upon completion of a master's degree, 2.5 years. Participants who do not complete the service requirement or withdraw without good cause must repay the amount paid on their behalf.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: First-time applications due by March 1; Continuation applications due by June 30; Transfer applications due by June 30
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers and staff who work in licensed child care centers or are registered family child care providers in Maryland, participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program, with at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: College tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degree programs in Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education at participating Maryland colleges and universities. Funds may only be used for actual expenses of college course work incurred after an award is made toward completion of a college degree. Funds cannot be used to pay fees or costs, including tuition, previously incurred for college enrollment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to child care providers working in Maryland at accredited Maryland institutions of higher learning.
requirements_list: Work in a licensed child care center or be a registered family child care provider in Maryland and work at least 10 hours per week
Must be participating in the Maryland Child Care Credentialing Program at Level Two or higher
Fulfill entrance requirements at the participating college of your choice
Have at least one year of documented experience working with groups of children in an approved setting
Maintain employment in child care in Maryland while participating in the program
Participate in professional development

Agree to complete the child care service requirement in Maryland for at least 20 hours per week after completion of the degree (two years for associate degree, four years for bachelor's degree, 2.5 years for master's degree)
Maintain at least a 2.50 cumulative grade point average from the point of first entering the program
Must pursue a degree from an accredited college or university recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Eligible degree fields: Early Childhood Education, Child Development, Elementary Education, or Special Education

Submit application with required documentation including employer letter or family child care license, Maryland Child Care Credential certificate, letter of college acceptance with declared major, and professional development plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Be accepted into a participating college of your choice from the approved CCCPDF list. Step 2: Schedule an appointment with the CCCPDF Coordinator at the participating college and review the application checklist. Step 3: The college Coordinator must review and sign the application checklist to confirm all required documents are included before submission. Step 4: Submit a completed CCCPDF application with all required documentation (completed application, proof of at least one year of child care experience, signed employer letter or current family child care license, Maryland Child Care Credential certificate at Level Two or higher, college acceptance letter with declared major, professional development plan, and FAFSA confirmation if appropriate) to the Office of Child Care. First-time applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis with priority given to applicants who have not yet completed any college courses for credit from an accredited college or university. Continuation applications must be resubmitted annually with updated documentation of continued employment, continued credential participation, current college transcript, and revised professional development plan if applicable. MSDE will notify applicants of approval or denial by letter sent to the applicant through the college/university.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child Care Quality Incentive Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program supports child care providers in improving the professionalism and quality of their care services and children's school readiness. It awards grant funds to incentivize child care providers to enhance the quality of care and helps them acquire supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments aligned with early learning standards and the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded based on the number of children in care: up to $1,000 for facilities with fewer than 10 children, up to $1,500 for facilities with up to 29 children, and up to $2,500 for facilities with more than 30 children. Grants are awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October. Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years. Funds can be used to acquire supplies, materials, and equipment that support quality improvement and align with the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment guidelines, as well as to support training and education in early childhood development.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Grants awarded quarterly in January, April, July, and October; check website for current application cycle.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and family child care homes in Maryland committed to improving quality and children's school readiness.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Supplies, materials, and equipment to create stimulating learning environments and implement knowledge gained through professional training and education. Applicants must itemize all proposed purchases and provide descriptions of how each item will be used to improve or enhance care quality.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland
requirements_list: Must possess a current license or letter of compliance
Must currently operate a child care center or family child care home
Must implement a curriculum that aligns with the Kindergarten Readiness and Early Learning Assessment (ELA) guidelines
Additional requirements vary by whether applicant is a child care center or family child care home
Each child care facility must submit a separate application if providers operate or own multiple sites
Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Social Security Number (SSN) identification must be provided per site to qualify for multiple awards
All statements on the application must be completed; when a statement does not apply, applicants must answer Yes, No, or Does Not Apply (N/A)
Application must be complete; incomplete applications will be returned
Applicants must itemize all supplies, materials, and equipment proposed for purchase with individual costs
Child care providers are eligible for a grant award once every three years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants complete a grant application form and submit it to the Credentialing Branch. The application must include responses to every statement, itemized lists of all proposed purchases with costs, and descriptions of how each item will improve or enhance care quality. Applicants will be notified in writing whether their application has been approved or disapproved. The revised Grant Information Guide and Application are periodically updated and announced through the IMPACT and Tidbits newsletter and posted on the MSDE website.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps eligible families in Maryland pay for high-quality child care and early education programs by providing scholarships that cover part of the child care costs. Families receive a temporary 60-day scholarship while their full application is processed, and if eligible, may receive a 52-week or longer scholarship for continued services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state pays a scholarship amount toward the cost of child care at a participating provider. Families pay a state-assigned co-payment (ranging from $0 to $3 per week, reduced for multiple children, zero for families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance or Supplemental Security Income) and any additional fees charged by the provider beyond the scholarship and co-payment. Scholarships come in three types: temporary 60-day scholarships for registered family homes or licensed child care centers, full formal scholarships for the same providers, and informal scholarships for relative care or non-relative care in the child's home. Advance payments are processed on the 1st and 15th of each month. Payments to providers are calculated by dividing weekly scholarship amount by five for daily rates, then multiplying by the number of payable days in the month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fast-Track applications are processed within 3 business days; Full applications must be submitted within 15 days of Fast-Track approval and are processed within 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receiving all required documentation. Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before current scholarship end date, preferably 15 days prior to avoid payment breaks.
structured_extraction.contact_phone: 877-227-0125 (office hours 8 am - 5 pm); 855-435-7410 (after hours Tuesday-Thursday 5 pm - 9 pm, Saturday 9 am - 12 pm)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families in Maryland with children younger than 13, or individuals age 13-19 with a qualifying disability (defined as physically or mentally incapable of self-care appropriate to the age of the child, as verified by a physician, licensed or certified psychologist, or licensed social worker), who are employed, in an approved training program, or attending school.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To pay for child care and early education at participating Maryland registered family homes, licensed child care centers participating in Maryland EXCELS, and for informal child care provided by relatives or non-relatives in the child's home.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
Be employed, in an approved training program, or attending school (both parents must meet this requirement if living in the same household)

Be a recipient of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) OR have family income below the CCS income guidelines (varies by family size and application type: new applications vs. changes/redeterminations)
Have child immunized to Maryland state standards or provide documentation supporting immunization exemption

Provide proof that each child is a citizen of the United States or qualified alien (U.S. birth certificate, proof of Head Start enrollment, permanent resident card, reentry permit, or employment authorization document)
Provide proof of identity for all household members (government-issued ID for adults, birth certificate for children)
Provide photo ID (head of household only)
Provide most recent 4 weeks of consecutive pay stubs for employed household members, or current school/training schedule on school letterhead
Provide proof of residency (utility bill, lease, mortgage statement, or Maryland driver's license with matching address)

Provide proof of all income sources including alimony, armed services pay, Social Security, SSI, self-employment, TCA, tips/commission, unemployment benefits, veterans benefits, and workers compensation
For informal child care: provide proof of provider relationship to child and child immunization records or exemption documentation for non-school-aged children
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Register for an account at the Child Care Scholarship Family Portal (family.childcareportals.org). Step 2: Submit a Fast-Track application with three required documents: proof of employment/enrollment/school attendance, proof of Maryland residency, and proof of income. Fast-Track applications are processed within 3 business days. Step 3: If eligible for Fast-Track, receive a temporary 60-day scholarship. Step 4: Within 15 days of Fast-Track approval, submit a Full Application with additional documentation including proof of citizenship status for all children, proof of identity for all household members, and any other benefits received (SNAP, TCA, WAG, GBI, housing assistance). Step 5: Full Application is processed within 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receiving all required documentation. If approved, receive a 52-week or two-year scholarship. Step 6: Select a participating child care provider in the Maryland EXCELS program and provide the scholarship. Step 7: Provider submits invoices for payment; state reimburses provider for scholarship portion. Advance payments are made twice monthly (15th and last day of month). For continued services, submit Redetermination Application 45 days before current scholarship end date. Customers may also submit Interim Change Requests for changes in circumstances. Dispute resolution procedures available for payment inaccuracies.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Scholarship Program provides scholarships to eligible families to help pay for child care services. The program serves families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, as well as families meeting income guidelines where parents are working, in approved training programs, or attending school. Families apply online through the family portal and can receive support with child care costs.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides scholarship funds to help eligible families pay for child care services on an ongoing basis. Scholarship amounts and terms vary based on family income and eligibility. Three application types are available: Fast Track (determined within 3 business days, one-time only), Full Application (determined within 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation, issues two-year scholarship if approved), and New Scholarship Application (determined within 30 calendar days or 5 business days of receipt of all required documentation, issues two-year scholarship if approved). Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before current eligibility end date for continued services. Applications are submitted online through the family portal at https://family.childcareportals.org.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Fast Track applications: 3 business days for determination. Full applications must be submitted within 15 days of Fast Track submission. Redetermination applications must be submitted at least 45 days before scholarship end date, and no later than 15 days prior to end date to avoid payment disruption.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness who need child care assistance. Families with at least one parent working, participating in an approved training program, or attending school. Families within Child Care Scholarship income guidelines.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Child care costs and services for children younger than 13 (or younger than 19 if disabled).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. After-hours support available Tuesday through Thursday from 5:00 pm to 9:00 pm and Saturdays from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm. County-specific homelessness service contacts available for all Maryland counties.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland resident who is working or employed, participating in an approved training program, or attending school
For families where both parents live in same household, both must meet all eligibility requirements
Must be within Child Care Scholarship income guidelines

Each child requesting a scholarship must be a U.S. citizen (as demonstrated on birth certificate or proof of citizenship) or a legal resident alien. Parents are not required to be citizens or legal residents
Must provide proof of identity for all household members
Applicant must be parent and/or caregiver of a child younger than 13 who is not disabled, or individual younger than 19 years old who is disabled
For Fast Track applications: must submit proof of Maryland residency, income, and activity documentation

For Full/New applications: must submit all required documentation including proof of identity, address, income, activity, citizenship/alien status for children, and other program participation if applicable

Self-employed applicants must provide previous year tax return (if after April 15) or profit and loss statements for past three months (if before April 15 or business is new), plus completed Self-Employment Attestation Statement
For those using informal providers related to child: must provide documentation proving relationship
For those using informal providers with non-school-aged children: must provide immunization records or exemption documentation
For applicants reporting homelessness: must provide referral letter on agency letterhead verifying homelessness status
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online at https://family.childcareportals.org. Step 1: Register for a new account or log in to existing account. Step 2: Choose application type - Fast Track (for new customers, determined in 3 business days), Full Application (for customers who submitted Fast Track within past 15 days, determined within 30 calendar days), or New Application (for returning customers, determined within 30 calendar days). Step 3: Complete all required fields including address and contact information (verify USPS address), applicant and co-applicant information, household members, household income and activities, activity schedules, children's care schedules, and housing situation. Step 4: Upload all required supporting documents including proof of residence, proof of activity, proof of income, proof of citizenship for children, and any other applicable documentation. Step 5: Review application, sign electronically, and submit. Step 6: Monitor application status through dashboard. Families needing language assistance can call CCS Central 2 at 1-877-227-0125 to request a translator (office hours 8:00 am to 5:00 pm). After-hours support available at 1-855-435-7410. Portal offers English and Spanish language options. Redetermination applications must be submitted 45 days before current eligibility end date; submit no later than 15 days prior to end date to avoid payment disruption.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal special education program that requires local education agencies identified as having racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B funds to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of over-identification. The program funds educational and behavioral evaluations, services, professional development, and systemic changes to increase equity and decrease disproportionate representation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: LEAs identified by the state as having significant disproportionality must reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement CCEIS. Funds support educational and behavioral evaluations, services, professional development, and organizational change initiatives. Allowable costs include: coaches/mentors for intervention support; extended contracts for staff delivering interventions; general education teacher salaries for academic and behavioral interventions; guidance counselor and school psychologist salaries for behavioral interventions and progress monitoring; professional development services for evidence-based instruction; RTI/MTSS coordinator salaries; social worker salaries; substitute teacher salaries; staff travel for professional development; tutoring services; computing devices for intervention delivery; instructional materials and software for interventions (not core curriculum); and special education teacher salaries for Tier 2 and Tier 3 interventions. Not allowable: alternative education replacing core programming, student transportation, core curriculum costs, furniture, special education eligibility evaluations, occupational/physical therapy for intervention purposes, office equipment, rent/occupancy costs, universal screening costs, or Child Find screening. An LEA is identified if it has one or more subgroups of students with a risk ratio greater than 2.0 for two or more consecutive years, or if the risk ratio declines by less than the defined amount (.15 if less than 4.0 and .5 if over 4.0) from one year to the next.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: January 31, 2025 (Interim Report #1); January 31, 2026 (Interim Report #2); August 15, 2026 (Grant Amendment); November 30, 2026 (Final Report)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA, Branch Chief; Demetria White, Interagency Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies in Maryland that have been identified as having significant racial or ethnic disproportionality in special education identification, placement, or discipline.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational and behavioral evaluations, services, and supports including evidence-based literacy instruction; professional development for staff; systemic awareness and leadership support; self-assessment and data review processes; development of comprehensive evaluation systems for plan outcomes; alignment of expenditures with specific actions to mitigate root causes of disproportionality; coaching and mentoring services; extended staff hours for intervention delivery; instructional materials and software for targeted interventions; staff training and professional learning experiences; implementation of Tier 2 and Tier 3 academic and behavioral interventions; and organizational change initiatives.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. LEAs are identified by the Maryland State Department of Education based on special education data analysis. The program applies to all Maryland counties where identified LEAs operate.
requirements_list: LEA must be officially identified as having significant disproportionality by the Maryland Department of Education based on risk ratio data
Address factors contributing to significant disproportionality in identification, placement, or discipline
Address and review policies, practices, or procedures contributing to over-identification or disproportionate placement/discipline
Convene a local implementation team to implement organizational change with regular meetings aligned to implementation timeline
Establish a diverse stakeholder group including parents, community members, school/student support representatives, general and special education coordinators, and school-based administrators
Engage in self-assessment and data review using an MSDE-recommended tool to determine root cause factors
Complete comprehensive data analysis examining decision-making processes, procedures, and practices for students ages 3-21
Consider implementation drivers including staffing, training, coaching, staff evaluation, and data systems
Develop job-embedded professional learning experiences for personnel
Create a comprehensive evaluation system for plan outcomes emphasizing implementation fidelity and measurable student outcomes
Align projected expenditures with specific actions to meet CCEIS Plan outcomes
Submit CCEIS Plan using SFY 2025 template with budget detail forms
Reserve funds must be calculated based on combined Part B 611 and Part B 619 passthrough funds
Submit interim progress reports by January 31, 2025 and January 31, 2026
Submit grant amendment requests by August 15, 2026 if needed
Submit final progress report and financial report by November 30, 2026
Comply with non-supplant requirement: use funds to supplement, not replace, state, local, and other federal funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. LEAs identified by MSDE as having significant disproportionality receive notification and are required to develop a CCEIS Plan. 2. Complete the SFY 2025 CCEIS Plan template including: identification of the local education agency implementation team; specification of significant disproportionality categories being addressed; programmatic self-assessment and root cause analysis using an MSDE-recommended tool; planned response actions (PRAs) for each area of disproportionality with aligned activities, goals, and interim benchmarks; and detailed budget. 3. Submit MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25 for each funding source and corresponding Budget Detail Forms with itemized expenses. 4. Obtain signatures from local director of special education, chief academic officer, finance officer, and superintendent. 5. Submit plan for MSDE, DEI/SES review and approval by designated deadline. 6. Upon approval, implement planned response actions and monitor progress using identified data tools. 7. Submit interim progress reports tracking student outcomes, implementation fidelity, and budget expenditures by January 31 of each year. 8. Submit budget amendments if needed by August 15, 2026. 9. Submit final progress report and cumulative variance report by November 30, 2026. Throughout implementation, LEAs may request programmatic or fiscal amendments as needed with updated budget documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A quality improvement and recognition program that allows licensed child care centers and public pre-K (prekindergarten) programs to demonstrate their commitment to providing high-quality early learning and school-age services. Programs work through a 24-month process to meet Maryland Accreditation Standards, complete self-appraisals with staff and family input, develop Program Improvement Plans, receive optional technical assistance (virtual or onsite), and undergo a validation visit. Once awarded, accreditation status is valid for five years. Accredited programs also receive higher Maryland EXCELS Payments (subsidy increases) and access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials. Family child care programs are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Accredited programs receive higher Maryland EXCELS Payments (subsidy increases), access to Accreditation Support Funds for purchasing instructional materials, and optional virtual or onsite technical assistance during the accreditation process. Virtual Technical Assistance consists of phone calls between a validator and program representative to discuss questions about Program Administration (Section 1) and Home and Community Partnerships (Section 3) indicators. Onsite Technical Assistance includes validator observations of indoor and outdoor learning environments for all Program Operation (Section 2) indicators across all classrooms. Validators provide written feedback within three business days of TA sessions. Accreditation is valid for 5 years once awarded. After initial accreditation award, programs must submit Annual Updates during years 1-3 of accreditation (up to 60 days before due date), with no Annual Update required in year 4. Re-accreditation begins 24 months before expiration.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care centers and public pre-K (prekindergarten) programs in Maryland seeking to demonstrate commitment to high-quality early learning and school-age services. Family child care programs are not currently eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Accreditation Support Funds can be used for purchasing instructional materials to support accreditation efforts and quality improvements to early childhood education and school-age care programs.

Family child care programs are not eligible

Program must form a Self-Appraisal Team

Program must apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds
Program must develop a Program Improvement Plan for indicators rated Partially Met or Not Met
Program must request or decline Technical Assistance (Virtual and/or Onsite) one time during the accreditation cycle
Program must complete and submit Final Self-Appraisal with required documentation and evidence
Program must request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expiration

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Access the Maryland EXCELS/Maryland Accreditation online system at excels.marylandexcels.org and create a user account with email verification. 2. Log in and select 'Complete a Program Application.' Search for your program using License Number, Registration Number, or School ID. 3. Select your program name and confirm you are the Lead Contact. 4. Complete Program Details, indicating participation in Maryland Accreditation, and submit the application. 5. Begin the accreditation process by completing the self-paced Maryland Accreditation Orientation. 6. Within 12 months of finishing orientation, select 'Begin Accreditation' in your online binder. 7. Form a Self-Appraisal Team and complete Initial Self-Appraisals, submitting comments and required documentation for each indicator. 8. Apply for Maryland Accreditation Support Funds. 9. Develop a Program Improvement Plan addressing indicators rated Partially Met or Not Met. 10. Request or decline Virtual Technical Assistance (for Program Administration and Home and Community Partnerships questions) and/or Onsite Technical Assistance (for program environment observations). 11. Complete and submit Final Self-Appraisal with all required documentation and evidence. 12. Request a Validation Visit at least 90 days before accreditation expiration. 13. Host the Validation Visit at least 30 days before expiration. 14. Within 3 days of binder re-opening, upload response comments, documents, and pictures to validator ratings. 15. Receive Accreditation Decision from MSDE; the date of receipt becomes the anniversary date. 16. While Accredited (Years 1-3): Submit Annual Updates up to 60 days before each due date. 17. Years 4-5: Begin re-accreditation process by completing Maryland Accreditation Orientation 24 months before expiration and repeating the accreditation cycle.
