The program helps develop a professional workforce, improve provider compensation, recognize professional learning and ongoing education, and provide a structure for career growth. The program reviews and processes applications for training vouchers and reimbursement to help professionals pay for pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participants earn achievement bonuses upon achieving a credential level: Staff Level 2 ($200 one time), Level 3 ($300 one time), Level 4 ($500 one time), Level 4+ ($600 annually), Level 5 ($750 annually), and Level 6 ($1,000 annually). Administrator Level 1 ($600 one time), Level 2 ($750 annually), Level 3 ($1,000 annually), and Level 4 ($1,500 annually). Participants with credential Level 2 or higher receive $400 in training vouchers and reimbursements as funds are available (for pre-service training, conferences, and college coursework). All participants are also eligible for tuition assistance for enrolling in an approved college or university program through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund. The program supports professional development through Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key areas (Child Development, Curriculum, Health/Safety/Nutrition, Special Needs, Professionalism, Community), approved pre-service training (45-90 hour programs), college coursework, and Professional Activity Units (PAUs) for activities that contribute to professional growth in the child care field.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Coming soon
structured_extraction.program_audience: Registered family child care providers and operators, directors, teachers, assistant teachers, or aides in licensed child care centers or Letter of Compliance programs in Maryland who want to advance beyond state licensing and registration requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Professional development through approved training, work experience, and professional activities. Funds can be used for achievement bonuses, training vouchers and reimbursements for pre-service training, conferences, college coursework, and tuition assistance for Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's Degrees in early childhood education or related fields through the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide
requirements_list: Must be a registered family child care provider or an operator, director, teacher, assistant teacher, or aide in a licensed child care center or Letter of Compliance program
Must exceed state licensing and registration requirements for training, education, and experience
Cannot have been sanctioned by the Office of Child Care
Cannot be a substitute or volunteer in a child care program
Cannot be a child care center employee who does not work directly with children on a daily basis (regional/district manager, administrative, maintenance, food service, transportation staff)
Must complete approved Core of Knowledge (COK) training in six key areas for the applicable credential level
Must participate in Professional Activity Units (PAUs) related to the child care profession for the applicable level
Must continue working in a child care setting for at least one year after acceptance
Must work directly with children in an approved setting for a number of years according to credential level
Credentials are issued for a 12-month period and must be renewed annually by submitting training, PAUs, and proof of employment if continuing in the program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Participants voluntarily enroll in the program to earn credentials recognizing their professional qualifications. Providers must complete approved training (Core of Knowledge and continued training as applicable for each credential level), accumulate required Professional Activity Units through professional engagement, and meet experience requirements. Providers must work with the Credentialing Program to ensure that training is approved and applicable toward credential goals. Annual renewal is required if continuing in the program, involving submission of training completed, PAUs earned, and proof of ongoing employment. Applications for renewals will open periodically; interested providers should watch the program website and email for updates. The program processes requests within 60 days of receipt and sends notifications via email.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Child Care Resource Network Technical Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Child Care Resource Network provides technical assistance services that cover all aspects of starting, expanding, and operating a child care center or becoming a family child care provider. Services include licensing and compliance guidance, behavioral support, special needs services, and assistance with credential and program accreditation.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Technical assistance services available to existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers and playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies. Core services include licensing and compliance issues, behavioral issues, children with special needs, and credential and program accreditation support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Existing and potential center-based and family child care providers, Head Start programs, nursery schools, cooperatives, drop-in centers and playgroups, community and non-profit organizations, community groups, employers, and public agencies committed to expanding child care resources.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Technical assistance services for starting, expanding, and operating child care centers or family child care businesses. Services include licensing and compliance guidance, behavioral support, special needs services, and accreditation support.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Child Care Resource Network for technical assistance services. The network determines eligibility based on organization type and child care focus.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state Quality Rating and Improvement System that awards child care and early education programs quality ratings from 1 to 5 stars based on meeting standards in areas like developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement. The program helps early childhood and school-age care programs improve their services, increasing the number of high-quality care options in Maryland. Participating providers receive guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training, incentives, and direct payments to improve their practices.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating child care and early education providers receive quality ratings (1-5 stars), guidance from a regional Quality Assurance Specialist, training opportunities, incentives to improve their practices, and direct payments for specified use. Providers show evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards through an online system and receive ratings for each standard area as well as an overall rating. Quality Assurance Specialists are assigned by region to provide individualized assistance with increasing quality ratings and connecting providers to available training, work groups, and resources.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing
structured_extraction.contact_email: See attachment for regional specialist contacts
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early childhood or school-age child care and early education programs and providers seeking to improve quality and earn quality ratings.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Providers use support and guidance to improve practices in developmentally-appropriate practice, professional development, and family engagement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. Regional Quality Assurance Specialists serve specific county and regional areas.
requirements_list: Must operate an early childhood or school-age child care or early education program.
Must be committed to providing high-quality care and education that exceeds basic licensing requirements.
Must commit to participating in the quality rating and improvement process.
Must create and upload evidence of meeting Maryland EXCELS Standards into the online system.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers sign up to participate in Maryland EXCELS by visiting marylandexcels.org to create an account. Contact a regional Quality Assurance Specialist assigned to your county or region for assistance and guidance. Providers upload evidence of meeting standards into the online system. Maryland EXCELS staff review the evidence and assign ratings for each standard area and an overall quality rating. Quality Assurance Specialists provide ongoing support to help increase quality ratings and connect providers to training, work groups, and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education distributes bonuses to child care programs that participate in Maryland EXCELS, a quality rating system for early childhood education. Programs receive bonuses ranging from $1,000 to $13,500 based on program type, quality rating level, and capacity.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Child care programs automatically receive flat bonuses based on program type, quality rating level (1-5), and capacity size. For Child Care Centers: Quality Rating 1-5 with capacities 1-50 range from $1,000-$4,500; capacities 51-100 range from $1,000-$9,000; capacities 100+ range from $1,000-$13,500. For Family Child Care Homes: Quality Rating 1-5 range from $1,000-$4,300. For Large Family Homes: Quality Rating 1-5 range from $1,000-$4,500. Programs may use bonuses at their discretion for items such as learning materials, furniture, staff hiring, and salary increases. Bonuses are typically processed within 60 days of quality rating publication.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program window: July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.contact_name: Quality Assurance Specialists available by county
structured_extraction.contact_email: County-specific specialists (e.g., laura.kefauver@maryland.gov, rhonda.paige@maryland.gov, ashley.hensley@maryland.gov, lisa.smith1@maryland.gov, patricia.aburn@maryland.gov, audreyc.green@maryland.gov, monique.dawkins@maryland.gov, rosemary.lober@maryland.gov, shanelle.patterson@maryland.gov, maryb.johnson@maryland.gov, petrea.hicks@maryland.gov, sabrina.scott-cunningham@maryland.gov, yvonne.bell@maryland.gov, urceal.cook@maryland.gov, korbalagae.kuawogai@maryland.gov, vickie.disanto@maryland.gov, meghan.leach@maryland.gov, lornya.bowie@maryland.gov)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care programs participating in Maryland EXCELS, including child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bonuses may be spent at the discretion of the program, including purchasing learning materials, furniture, hiring qualified staff, supporting salary increases, and achieving accreditation.

Program must be in compliance with all Maryland EXCELS regulations
Program must participate in scheduled Continuous Quality Improvement visits
Program must publish a quality rating for the first time OR re-publish a quality rating of 4 or 5 to receive a bonus
Bonus eligibility window: July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No application or form submission is required. Eligible programs automatically receive bonus payments by check or direct deposit when they meet eligibility criteria (publishing a quality rating for the first time or re-publishing a quality rating of 4 or 5). Bonuses are typically processed within 60 days of the quality rating being published. Programs can check payment status on the General Accounting Division (GAD) website. Contact a Quality Assurance Specialist by county for assistance with increasing quality ratings and learning about available training and resources.

structured_extraction.program_description: A reimbursement incentive program that rewards early childhood and school-age care programs for providing high-quality services to families using Child Care Scholarship. Programs receive increased reimbursement payment rates ranging from 10% to 44% above base reimbursement amounts based on their Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating level (3, 4, or 5), the age of children served (under 2 years or 2 years and over), and the type of care provided (family child care home or child care center). For example, a Level 5 child care center caring for children under 2 years receives a 44% increase, while a Level 3 family child care provider receives a 10–11% increase depending on child age. Payments appear automatically on the Invoice Detail Report as EXCELS payments for each child.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Licensed child care providers participating in the Child Care Scholarship program receive increased reimbursement payments based on their Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating. Family child care homes receive 10–29% increases and child care centers receive 10–44% increases, depending on child age and quality rating level (3, 4, or 5). Payments are shown on the Invoice Detail Report as EXCELS payments for each child.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Licensed child care providers (family child care homes and child care centers) who participate in the Child Care Scholarship program and achieve Maryland EXCELS Quality Ratings of level 3 or higher, serving early childhood and school-age children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Increased reimbursement payments for providing high-quality child care and early education services to scholarship program participants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Provider must be licensed
Provider must be participating in Maryland EXCELS
Provider must participate in the Child Care Scholarship program
Provider must achieve and maintain a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of level 3, 4, or 5
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: No separate application is required. Providers earning a Maryland EXCELS Quality Rating of level 3 or higher automatically receive increased reimbursement rates. Payments are shown as 'EXCELS' payments on the Invoice Detail Report for each child.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal and state funds awarded to local jurisdictions through Local Lead Agencies via the Consolidated Local Implementation Grant (CLIG) mechanism. The grant covers fiscal year 2026 (SFY 2026) and includes both federal and state general funds. Funds support the creation and operation of local early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities in compliance with federal and state regulations. structured_extraction.contact_name: Daniele Redivo, Management Associate; Glenn Graymen, Lead Fiscal Grants Liaison; Nancy Vorobey, Fiscal Liaison; Brian Morrison
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Lead Agencies (LLAs) of Local Infants & Toddlers Programs (LITPs) and non-profit organizations that implement early intervention services for infants and toddlers with disabilities in Maryland jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support the creation and operation of local early intervention programs for infants and toddlers with disabilities, including grant applications, reporting, amendment request submissions, and compliance with federal and state regulations, policies, and procedures.

Must aggregate information from LITP partner agencies
Must complete grant application using current SFY 2026 forms
Must submit all budget and post-application submissions as specified
Must upload all submissions to MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website (https://msde.sftp.md.gov/)

Must send email notification to assigned fiscal grants liaison upon submission confirming document name(s) uploaded
Must save screenshot as proof of submission from MOVEit website
Must file reports by specified deadlines
Grants Submission Coordinator (GSC) must maintain access control and immediately notify fiscal liaison of personnel changes requiring deactivation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local Lead Agencies download current forms from the MSDE website. They complete the SFY 2026 CLIG Application, SFY 2026 CLIG Budget Submissions Workbook, and required assurances and certifications. All submissions must be uploaded to the MSDE MOVEit Secure File Transfer Website at https://msde.sftp.md.gov/ to the designated shared folder's 'ToMSDE' folder. Submissions must follow strict file naming conventions. After uploading, grantees must send an email to their assigned fiscal grants liaison specifying the name(s) of uploaded documents. The MSDE recommends saving a screenshot of the upload timestamp as proof of submission. Grant documents sent by MSDE are available in the 'FromMSDE' folder but are subject to deletion 30 days from posting, so grantees should immediately download and save files locally. Budget and post-application submissions follow instructions in the CLIG Grant Information Guide and use forms from designated Excel workbooks. Each Local Lead Agency's designated Grants Submission Coordinator receives individual log-on credentials and Entity Code for MMSFTW access.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: The Autism Waiver provides community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support to eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care. Services include adult life planning, environmental accessibility adaptations, family consultation, intensive individual support services, residential habilitation, respite care, and therapeutic integration. Participants also receive service coordination and full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver covers community-based therapeutic services and support provided by approved Medicaid provider agencies. Over 60 provider agencies statewide are approved to deliver one or more of the nine available services: Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance for self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills); Therapeutic Integration—Regular or Intensive (structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies); Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living); Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical home modifications to ensure health, welfare, and safety); Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training to the family); Adult Life Planning (family-centered education and support in accessing adult community services); and Residential Habilitation—Regular or Intensive (community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home). Participants must use at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month to maintain eligibility. Participants receive full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, mental health services, and service coordination through their local education agency.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of application letter from Maryland Department of Health
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old with Autism Spectrum Disorder who reside in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services including adult life planning, environmental home adaptations for safety and independence, family consultation and training, one-on-one support services, residential habilitation for community-based living, respite care, and structured therapeutic integration programs. Funds also cover full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. Children and youth must reside in Maryland. Application and enrollment procedures are coordinated through local education agencies and early intervention programs in each county.
requirements_list: Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder
Be ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old
Reside in Maryland

Receive early intervention or special education services through an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 or more hours of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit
Meet eligibility requirements for an Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) institutional level of care
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs
Maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register interest in the Autism Waiver. Parents must provide the child's name, date of birth, address, county of residence, and contact information, and confirm the child has a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder and an IFSP or IEP with at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week (for first grade and above). 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during intake call based on parent self-report to verify technical eligibility criteria (Maryland residency, age under 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services). 3. If technical eligibility is met, child's name is added to the Autism Waiver Registry and the family receives a letter from MSDE. 4. When a vacancy occurs, MDH sends an application invitation letter to families on the waitlist in chronological order. 5. Family has 45 days from the application letter date to accept the invitation, establish contact with the Autism Waiver Contact at their local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the Medical Assistance financial application. 6. Family works with the assigned Autism Waiver Contact and Service Coordinator to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility through the Level of Care assessment process. 7. Upon determination of eligibility, the State sends a notification letter including a start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 8. Family attends a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. 9. Child begins receiving Autism Waiver services and must use at least 5 hours per month to maintain eligibility. Parents must keep demographic information updated and contact the Autism Waiver Helpline to report any changes.

structured_extraction.program_name: Medication Administration Training (MAT) for Child Care Providers
structured_extraction.program_description: A required pre-service training program for individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration in Maryland. The training covers medication administration theory and practice through a six-hour classroom course conducted by licensed Maryland Registered Nurses who have completed Medication Administration Trainer training.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A six-hour classroom training course combining theory and practice in medication administration. The training covers Health, Safety, and Nutrition topics. Participants must pass both content and skill tests to receive a certificate of completion. Training is offered by approved RN trainers throughout Maryland, with flexible scheduling options available (day and/or evening hours). Individual trainers set their own fee structures, payment methods, refund and cancellation policies. Some trainers offer special needs support services for children with individualized medical management needs (Type 1 Diabetes, Seizure management, Tube Feeding, Urinary Catheter, Oxygen Mask/Cannula) and some offer Spanish language instruction.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in medication administration for child care providers
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide - All 24 counties plus Baltimore City. Approved RN trainers serve specific county combinations.
requirements_list: Individuals must be seeking to acquire a Child Care Center License or Family Child Care Registration

Training must be provided by a licensed Maryland Registered Nurse who has completed Medication Administration Trainer training and is approved by the Nurse Consultant in the Office of Child Care's Licensing Branch
The RN trainer must have a current Maryland Board of Nursing (MBON) RN license
Participants must pass content and skill tests to receive certificate of completion
Training must be six hours in duration covering medication administration theory and practice
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Nursing Consultant at (410) 767-1853 or find an approved Medication Administration RN Trainer in your area using the approved trainer list. Individual trainers have their own registration processes and fee structures. Trainers are responsible for establishing their own application/registration procedures, class schedules, fees, and policies. Contact the specific trainer directly to enroll in a class. Trainers must submit their Training Plans to MSDE Office of Child Care, Licensing Branch specifying counties served, hours offered, fee structure, payment methods, refund and cancellation policies, and advertising methods.

structured_extraction.program_name: Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Funds community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and additional services designed to complement their regular academic program. Community learning centers offer families literacy instruction and related educational development programs. The program targets students and families at schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Programs occur before school, after school, during the summer, and on Saturdays to keep students safe, assist working families, and improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to local education agencies (LEAs), non-profit agencies, city or county government agencies, community and faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, and for-profit corporations to provide academic enrichment and educational services to students and families at Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students. Programs must provide minimum hours of programming: School Year programs require no less than 12 hours per week for 25 weeks (or 4 hours on Saturdays for 25 weeks) with at least 4 hours of academic programming per week; Summer programs require no less than 80 hours including at least 32 hours of onsite academic and enrichment programming. Funds can support salaries and fringe benefits for staff, professional development, curriculum purchases, classroom materials and supplies, remedial and academic enrichment activities, arts and music education, tutoring and mentoring, technology education, expanded library services, drug and violence prevention programs, counseling, and character education. Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance. Grant awards are three-year cycles with funding at 100% of original award contingent on availability of funding and satisfactory performance. Grants must be expended in the grant year awarded; no carryover of funds is permitted. Final expenditure reports are due 60 days after the end of the grant period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Schools, local education agencies, faith-based organizations, and community-based organizations serving students and families primarily attending Title I eligible schools or schools with high percentages of low-income students. Eligible applicants include LEAs, Title I schools serving at least 40% low-income students, high schools with graduation rates less than 67%, and other schools determined by LEAs to need intervention and support.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Intervention strategies and curriculum purchases (meeting ESSA evidence criteria); salaries and fringe benefits for staff; professional development and trainings; consultants and evaluators; classroom materials and supplies; remedial educational activities and academic enrichment programs; core academic subject activities; arts and music education; entrepreneurial education and college/career readiness programs; tutoring and mentoring services; programs for limited English proficient students; recreational activities; telecommunications and technology education; expanded library services; drug and violence prevention programs; counseling programs; character education programs. Unallowable expenses include proposal preparation costs, pre-award costs, entertainment and refreshments, unapproved field trips, end-of-year celebrations, game systems, unapproved overnight trips, incentives, advertisements, decorative items, facility or vehicle purchases, capital improvements, supplanting other funds, and personal dues to organizations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided to students and families who primarily attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. The program is available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Participants must provide services to students and families of students who primarily attend Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of low-income students
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance
Proposed activities must target students and families from low-income backgrounds
Demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served as indicated in the original application or most recent grant renewal application
Attend required out-of-school time national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings
Submit required documentation in a timely manner including monitoring components, corrective actions, monthly reimbursement expenditure reports, and detailed local narrative evaluation reports
Maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to U.S. Department of Education 21 Annual Performance Report database by established deadlines
Participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements

Meet minimum programming hours: School Year programs no less than 12 hours per week for 25 weeks or 4 hours on Saturdays for 25 weeks with at least 4 hours of academic programming; Summer programs no less than 80 hours including at least 32 hours onsite academic and enrichment programming
Provide comparable opportunities for public and private school student participation with evidence of consultation with private school officials
Provide timely notice of intent to apply and disseminate information about the grant opportunity
Provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes and safety standards
Operating sites in non-public school facilities must submit required licenses, certifications, U&O permits, and current fire inspection reports
Align programs with Maryland College and Career Readiness Standards
Identify at least one Maryland Leads Strategy, Maryland Strategic Plan, or Blueprint for Maryland's Future Priority area as focus of proposed programming
Report on GPRA measures including academic achievement, grade point average, school day attendance, behavior, and student engagement in learning
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit a grant application through the Qualtrics application portal by the August 29, 2025 deadline. Applications are released on a competitive basis approximately every three years. Customer Service Support Sessions are available to assist applicants with the application process. All applications are reviewed by MSDE staff using a comprehensive peer review process. Upon submission, MSDE reviews the application and applicant's prior year performance data including start-up reports, critical elements monitoring, timely invoice submissions, and number of amendments. Subgrantees approved for funding receive a risk assessment level (1-5) reflected on the Notification of Grant Award (NOGA). Following the initial award, subsequent award years are contingent upon availability of funding, satisfactory performance by the grantee as evaluated by MSDE, and compliance with all grant requirements and conditions. Grant renewal applications must be submitted in Qualtrics with required exhibits including Performance Goals and Indicators, Management Plan, Partner Plan, and Evaluation Plan documents uploaded to the Critical Elements Monitoring folder by the deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state aid program that reimburses the cost of tuition for students with special education needs who are placed in nonpublic special education schools through their Individualized Education Program (IEP). The state covers a portion of the tuition cost as calculated under Maryland Education Article §8-415.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State reimburses a share of nonpublic special education tuition costs through a cost sheet submission process. Students placed in MSDE-approved nonpublic special education schools or individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs are included in the September 30th enrollment count and receive state aid through a tuition reimbursement process. The reimbursement covers standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services (when applicable), and supplemental aides and program modifications as outlined in the student's IEP. Reimbursement amounts are calculated based on billable units of service and IEP frequency requirements.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: ESY or Entry dates occurring during July/August 2022 submit by September 30, 2022; Entry dates occurring on or after September 1, 2022 to June 2, 2023 submit within 30 calendar days of Entry Date; Entry dates occurring between June 3 and June 30, 2023 submit by July 7, 2023; Discharge applications submit within 30 calendar days of Discharge Date; Service Revision applications submit within 30 calendar days of Service Revision Date
structured_extraction.contact_name: Sheila F. Philip, JD, Section Chief, Nonpublic Special Education; Jeffrey Miller, Data Specialist
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local school districts placing students with special education needs in nonpublic special education schools (MSDE-approved day programs, residential programs, non-approved programs, and out-of-state programs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nonpublic special education tuition costs for students placed through the IEP process, including standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services, related services, supplemental aides, and program modifications as specified in the IEP.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide for students in MSDE-approved nonpublic special education schools and programs in Maryland. Individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs may also be considered.
requirements_list: Student must have an Individualized Education Program (IEP) that documents placement in a nonpublic special education school or approved program
School or program must be MSDE-approved or individual placement must meet MSDE requirements
Student must be included in the September 30th enrollment count with a code 09 attached to indicate nonpublic placement
Application must include an approved cost sheet with each submission

For new/renewal individual placements, submission must include: IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from service-providing school stating they can implement FAPE in the least restrictive environment, and copy of agreement/decision for mediated or due process cases
Applications must be submitted to MSDE within specified timelines based on entry date, discharge date, or service revision date
All information on application must be typed or printed legibly
Local Education Agency Special Education Supervisor/Director or Designee must sign and verify the application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit either the MSDE Approved Day and Residential Program Application or the Individual Placement Application to request nonpublic tuition assistance. Both applications require submission of an approved cost sheet. Applications include sections for student information, IEP placement information, requested reimbursement for IEP services, residential placement information (when applicable), and verification/assurance from the LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or Designee. For MSDE-approved programs, applications must be submitted within specified timelines: ESY or July/August entry dates by September 30; September 1-June 2 entry dates within 30 calendar days of entry; June 3-30 entry dates by July 7; discharge applications within 30 calendar days of discharge; service revision applications within 30 calendar days of revision. For individual placements, applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry, discharge, or service revision date and must include IEP team minutes, school letter regarding FAPE implementation, and mediation/due process documentation. All documentation supporting the placement must be retained by the LEA and available for MSDE review.

structured_extraction.program_name: Office for Blindness & Vision Services (OBVS) - Vocational Rehabilitation
structured_extraction.program_description: Vocational rehabilitation services help people with vision loss obtain competitive employment through career guidance, assistive technology training, career training, job placement, and related support services.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: OBVS provides career guidance and exploration, assistive technology such as screen reading software and magnifiers, career training or academic education, job placement services, and other support to help people with vision loss find and maintain competitive employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals who are blind, vision impaired, or deaf-blind and seeking employment or vocational rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support employment and vocational rehabilitation including career guidance, assistive technology, training, and job placement.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. OBVS counselors, case managers and teachers are located in DORS offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Primary disability must be vision loss
Eligible individuals can be any age
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the Request DORS Services form online or contact your local DORS office. The form can be completed by the individual, family member, medical provider, teacher, or other referral source. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and determine eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a counselor or teacher who works in your community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Outdoor Nature-Based Child Care License Pilot Program
structured_extraction.program_description: An initiative that expands high-quality child care options in Maryland by allowing early education in outdoor settings. The program supports child care providers who want to offer nature-based care by providing a pilot licensing framework for outdoor child care programs and accepting applications for outdoor child care initiatives.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pilot program accepting applications for outdoor, nature-based child care initiatives, including support for outdoor child care program development and operations.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers who want to offer nature-based early education in outdoor settings
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Outdoor child care program development and operations
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All counties in Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are now open.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pathways provides educational support services for people with Autism attending community colleges throughout Maryland. The program is a collaboration between DORS and community colleges, offering adjustment to college life, career guidance, assessment services, employment and communication skills development.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pathways provides free educational support services including adjustment to college life, career guidance and counseling, assessment services, employment and communication skills training, and individual and group sessions. Students enroll in credit or certificate classes and register with Disability Support Services at their college.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with a documented diagnosis of Autism who are attending community colleges and developing a vocational plan.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Educational support, career guidance, skills training, and counseling to support college success and employment preparation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Offered at Anne Arundel Community College, Community College of Baltimore County, Howard Community College, Prince George Community College, College of Southern Maryland, and Montgomery College.
requirements_list: Have a documented diagnosis of Autism
Have a DORS Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) that supports college as part of a vocational plan
Register with the Disability Support Services program at the college
Attend weekly group sessions and schedule classes around this standing appointment
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals enroll in credit or certificate classes, register with Disability Support Services at their community college, and work with a DORS Pathways coordinator who coordinates with students, families, DORS Counselors, and college staff.

structured_extraction.program_name: Patty Centers / Family Support Center Network
structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide network of centers overseen by the Maryland Family Network that provides free, comprehensive educational, health-related, and family support services to parents and their children from birth through age three. Services are provided either on-site or through referral, and include quality infant and toddler care and assessment, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training, health education and referral, home visits, peer support, and service coordination between agencies. The network operates across 14 counties in Maryland with 24 Patty Centers total.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free services including quality infant and toddler care, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training programs, health education and referral services, home visits, peer support, and service coordination provided either on-site or through referral. Centers are located across 14 counties in Maryland with 24 Patty Centers total.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Parents and their children ages birth through three
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include infant and toddler care and assessment, parent education, adult education, family literacy, job readiness training, health education and referral, home visits, peer support, and service coordination
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Network operates in 14 counties across Maryland with 24 Patty Centers. Locations include Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Caroline, Cecil, Dorchester, Talbot, and additional counties statewide.
requirements_list: Families must have children ages birth through three
Services are provided free of charge
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Maryland Family Network to find your local Maryland Family Support Center for enrollment information and to access services.

structured_extraction.program_description: PEAS provides instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training to Pre-ETS students with Autism. Students participate in classroom and other activities to develop soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: PEAS provides free instruction in self-advocacy and social skills training through classroom and other activities designed to expose Pre-ETS students with Autism to the soft skills needed to obtain and maintain employment.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Pre-ETS (Pre-Employment Transition Services) students with Autism.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training in self-advocacy and social skills needed for employment.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to Pre-ETS students with Autism in Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a Pre-ETS student
Have Autism
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Students participate through their Pre-ETS enrollment with DORS.

structured_extraction.program_description: Pre-Employment Transition Services are five specific services designed to help students with disabilities identify their career interests and enhance their awareness of the world of work. Services include job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences. These services are generally short-term and cover introductory topics emphasizing exploration and preparation for employment and post-secondary education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Pre-ETS provides five services to eligible students at no cost: (1) Job Exploration Counseling to explore career interests and opportunities through interest inventories and labor market information; (2) Instruction in Self-Advocacy to learn strategies for communicating interests, needs, rights and responsibilities; (3) Counseling on Post-Secondary Education Opportunities to gain awareness of career pathways and training options available after high school; (4) Workplace Readiness Training to learn workplace knowledge and skills including how to interact with supervisors and coworkers, timeliness, and appropriate workplace behavior; and (5) Work-Based Learning Experiences to complete learning objectives through work opportunities outside the traditional school setting. Specific services vary based on individual needs and local availability.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum, Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth; Muttasim Fadl, Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with documented disabilities who are at least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old and are currently in school or an approved educational program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Pre-ETS funds support five types of transition services for students with disabilities: job exploration counseling, instruction in self-advocacy, counseling on post-secondary education opportunities, workplace readiness training, and work-based learning experiences.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local DORS offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be at least 14 years old and no more than 21 years old
Must be in school or other approved educational program
Must have a documented disability (i.e., on an Individualized Education Program [IEP] or 504 plan, or have medical documentation of a disability)
Must provide Social Security Number
Must provide documentation of disability
Must provide proof of school enrollment
Must provide proof of age
Must sign and date the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request DORS Services by completing the Request DORS Services form. This can be completed by the student, parent, medical provider, or school staff. Step 2: Qualify for Pre-ETS by providing additional documentation including Social Security Number, disability documentation, proof of school enrollment, and proof of age through the secure SARA system. Sign and date the Pre-ETS Consent to Participate form. Step 3: Attend a Pre-ETS Service Agreement Meeting with a counselor from the local DORS office to discuss career interests, service needs, and transition-aged services.

structured_extraction.program_description: A competitive grant program that provides funding to local education agencies (Local School Systems) and qualified private providers to deliver high-quality full-day prekindergarten and school readiness services to three- and four-year-old children from families with household incomes up to 300% of the Federal Poverty Level at no cost to families. Funding is aligned with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive grant funding of $19,950 per full-day slot for three- and four-year-olds. Total funding available is $26,644,000 with an estimated average grant award of $400,000 and approximately 50 grants to be awarded. Grant funds must be used to provide educational programs for high-quality prekindergarten services for a minimum of 180 instructional days per year with a full-day program (at least 6.5 hours per day). Funds support salaries and wages for teaching and assistant staff with appropriate qualifications, equipment and materials aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards, professional development (minimum 20 hours annually), contracted services including screening and intervention, program evaluation and monitoring, technology costs (not to exceed 10% of total), accreditation and quality rating maintenance costs, meal services meeting CACFP requirements, field trips, and reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs. Indirect costs are capped at 15% for non-profits and 10% for all other grantees. Grant funds may not be used for capital improvements, supplanting existing funds, pre-approval costs, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Wednesday, March 11, 2026. No later than 5:00 pm EDT.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Dr. Nykia Washington, Prekindergarten and Mixed Delivery Program Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies (school systems) and private child care providers (including Head Start, center-based, and family child care programs) that are licensed or registered and can deliver high-quality prekindergarten services to young children from low- and moderate-income families. Also benefits three- and four-year-old children from families with incomes at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Level.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grant funds support the delivery of high-quality full-day prekindergarten educational programming and school readiness services. Funds may be used for salaries and wages for qualified teaching staff (with salaries commensurate with local K-12 salaries based on credentials and experience), assistant teachers, equipment and materials (including MSDE-approved curriculum resources aligned with Maryland Early Learning Standards), reasonable rental/mortgage and utility costs (prorated by classroom square footage), technology costs (not exceeding 10% of total request), costs for maintaining accreditation or Maryland EXCELS rating, screening and intervention services, evaluation and monitoring (not exceeding 5% of total request), meals meeting CACFP requirements, professional development activities for instructional staff (minimum 20 hours supporting school readiness and early language/literacy, science of reading, early mathematics, social foundations, and HIGH QUALITY INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS alignment), academic field trips, and indirect costs. Funds cover tuition and fees for eligible families. Funds may not be used for capital improvements, supplanting existing program funds, pre-approval costs, or transportation (except field trips).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland, statewide. All Maryland counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must hold a valid license or registration (if applicable)
Applicant must be a Head Start program or meet comparable qualifications as defined in COMAR 13a.06.02
Must be rated at Maryland EXCELS Level 3 or higher for private providers; Level 4 or higher for public providers
Serve children from families with household incomes up to 300% of Federal Poverty Level
Deliver high-quality prekindergarten programming aligned with The Blueprint for Maryland's Future
Child must be age 3 or 4
Program must provide full-day instruction of at least 6.5 hours for 180 school days per year

Lead teachers must meet Blueprint for Maryland's Future requirements and hold appropriate credentials (P-3 certification, bachelor's degree in ECE or related field, or alternative pathway with minimum CLASS score)
Lead teachers with P-3 certification must be paid commensurate salary with LEA in respective county
Lead teachers without P-3 certification must be paid at least minimum salary per Lead Teacher Salary Schedule
Assistant teachers required for classrooms with more than 10 students; must meet Blueprint requirements
For classrooms with more than 10 students, must maintain child-to-staff ratio of no more than 10 to 1
Class size not to exceed 20 students
Programs must use valid and reliable child assessment tools
Programs must provide health screenings and referrals for vision, hearing, speech/language, general health, and physical development
Programs must provide family engagement, supports, and referrals for parenting support, physical and mental health services, and early intervention
Must have qualified individual with bachelor's degree or higher in ECE or related field responsible for instructional oversight

Applicants seeking renewal or expansion must demonstrate track record of success: maintained qualifying lead teacher, maintained minimum EXCELS Level 3 (private) or Level 4 (public), remained in compliance with reporting and fiscal guidelines, not under corrective action plan, and filled 85% of seats by December 31, 2025
Lead teachers must be hired by July 1, 2026
All grant requirements must be met before invoices or advance requests can be paid
For private providers: valid child care license required
For Head Start programs only: must submit letter of support from funded grantee if applicant is not the funded grantee
Upon grant award, LEAs must submit signed Memorandum of Understanding with MSDE and private providers by September 30, 2026
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must submit a completed application electronically through the Qualtrics portal at https://msde.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0qxUC1IT7xwk08C by 5:00 p.m. EDT on March 11, 2026. A paper application is available for reference only. Applications have two pathways: (1) Full Application for all new applicants and existing grantees without a track record of success, requiring minimum score of 80 points; (2) Modified Short Form Option for applicants seeking expansion of existing approved programs with demonstrated track record of success, requiring minimum score of 45 points. The application is divided into four sections: Applicant Information, Slots Requested, Application (Full or Modified based on eligibility), and Appendices. Applicants can move back and forth within sections but cannot return to previous sections once completed. Application consists of 10 sections covering program eligibility, evidence of need/market analysis, measurable SMART goals, program quality and curriculum, plan of operation, staffing and key personnel, project timeline/implementation plan, collaboration and sustainability, fiscal systems and controls, and budget narrative. Before submitting, applicants must answer initial eligibility questions confirming valid license/registration and appropriate Maryland EXCELS rating. Required appendices include works cited page, documentation of income eligibility policies per Federal Poverty Guidelines, resumes of key personnel, grant budget form, and supporting documents. Applicants should review all answers and download PDF copy before final submission. MSDE offers customer service support sessions and office hours to help applicants. Modified short form applications only require completion of Program Eligibility, Maryland EXCELS and Accreditation, Goals and Objectives, Plan of Operation (if different from prior year), Blueprint and Expansion slots information, Staffing/Management/Key Personnel (if different from prior year), Budget and Budget Narrative, and Evaluation and Scoring sections. For questions, contact prekexpansiongrant.msde@maryland.gov with subject line 'Pre-K Expansion Application.'

structured_extraction.program_name: Project SELECT (Student Education, Lunchroom Environment, and Culinary Training)
structured_extraction.program_description: A USDA Team Nutrition training grant that targeted middle schools to increase students' selection and consumption of vegetables and fruits through culinary training, food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: A USDA Team Nutrition grant implemented from 2016 through 2019 providing training and technical assistance in culinary and food service operations, Smarter Lunchrooms strategies, food tasting events, and nutrition education. Also included development of a family engagement wellness toolkit to support wellness policy implementation involving families and parents.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Middle schools in targeted school systems
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Culinary training, food service operations training, Smarter Lunchrooms implementation, food tasting events, nutrition education, and family engagement wellness toolkit development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Middle schools in Allegany, Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico County school systems
requirements_list: Middle school enrollment in targeted school systems
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: This was a time-limited grant program implemented from 2016 through 2019 and is no longer accepting new applications.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that helps child care providers expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding by providing guidance through the grant application process and connecting providers with Pre-K Specialists who walk them through every step.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides access to state prekindergarten funding through grants and offers technical assistance through Pre-K Specialists who guide child care providers through the application process and requirements for obtaining Pre-K grants.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers seeking to expand their business and access state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To expand child care services and meet requirements for state prekindergarten funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide.
requirements_list: Organization must be eligible to apply based on eligibility criteria in the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
Organization must have technical expertise, personnel, and financial capacity to successfully provide services as described in the GIG
All organization stakeholders must be supportive of applying for the grant
Applicant must read and understand the Grant Information Guide (GIG)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Pre-K Specialists provide guidance through every step of the process. Applicants should refer to the Pre-K Grants resource and complete the eligibility checklist to determine if the grant is appropriate for their program. Before beginning the grant application process, applicants must confirm they can answer 'yes' to all questions on the Grant Consideration Checklist, including: understanding the Grant Information Guide, eligibility confirmation, technical and financial capacity assessment, and stakeholder support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides nutritious breakfast meals to students in Maryland public schools, private nonprofit schools, and residential childcare institutions. The program reimburses schools and residential child care facilities with federal dollars for each meal served that meets USDA nutrition standards, helping cover the cost of providing breakfast to school-age children. Students may qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on family income.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive federal reimbursement for each meal served that complies with USDA nutrition standards. The program provides direct payments to help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals. Students from families with incomes at or below 130–185% of the poverty level may receive free or reduced-price meals. Students in families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits are eligible for free meals. All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 898,000 students daily.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public schools, private nonprofit schools, and residential childcare institutions. Over 898,000 students have access to this program daily across all 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious breakfast meals for students that meet USDA nutrition standards; funds help cover the costs of producing breakfast meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems, 17 non-profit private schools, and residential childcare institutions throughout the state.
requirements_list: Meals must comply with USDA nutrition standards
Free or reduced-price eligibility: family income at or below 130–185% of the poverty level
Students receiving Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and/or food stamp benefits qualify for free meals
Must be a participating public school, private nonprofit school, or residential childcare institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education. Individual students apply for free or reduced-price meal status through their school district based on family income documentation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides milk to children in schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate. Eligible public and private nonprofit schools, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit institutions receive financial reimbursement to help offset the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial reimbursement for milk served to children in schools, childcare centers, and eligible camps that do not participate in other federal child nutrition meal programs. Funds help lower the cost of milk served to children. Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public and private nonprofit schools, childcare centers, summer camps, and other eligible nonprofit organizations that serve milk to children, including schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for milk served to children; funds must be used to lower the cost of milk served to children.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a school, childcare center, or eligible camp not participating in other federal child nutrition meal programs
Schools with half-day pre-kindergarten and kindergarten programs where children do not have access to school meal programs may also participate
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Eligible institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. Eligible programs provide learning experiences aligned with the State's curricular and educational priorities that cannot be replicated in the classroom, emphasizing experiential learning and one-on-one support services including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants of approximately $6,706,449 available with an estimated 60-65 grants awarded. Applicants must be 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations in good standing providing direct service to Maryland students and teachers. Funds must be used within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Funds may be used for: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may NOT be used for: construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit organizations that provide enriching educational programs to Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports educational programs including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers, and professional development opportunities for teachers that connect SAI programs to classroom curriculum. Salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service staff; supplies and materials; outreach and marketing tools; and equipment for direct service delivery.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide across Maryland. For fiscal year 2027, approximately 57 organizations are in the SAI program, with an estimated 60-65 grants available. In fiscal year 2024, approximately 440,000 Maryland students and teachers were served through this program.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing
Must provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers
Programs must provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities
Programs must offer educational opportunities that cannot be replicated in the classroom
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement
Must provide names of members of an independent governing board
Must provide proof of 501(c)(3) status
Must provide copy of most recent independent annual audit or internally generated financial statements
Must provide evidence of liability insurance coverage
Must submit detailed operating budget indicating less than 50% of budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo)
Must specify all sources of income and expenditures
Must provide evidence of direct service provision to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including student age levels and projected numbers served
Must provide plans to align educational programs with MSDE educational and curricular priorities
No more than 20% of participants may come from non-public or homeschools
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application opens May 1, 2025. Applicants must download the electronic SAI application, complete it with all attachments, and save it as one PDF file. Grant applications must be submitted by June 13, 2025, at 5:00 p.m. EDT via email to sai.applications@maryland.gov. MSDE will review applications on a rolling basis and provides customer service support sessions on May 5 and May 23, 2025 to review program requirements and walk through the application process. Required documents include: Proposal Cover Page (signed by Head of Grantee Institution), Fiscal Impact Statement (Appendix A), Student Safety Response (Appendix B), GEPA Section 427 Response (Appendix C), Independent Governing Board Member List (Appendix D), Signed C-1-25 MSDE Budget Form (Appendix E), 501(c)(3) Status Proof (Appendix F), Liability Insurance Evidence (Appendix G), Detailed Operating Budget (Appendix H), and Most Recent Annual Audit or Financial Statements (Appendix I). Applications are pre-screened for submission requirements. A review committee evaluates applications using the scoring rubric. For any section scored Level 1 (Does Not Meet Criteria), written feedback is provided with opportunity to revise and resubmit. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July, sent to the State Board of Education for review in August. Final approval is determined through legislation in the budget bill for fiscal year 2027, with the Governor releasing the draft budget in January 2026 and final vote around April 2026. Grant period runs July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: Student Employment Services help students with disabilities prepare for and obtain employment in a career field of their interest, making at least minimum wage and working with peers without identified disabilities. Services are individualized to the student's career goal and specific needs and can include Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Individualized services to help students with disabilities prepare for and obtain employment. Services are tailored to the student's career goals and specific needs. Students who are eligible but on the waiting list may still receive Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jessica Markum, Staff Specialist for Students and Transitioning Youth; Muttasim Fadl, Employment Services Specialist for Students with Blindness or Vision Impairments
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities who are currently in school and meet DORS eligibility requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Career preparation and employment services to help students obtain employment in their field of interest at minimum wage or higher, working alongside peers without identified disabilities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Contact your local DORS office for services.
requirements_list: Student must meet DORS eligibility requirements for services to individuals with disabilities
Student must be currently enrolled in school (documented through IEP or 504 Plan)
Documentation of disability required (recent medical records, IEP, 504 Plan, etc.)
Student's Social Security number required for intake meeting
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete a Request DORS Services form (can be submitted by student, parent, medical provider, school staff, or others). DORS will contact the student and family via email, text, or letter to assign the request and schedule an intake meeting. Bring required documents (Social Security number, disability documentation, school enrollment documentation) to the intake meeting. DORS staff will review information and determine eligibility. If additional information is needed, assessments may be scheduled. Once eligibility is determined, the student receives a letter with information about next steps.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded program that provides free nutritious meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income areas during the summer months when school is not in session. The program reimburses providers (non-profits, government entities, and community organizations) who serve meals at designated summer meal sites. Two types of meal service are available: SUN Meals (consumed on-site with activities provided) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes available for pickup, requiring registration).
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses organizations that serve free nutritious meals to children and teens. Meals are provided at designated summer meal sites in low-income areas statewide. Two types of meal service are available: SUN Meals (where meals are consumed on-site with activities provided) and SUN Meals To-Go (where multi-day meal boxes are provided for pickup, requiring registration).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income/economically disadvantaged areas during summer months when school is not in session
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing free nutritious meals to eligible children and teens during summer
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; program operates through county-based sponsoring organizations across all 24 Maryland counties, focused on economically disadvantaged areas
requirements_list: Must be a child or teen 18 years old and under
Must reside in or be served at a site in an economically disadvantaged area
Organization must apply through the sponsoring organization in their county
Sites must serve free meals in low-income areas
Meals must meet federal nutrition requirements and meal patterns by age and grade
For SUN Meals To-Go sites, beneficiaries must register to receive multi-day meal boxes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in becoming a SUN Meals site should contact the sponsoring organization in their county. Baltimore City has an online application available. Other counties require phone contact with their county public schools or designated sponsoring agency. Program sponsors apply to operate summer food service sites through the Maryland State Department of Education.

structured_extraction.program_name: Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) Annual Training
structured_extraction.program_description: Required annual training for participating agencies providing updates on USDA regulations and guidance and professional development for the Summer Food Service Program.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Free required annual training providing updates on USDA regulations, guidance, and professional development for participating Summer Food Service Program agencies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agencies participating in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Annual training on SFSP regulations, updates, and professional development
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Participation in the Summer Food Service Program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs at 410-767-0199 for dates and locations of annual training meetings.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides funding to Local Education Agencies (school districts) that participate in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option to support recipe development using local agricultural products. The grant funds staff training, recipe tasting events, and supplies to develop high-quality recipes that appeal to students and can realistically be implemented in school kitchens. MSDE works with chefs from Prince George's Community College's Department of Wellness, Culinary Arts, and Hospitality to develop four standardized recipes using local agricultural products.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MSDE provides grant funding to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) to support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events during the grant period (May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023).
