Funds may be used for: salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside of normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (crinkle cutters, peelers, food processors, knives, roasting pans, utensils) to support recipe development and preparation, with total equipment value not exceeding 5% of the LEA subgrant total; food costs for grant-related training and taste tests, not exceeding 20% of LEA subgrant total; and consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests. Approximately ten (10) grants are anticipated to be awarded. Grant period is May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No later than 5:00 pm EST on April 22, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option that are in good standing and can commit participation of up to three schools
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Salaries/wages for substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; stipends for staff time attending training activities outside normal work hours; food and nutrition equipment and smallware (up to 5% of subgrant total); food costs for training and taste tests (up to 20% of subgrant total); and consumable costs for grant-related training and taste tests. Funds cannot be used for child nutrition program costs outside the grant scope, purchasing meals for training participants, foods for meals receiving FNS reimbursement, foods as incentives or prizes, foods provided to students and families for home preparation, foods unrelated to the standardized recipes, costs for prizes or incentive items, gardening tools or materials, or clothing such as chef hats and aprons.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Schools participating in the grant must be enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools and registered prior to application submission. LEAs selecting more than one school must ensure at least two schools serve different grade levels, though exceptions may be approved to maintain grade level distribution across all applications.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Education Agency (LEA) participating in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during 2021-2022 and in good standing
Must commit participation of up to three schools
If LEA selects more than one school, at least two schools must serve different grade levels
Selected schools must be enrolled as Team Nutrition Schools and registered prior to application submission
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners, manage subgrant funds, and ensure grant activities are implemented
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners
Schools must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
School nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Feedback from taste tests will be collected and used to modify recipes
LEA must menu at least one final recipe in a reimbursable meal by end of grant
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
Grant Coordinator must submit quarterly reports on grant activities and utilization of funds
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, training attendance records, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must: (1) Identify school(s) to participate and ensure they participate in NSLP or SSO and are registered as a Team Nutrition School; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school (up to three total) requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member; (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application including all components (school listing, recipe selection from four options: Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad, budget, and school agreements); (4) Complete the Team Nutrition Budget Form (excel sheet) with budget narrative for each category; (5) Obtain signatures from LEA Superintendent, Food and Nutrition Services Director, and LEA Grant Coordinator on LEA Agreement Form; (6) Compile all required attachments including MSDE Signed Assurances Page, signed LEA and School Agreement Forms, and Team Nutrition Budget; (7) Save completed application as PDF and submit via email to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov. Applications and all attachments must be received by close of business on April 22, 2022. MSDE will review applications for eligibility compliance, score using published selection criteria, and award approximately ten LEAs based on scores. Award notification will be sent by email with official Notice of Grant Awards processing beginning May 1, 2022 (4-6 weeks processing time). Grantees must submit quarterly narrative and fiscal reports (due June 30, September 30, December 30, 2022 and March 31, June 30, 2023), invoices as costs are incurred, and a final report by September 30, 2023. An informational webinar was held March 31, 2022 at 2:00-3:00 pm.

structured_extraction.program_name: The Judith P. Hoyer Early Child Care and Education Enhancement Program (Judy Center Early Learning Hubs)
structured_extraction.program_description: Grant-funded early learning hubs (Judy Centers) located in elementary schools across Maryland that serve as comprehensive support centers for families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 (birth through Kindergarten). Using a multigenerational approach, Judy Centers prepare at-risk children for success in school and life by connecting families with high-quality, comprehensive, full-day, full-year early education services. The program also provides grants to child care providers for accreditation and staff professional development. Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals for services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management and service coordination with community partners, and professional development for early childhood educators. Services are typically available 10–12 hours per day, year round. As of FY2024, there are 86 Judy Center sites serving every local school system in Maryland.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant-funded programs providing comprehensive family support services including developmental screenings, family engagement and learning activities, parenting training and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development programs, evidence-based family and child playgroups, referrals to services and supports, early intervention identification, evidence-based home visiting, case management with families, service coordination with community partners, and professional development for early childhood educators. The program also offers grants to child care providers to pay for accreditation and professional development programs for staff. Services are available 10–12 hours per day, year round. Judy Centers provide meals to children and families during school days, school breaks, weekends, and after-school hours. Each Judy Center organizes a minimum of two on-site parent and child playgroup sessions every week (statewide average is three per week). Judy Centers are required to partner with early childhood providers and programs and form partnerships with Early Head Start and Head Start programs, licensed child care centers, family child care providers with accreditation or pursuing accreditation, preschool special education programs, workforce development programs, family literacy programs, early intervention programs, and community health and family support organizations.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually (approximately June).
structured_extraction.contact_name: Kaymi Plank, Judy Center Program Manager; Nancy Garcia, Judy Center Specialist (Spanish language assistance); Judy Walker; Individual Judy Center coordinators by school location
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children from prenatal stages through age 5 (birth through Kindergarten) who live within the school zone of a Judy Center location, with priority for families in Title I school districts and historically underserved communities. Also serves child care providers who serve at-risk children from birth to age six, and early childhood educators and early childhood program partners through professional development, training, and collaboration opportunities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services include developmental screenings, family learning activities, parenting classes and workshops, connections to adult education and workforce development, evidence-based playgroups, service referrals, early intervention identification, home visiting, case management, service coordination, professional development for early childhood educators, meals for children and families, health-related services (dental, vision, hearing screenings; mental health assessments; physical growth and nutritional assessments), connections to health care insurance and WIC programs, and grants for child care provider accreditation and staff professional development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Judy Centers are located in elementary schools across Maryland, serving every local school system in all 24 Maryland jurisdictions (counties and Baltimore City). As of FY2024, 86 Judy Center sites operate statewide. Families must live within the school zone/catchment area where their Judy Center is located. The program prioritizes Title I and high-needs school districts.
requirements_list: Child must be prenatal through age 5 (birth through Kindergarten)
Child must live within the school zone/catchment area where the Judy Center is located
Family must reside in the designated Judy Center school zone
Children in the service zone may attend Pre-K and Kindergarten at the school where the Judy Center is located

Families are considered served by the Judy Center if they engage with the Judy Center at least 12 times during the fiscal year or are enrolled in formal partner programs such as Kindergarten, Prekindergarten, Early Head Start, Head Start, Patty Centers, family child care providers, or accredited child care centers
Children with disabilities and their families are fully included in all services as part of the Individualized Education Program (IEP) and Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP)
Child care providers seeking grants must use funds for accreditation and professional development programs for staff
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Families interested in Judy Center services should contact their local Judy Center directly or visit the Judy Center locations map at marylandfamiliesengage.org/judy-center-hubs-map/. Individual Judy Center coordinators can provide enrollment information and answer questions about services available in each school zone. A comprehensive contact list of all 86 Judy Center sites with coordinator names, phone numbers, and emails by county and school location is available to help families locate and contact their nearest Judy Center. Child care providers interested in grants should contact the program annually (approximately June).

structured_extraction.program_description: The Ticket to Work program connects people with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) with the Department of Rehabilitation Services (DORS). DORS develops an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with participants and provides services including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, benefits counseling, and ongoing support to help achieve and maintain employment. The program provides protection from Continuing Disability Reviews as long as the Ticket is in use and timely progress is demonstrated.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: DORS provides free services to help individuals with disabilities find employment. Services include training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement assistance, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services. There are no costs to participate in the program. After achieving employment and closing the case with DORS, the individual is connected with a partner Employment Network to provide continued employment supports.
structured_extraction.program_audience: People with disabilities who receive Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) or Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support employment goals including training, career counseling, vocational rehabilitation, job placement, benefits counseling, and ongoing support services.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland
requirements_list: Must receive SSDI or SSI from the Social Security Administration
Must sign an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE) with DORS to have Ticket considered 'In Use'
Must demonstrate timely progress toward employment or educational goals as defined by SSA
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DORS Ticket Coordinator to begin services. Work with a DORS counselor to develop an Individualized Plan for Employment (IPE). If your Ticket is already assigned to another Employment Network, DORS will coordinate with that provider. DORS handles coordination with SSA to ensure your Ticket is available and assignable.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides eligible child care providers with up to $400 annually to cover the costs of approved training, conferences, and college coursework. Providers can either receive a training voucher to pay for training in advance or submit for reimbursement after training completion.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible child care providers receive up to $400 per year. Training vouchers are issued to approved applicants to use as payment for approved training before it occurs. Training reimbursement is provided after training completion for eligible expenses including approved Core of Knowledge training (minimum 2 clock hours), pre-service training, conference registration, and approved college coursework. To use a voucher, the recipient signs and forwards it to the approved trainer or training organization. For reimbursement, providers submit documentation of training completion including transcripts, grade slips, or certificates of successful completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Training voucher applications must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training. Training reimbursement applications must be submitted within 180 days of training completion. Applications accepted beginning December 29, 2025. Applicants will receive notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Child care providers in Maryland who hold a Maryland Child Care Credential at Level 2 or higher, or who held such a credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Approved Core of Knowledge training, pre-service training, registration at statewide and national child care conferences, and approved college coursework. Ineligible uses include training not approved by MSDE, training fees, association membership fees, and CDA credential or CDA renewal fees.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must hold a Maryland Child Care Credential Level 2 or higher, OR have held a Level 2 or higher credential that expired between July 1, 2024 and August 30, 2025
Training must be MSDE-approved according to COMAR 13A.14.09
For training vouchers: application must be submitted at least 60 days before the conference or pre-service training
For training reimbursement: application must be submitted within 180 days of training completion
For training reimbursement: training must have taken place less than 181 days before the application date
Documentation of training completion (transcript, grade slip, or certificate of successful completion) is required
For reimbursement: receipt showing amount paid must be included
All applications must be submitted via Maryland OneStop platform
If a training voucher is not used without good cause, the provider must repay the voucher amount and becomes ineligible for additional vouchers until repayment is made
Applicants will receive approval or denial notification via email within 30 days of application submission
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a completed application and required documentation via the Maryland OneStop online platform. Applicants must create an individual account on Maryland OneStop. For training vouchers, submit at least 60 days before the training or conference. For training reimbursement, submit within 180 days of training completion. Applicants will receive a notification of approval or denial via email within 30 days of application submission. If approved, download your training voucher PDF from your Maryland OneStop dashboard by clicking 'View Submission', then 'My Dashboard', selecting the application, scrolling to the 'MSDE Approved Training Voucher' section, and downloading the PDF. Sign and forward the voucher to the Trainer/Training Organization to complete training registration. Once training is completed, log back into Maryland OneStop, go to 'My Dashboard', select the application, scroll to the 'Verification of Training Completion' section, click 'Choose File' to upload your certificate of completion, and press 'Submit'. Trainers and training organizations submit the used voucher to MSDE for payment.

structured_extraction.program_name: Transition Services for Students with Disabilities
structured_extraction.program_description: Transition services are activities that prepare students with disabilities, including those with vision loss, to move from school to post-school life, including employment, education, and independent living.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Transition services help students with disabilities, including those with vision loss, prepare for post-secondary employment, education, and independent living through career exploration, training, and support.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students with disabilities, including those with vision loss, preparing to transition from school to post-school employment, education, or independent living.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Services to support student transition from school to post-school life including career exploration, training, and skill development.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Available through DORS offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a student with a disability
Must be preparing to transition from school to post-school life
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local DORS office or complete the Request DORS Services form. The form can be completed by the student, parent, family member, teacher, or other referral source. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and determine eligibility.

structured_extraction.program_description: VCAMP is a virtual mentoring and support service for individuals on the autism spectrum attending college who are not participating in the Pathways program. The program helps students transition into and navigate college while developing self-advocacy and social skills for college success.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: VCAMP provides free remote mentoring and support services to help college students on the autism spectrum transition into college, navigate the college environment, develop self-advocacy skills, and increase social skills for college success.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals on the autism spectrum attending two- or four-year colleges (in-state or out-of-state) who are not participating in the Pathways program.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Remote mentoring and support services to assist with college transition, navigation, self-advocacy development, and social skills.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available to students attending in-state or out-of-state two- or four-year colleges.
requirements_list: Be on the autism spectrum
Attend college (two- or four-year institution)
Not be participating in the Pathways program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Individuals contact DORS to enroll in the VCAMP virtual mentoring program.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that reimburses businesses for employee wages while hiring and training qualified job seekers from the Department of Rehabilitation Services. Offers both short-term training (one month) with up to 100% salary reimbursement and long-term training (up to four months) with gradually decreasing reimbursement as the employee becomes more skilled.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Short-term on-the-job training provides up to 100% salary reimbursement for one month. Long-term on-the-job training provides gradually decreasing wage reimbursement over up to four months as the employee becomes more skilled and independent.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses that hire qualified job seekers referred by the Department of Rehabilitation Services.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wage reimbursement for employee salaries during on-the-job training periods.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland through local DORS Business Services Representatives.
requirements_list: Complete vendor application form
Hire a qualified DORS job seeker
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the vendor application form available on the DORS website. Contact your local DORS Business Services Representative for assistance or questions about the program. Review the DORS Provider/Vendor Application and Fact Sheet for additional information.

structured_extraction.program_description: A two-part training program designed to help individuals with disabilities who have little or no work experience, or who have been out of the workforce for an extended period, develop the skills needed to succeed in competitive employment. The program combines classroom instruction with real-world work experience through internships and community worksites.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two six-week courses (Work Readiness 1 and 2) offered as classroom sessions and community-based activities. Work Readiness 1 focuses on career exploration, soft skills, financial management, and workplace preparation through videos, lectures, guest speakers, worksite tours, and job shadowing. Work Readiness 2 emphasizes soft skills development and real-world work experience at community worksites with half-day participation requirements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Job seekers with disabilities who have little or no work experience or have been out of the workforce for an extended period
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Training and skill development for employment readiness, including soft skills, workplace communication, customer service, resume writing, and interview preparation
requirements_list: Work Readiness 1: Must be able to function in a classroom setting and fully participate in all individual and group activities
Work Readiness 2: Must demonstrate the ability to work in a real work environment and be able to spend half of each day at a community worksite with only drop-in support

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides services to individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently at home and in their community. It is for people whose main goal is not employment. A specialized component, the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), helps individuals who are 55 or older who are blind or have a vision impairment to live independently through independent living skills training, including safe cooking techniques, managing personal care and household tasks, orientation and mobility instruction, and other support to maintain independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers independent living services to help individuals with disabilities be more independent at home and in the community. The Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB) provides independent living skills training including safe cooking techniques, managing personal care and household tasks, orientation and mobility instruction, and other support to help older individuals with vision loss maintain independence in their homes and communities.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals with disabilities who want to live more independently. A specific program (ILOB) is also available for blind or vision-impaired individuals who are 55 or older.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Independent living skills training and support services to help individuals with disabilities, including older adults with vision loss, maintain independence at home and in the community.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Available through DORS offices throughout Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be an individual with a disability.
The primary goal should be independent living, not employment.
For the Independent Living Older Blind Program (ILOB), applicant must be 55 or older and blind or have a vision impairment / primary disability must be vision loss.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To learn more about general independent living services, contact the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC). For the ILOB program, contact your local DORS office or complete the Request DORS Services form. You will be contacted to set up an intake meeting where a DORS counselor will gather information and determine eligibility. If eligible, you will be assigned a counselor or teacher who works in your community.

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides reimbursement to childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, emergency shelters, and adult day care facilities for serving nutritionally balanced meals and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards. The program helps licensed daycare providers pay for nutritious meals and snacks for children, older adults, and people with disabilities in their care, supporting healthy growth and development of young children, and health and wellness of older adults and people with disabilities. Over 300 agencies across the state participate in CACFP.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: CACFP sponsors receive federal cash reimbursement for meals and snacks served to eligible children and adults that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns. Participating facilities receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Emergency shelters receive the highest reimbursement rates with minimal paperwork requirements. Child care centers that participate receive reimbursement for food costs to help ensure young children are well-fed and ready for kindergarten. Child and adult care centers serving 25 free-eligible participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week can receive annual maximum reimbursement. Family child care homes serving 6 Tier I participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week can receive annual maximum reimbursement.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible children including infants at childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool programs, emergency shelters (children 18 years and younger), and adults over 60 or living with a disability enrolled in adult daycare facilities. Also serves child care providers, public, private non-profit, and for-profit centers, and programs serving low-income families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Federal reimbursement for providing nutritionally balanced meals and snacks to enrolled children, older adults, and people with disabilities that meet USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties; statewide
requirements_list: Must be licensed to provide non-residential child or adult care services.
Participating facilities must comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns
Children 18 years and younger in emergency shelters are automatically eligible for free meals
Must be a participating childcare center, daycare home, afterschool program, emergency shelter, or adult daycare facility
Must complete CACFP Basics Training and three-part online application
Must pass pre-approval visit from MSDE
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS). For Child and Adult Care Centers: Call MSDE at (410) 767-0199 to begin the CACFP Interest Process. Complete the CACFP Interest Survey and Budget Worksheet. MSDE determines eligibility. Complete CACFP Basics Training and three-part online application. MSDE completes a pre-approval visit. Upon approval, the center can begin to claim reimbursement for meals served. For Family Child Care Homes: Contact your county's sponsoring organization to begin enrollment. Sponsoring organizations by location: Cecil County Government (410-996-0253) for Cecil, Baltimore City, Baltimore, Harford, and Kent counties; Frederick County Community Action Agency (301-600-6263) for Frederick and Carroll counties; Montgomery County Public Schools (301-284-4937) for Montgomery County; Prince George's County Public Schools (301-817-0535) for Prince George's County; The Planning Council (757-657-0716) serves all counties.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides nutritious lunches and snacks to students in Maryland public and private schools and residential childcare institutions. The program helps schools and residential child care facilities cover the cost of producing and serving meals to students.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education, Office of School and Community Nutrition Programs
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Schools receive reimbursement from the federal government for nutritious lunches and snacks served to students. The program provides direct payments to help offset the cost of producing meals. All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate, serving over 900,000 students daily.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students in Maryland public and private nonprofit schools and residential childcare institutions; Schools and residential child care institutions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Nutritious lunches and snacks for students; funds help cover the cost of producing meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems participate, plus 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions throughout the state
requirements_list: Must be a participating public or private nonprofit school, residential childcare facility, or eligible institution
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Schools and institutions apply to participate in the program through the Maryland State Department of Education

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland offers this gap financing loan program to help small businesses locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. It partners with banks and other lenders to fund the portion of a project that a primary lender cannot cover, with the main goal of creating or retaining jobs in the region. The program has been operating since 1980 and is funded by federal and state grants; as borrowers repay loans, funds are returned to the revolving loan fund to make additional loans.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides gap financing loans from $10,000 to $400,000, funded by federal and state grants. A bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. Interest rates are tied to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets such as real estate. As borrowers repay loans, funds return to the revolving loan fund to support additional loans.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships, seeking to locate or expand in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County that cannot obtain all needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, machinery and equipment purchases, start-up costs, working capital, and other business financing for location and expansion projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in, or planning to locate in, Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County in the Appalachian region of Maryland.
requirements_list: Must be a small business located or planning to locate in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington county.
A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank or lender to determine how much they will finance. Third, work with participating banks and lenders to complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that provides financial assistance to agricultural operations in Washington County for innovation and equipment purchases to enhance farm operations.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support agricultural innovation and equipment purchases for farms operating in Washington County. Through MARBIDCO and other state programs, additional financing options are available including low-interest loans for equipment, real estate, and working capital (4.75%-6.75% rates), specialty lending programs for energy efficiency and forestry operations, and various grant incentive programs such as the Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (up to $15,000 for equipment or $35,000 for real property), Maryland Value Added Producer Matching Grants (up to $75,000 for planning, $250,000 for working capital), and federal programs including USDA Rural Development Grants ($10,000-$500,000), Value Added Producer Grants ($75,000-$250,000), and the Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) for renewable energy and efficiency improvements.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural operations and farmers in Washington County, including beginning farmers, food producers, processors, and rural small businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Agricultural innovation projects, equipment purchases, land acquisition, working capital, energy efficiency improvements, conservation measures, and value-added product development and marketing
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland and rural areas as defined by USDA (territory not within outer boundary of any city with 50,000+ population and its immediately adjacent urbanized area)
requirements_list: Agricultural operation must be located in Washington County, Maryland
Applicant must be involved in agriculture, forestry, fishing, hunting, or related resource-based industries
For some programs, commercial lender participation or matching funds may be required
For USDA programs, compliance with federal regulations and rural area definitions apply
Energy efficiency projects may require third-party energy auditor recommendations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Kelsey Keadle at the Washington County Department of Business and Economic Development for information about the Agricultural Innovation and Equipment Grant. The department also coordinates with MARBIDCO and federal agencies to provide information about multiple financing and grant programs. Additional resources are available through Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org). Applicants can access program details through direct contact or by visiting the Washington County business development website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to enter into a ten-year agreement restricting their land from development. In exchange, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints through the Right to Farm Ordinance, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), and receive a property tax credit on their agricultural real property.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners who voluntarily enter the program agree not to develop their land for a minimum of 10 years. In exchange, they receive county property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home; protection from nuisance complaints via the Right to Farm Ordinance; and eligibility to apply to sell a permanent agricultural preservation easement to the State of Maryland (MALPF). The district agreement is notarized and recorded in the county land records and remains in effect for at least 10 years even if the property is sold or transferred during that period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land restriction and preservation; program does not provide direct financial assistance but offers tax credits and protections for preserved farmland
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, outside water and sewer service areas, and outside of growth areas
requirements_list: Landowner must own agricultural land
Property must be a minimum of 50 acres standalone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Property must have a minimum of 50% of soil classes I, II, and III
Must be outside water and sewer service areas
Must be outside of growth areas
Must voluntarily agree to a ten-year development restriction with notarized agreement recorded in county land records
Land may not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except as permitted by county regulations
Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within an approved soil conservation plan must be implemented within 10 years of establishment
No signs or billboards except those smaller than four feet square for property identification, home-based occupation, or sale/rental advertising
No trash or rubbish dumping except materials for regular agricultural use
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners contact the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning / Land Preservation Office. They complete the Agricultural District Intake Form providing information about their property, acreage, farming operation, and soil conditions. The county evaluates the application for eligibility. Once approved, landowners execute the Agricultural Preservation District Agreement with the Board of County Commissioners, which is notarized and recorded in the Washington County Land Records. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive program providing incentives and financial assistance to agricultural businesses and operations through multiple funding mechanisms including loans, grants, and technical assistance programs administered by MARBIDCO, USDA, and other partners.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple programs offering varying assistance: MARBIDCO Maryland Resource-Based Industry Financing Fund provides low-interest loans (2.25% initially) up to $250,000-$750,000 for equipment, land, and processing; Rural Business Equipment loans at 5.25% up to $100,000; Vineyard/Hops/Orchard Planting loans at 4.50% up to $100,000; Forestry loans at 4.75% up to $150,000. Grant programs include Maryland Urban Agriculture Commercial Lending Incentive Grant (up to $10,000), Maryland Value Added Producer Grant ($2,500-$10,000), and USDA matching grants. USDA programs provide Farmers Market Promotion Program ($50,000-$500,000 with 25% match), Local Food Promotion Program ($25,000-$500,000 with 25% match), Rural Business Development Grants ($10,000-$500,000), and Value Added Producer Grants ($75,000-$250,000). Additional programs include farmland acquisition assistance, food access programs, rural energy grants, agricultural water quality cost-sharing up to $300,000, and education funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Varies by program; many offer annual cycles. Community Food Projects available April with June deadline.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses, farmers, agricultural cooperatives, seafood/livestock processors, timber processors, rural small businesses, beginning farmers, urban farmers, and nonprofit organizations supporting agricultural and rural development in Washington County and Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, equipment purchases, capital assets, building construction, working capital, energy efficiency improvements, conservation measures (BMPs), farmers market development, local food business enterprises, technical assistance, training, feasibility studies, and business planning.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County and surrounding areas. Some programs serve statewide Maryland. USDA programs available in rural areas as defined (territories not within outer boundary of cities with 50,000+ population).
requirements_list: Operate an agricultural business or operation
MARBIDCO lending: minimum 2-year business history for value-added producer grants; hemp fiber processors must have been in business in Maryland on or before June 30, 2020
USDA VAPG: must be eligible under USDA program requirements
Value Added Producer Grants: product must meet value-added criteria (change in physical state, differentiated production/marketing, product segregation, or economic benefit from biomass energy)
Small Acreage Next Generation Program: target young and beginning farmers purchasing 10-49 acre farms
Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share: must install BMPs to prevent erosion and manage nutrients
MAERDAF: projects must serve two or more counties; maximum $40,000 award
Youth Apprenticeship: current juniors and seniors, ages 16+, in approved career pathways
Federal nutrition benefits programs require verification of matching funds for USDA grants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact Washington County Department of Business Development at 240-313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net for specific program details and application procedures. Each program has distinct requirements and deadlines. MARBIDCO programs can be accessed through MARBIDCO directly or county agricultural land preservation program offices. USDA programs are accessed through USDA Rural Development and AMS websites. Tri-County Council for Western Maryland (www.tccwmd.org) provides additional funding resources and guidance. Applicants should contact program administrators directly for current application cycles and specific requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded grant program that provides funding to eligible entities for projects supporting economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity in the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to eligible entities for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development), and Leadership and Community Capacity (organizational skills and innovation). Grants require a 50% match from other sources that must be identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact. Priority is given to projects aligned with the ARC 2024 Strategy Statement, including Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 3, 2026 for preliminary project submission; November 15, 2024 for formal grant application to Appalachian Regional Commission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities seeking to advance community and economic development in Washington County and the Appalachian region, including nonprofits, government agencies, and private organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities (entrepreneurship and business development), workforce development (education, skills, and health), critical infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water/wastewater systems), natural and cultural assets (community and economic development), and leadership and community capacity building. Projects must be consistent with ARC Strategic Goals and Objectives and demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; part of the Appalachian region
requirements_list: 50% project match from other funding sources required
Matching funds must be identified, committed, and in place at time of application
Commitment letters for all matching funds with committed status must be attached
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values
Project proposals must be submitted through Washington County Office of Grant Management

Projects should be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement priorities (Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, Traditional Infrastructure)
Projects must align with ARC Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028
Projects should reference relevant economic development plans and documents showing project is part of overall economic development strategy
Applicants must describe organizational capacity to administer federal grants, including recent awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a Preliminary Project Description (PPD) and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Washington County Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners, then submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive a letter in early fall inviting submission of a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with final application due by November 15, 2024. The review committee may reduce the amount of funding requested for each project to allow the maximum number of Washington County projects to be funded.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based on addressing specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County sets aside funding annually through Board of County Commissioners budget allocation. For FY2027, $1,200,000 is allocated across priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List (§1-108) receive grants to support their charitable work and community services. Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) beginning July 2026. All funds must be expended between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027, and cannot be carried forward. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total request. Eligible expenses include operating and capital expenses/projects that can be completed within the one-year funding period.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm
structured_extraction.contact_name: Maria Kramer, Director, Office of Grant Management; Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations within Washington County that are included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (§1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws). Organizations must have an office located in Washington County and provide services to Washington County residents.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funding supports programs and services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Grants may be used for operating expenses or capital projects/expenses. Funds cannot be used for endowments or to benefit individuals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Organizations must be located in or provide services to Washington County, Maryland.
requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners Recognized Non-Profit List (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Organization must be a charitable organization recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with Valid status
Organization must be incorporated with Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be In Good Standing at time of application submission
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must submit proof of good standing status with State of Maryland
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Application must be submitted during published application window with all required signatures and attachments
Organizations must demonstrate efficient use of funds and results-based programmatic outcomes
Organizations must select one prioritized service area: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, or Other
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of total request amount
Organizations must submit most recent audit (preferred) or detailed financial statement signed by fiscal representative(s)
Organizations funded in prior year must submit grant report by June 30, 2026 showing full expense of funds and supporting documents
Must be able to implement capital projects within quarterly disbursement schedule and one-year funding period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) annually. For FY2027, applications and guidelines become available December 1, 2025. Applicants must complete the Community Organization Funding application packet including: application form signed by authorized representative, statement of need, past performance documentation, organizational capacity and staffing plan, detailed program plan, collaboration and partnership information, budget spreadsheet using required FY27 Excel template, letters of support, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, most recent audit or financial statement, copy of IRS Form 990, and W-9 form if organization has not received County funds previously or has address change. Submissions require six hard paper copies (unbound, secured by staple/clip/rubber band) and one electronic copy combined into single PDF file. Hard copies mailed or delivered to Office of Grant Management, 100 W. Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copy emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net. Deadline is Tuesday, January 6, 2026, by 3:00pm. Applications received after deadline will not be accepted. Office of Grant Management will not check applications for accuracy or completeness at submission; applicants must verify completeness against submittal checklist. Applications scored using rubric with criteria: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), Budget and Narrative (15 points). Scoring range: Exemplary 90-100, Acceptable 70-89, Needs Improvement 50-69, Inadequate 0-49. COF Committee reviews and ranks applications; Board of County Commissioners determines final awards in May-June 2026 during budget approval. Applicants notified in writing upon completion of budget process. Funding decisions consider total allocated funding, amount per priority service area, geographic distribution, service duplication, and previous performance. Technical assistance available; contact OGM at least two weeks before deadline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A fund that reinvests cannabis sales tax revenue and business conversion fees into communities that were disproportionately impacted by cannabis prohibition enforcement prior to July 1, 2022. The fund supports community-based initiatives that benefit low-income communities and disproportionately impacted areas.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants from cannabis sales tax revenue and one-time cannabis business conversion fees to support community-based initiatives. Funds are maintained in a separate special revenue fund as restricted cash reserves and must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community organizations and programs serving low-income and disproportionately impacted communities in Washington County ZIP code 21740, which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based initiatives benefiting low-income communities including mental health and substance use services, education and after-school programs, small business grants and economic development initiatives, parks and recreational opportunities, criminal justice reform and re-entry programs, and housing assistance and homelessness prevention. Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Restricted CRRF cannabis sales tax funds in Washington County may only be used for initiatives serving ZIP code 21740, which includes portions of the City of Hagerstown and surrounding unincorporated areas of the County.
requirements_list: Funds must supplement, not replace, existing local government funding for programs and services
Programs must serve low-income communities or disproportionately impacted areas as defined in § 36–101
Funds may not be used for law enforcement agencies or law enforcement activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Washington County is developing application procedures and guidelines for eligible organizations. The County is continuing to gather community input and holding public hearings to establish the funding plan. Applicants should contact Grant Management for current application procedures and guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_name: Commuter and Shuttle Bus COVID RELIEF Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Supports Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus. Established in 2021 through bipartisan legislation with $8 million in state Relief Act funding.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: $8 million in state Relief Act funding distributed as grants to commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland commuter and shuttle bus companies facing continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Relief for continued financial impacts from the Coronavirus
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: A state-funded program that works with the Federal Farm Service Agency's CREP Contract Program to make conservation agreements permanent through state-funded conservation easements. Landowners with existing FSA CREP Contracts can add up to ten times the acreage of their contract to maximize land preservation and easement value. As of available data, the program has protected 1,926 acres with $4,835,547 invested in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State-funded conservation easements that make existing Federal Farm Service Agency CREP Contracts permanent. Landowners can extend their easement to include additional acreage up to ten times the original contract amount to maximize preservation and easement value. Once the easement is sold, it remains effective in perpetuity.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners with existing Federal Farm Service Agency (FSA) CREP Contracts in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of permanent conservation easements to make CREP contracts permanent and protect agricultural and conservation lands
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Must have an existing FSA CREP Contract in place
Landowner must be willing to sell easement
Easement remains effective in perpetuity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants with existing FSA CREP Contracts apply through the County's Land Preservation Office. The easement is processed and becomes permanent upon completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in the designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State income tax credits and local real property tax credits. State Income Tax Credit (Job Creation): $1,000 maximum one-time credit for most new jobs; $3,000 first year, $2,000 second year, $1,000 third year for economically disadvantaged employees (certified by Maryland Department of Labor). Employees must work at least 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, and work at least 6 consecutive months in the zone or zone-related activities. Local Real Property Tax Credits: 80% credit on increased property assessment for years 1-5, then 70% (year 6), 60% (year 7), 50% (year 8), 40% (year 9), and 30% (year 10). Credits apply to real property only for 10 full years following capital investment. Exemption from Commercial Building Excise Tax on new construction within Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying for-profit businesses making job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones. Businesses in manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate/regional headquarters, service industries, and retail/mercantile businesses (with location restrictions) are eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits for businesses investing in Enterprise Zones through job creation and capital improvements
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: (1) City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, includes Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and Central Business District); (2) Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (approximately 1,500 acres, stretching from Pennsylvania border to Potomac River).
requirements_list: Business must be located within Zone boundaries on designation date, relocated after designation, or started construction/expansion after designation date
For income tax credits: Minimum job creation in Central Business District = 1 new job; Outside Central Business District = 5 new jobs; Hancock Enterprise Zone = 1 new job
For property tax credits: Minimum capital investment in Central Business District = $5,000; Outside Central Business District = $50,000; Hancock Enterprise Zone = $5,000
New jobs must be created after Zone designation date
Employees must be hired after Zone designation or business location date, whichever is later
Employees must work at least 35 hours per week for at least 6 consecutive months during taxable year
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must spend at least 50% of work time in Enterprise Zone or activities directly related to the Zone
New employees must not be replacement hires
For property tax credits: Application must be submitted before project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
Property improvements must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation during calendar year of construction completion (by December 31st)

Eligible business types: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, offices for corporate or regional headquarters, service industries; retail/mercantile only in Hancock Enterprise Zone or Central Business District of Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Determine business property is in an Enterprise Zone by contacting Washington County Department of Business Development. 2. Verify minimum eligibility criteria for jobs or capital investment are met. 3. Complete Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form. 4. For property tax credits: submit form before project completion. 5. For income tax credits: submit form after hiring new employee(s) and include New Jobs Created form listing employees meeting requirements. 6. For income tax credits only: Local Job Service Office reviews employee list and determines individual eligibility as disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged. 7. Washington County Department of Business Development sends approval letter or denial explanation. 8. For property tax credits: credits automatically appear on Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher. 9. For income tax credits: claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR with copy of approval letter from DBD. 10. Submit completed application to Linda Spence, Washington County Department of Business Development, 100 West Washington Street, Suite 1401, Hagerstown, MD 21740, or LSpence@WashCo-MD.net, or call 240-313-2286.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides up to $5,000 in reimbursement for Maryland companies that receive an ExportMD Award for expenses associated with an international marketing project.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $5,000 in reimbursement for expenses associated with an international marketing project.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland companies pursuing international marketing projects
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Expenses associated with an international marketing project
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Must be awarded an ExportMD Award

structured_extraction.program_description: The Gaming Commission distributes funds from the Washington County Gaming Fund to eligible 501(c)(3) charitable organizations. Monies are collected from tip jars and deposited into a dedicated Gaming Fund account. By statute, 50% of Gaming Funds are allocated to the Washington County Volunteer Fire & Rescue Association, with the remaining funds allocated to local charitable organizations making application annually to the Gaming Commission. The Commission reviews applications and awards grants to support community initiatives in Washington County.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are distributed from the Washington County Gaming Fund to qualified 501(c)(3) charitable organizations. Distributions may not exceed $100,000 per application. Organizations may apply for multiple projects by submitting separate applications for each project. The grant performance period is one year from award announcement (typically early August). Any funds not spent within the performance period must be returned to the fund. Funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Susan M. Buchanan, Director; J. Mackereth; S. Lapole; S. Buchanan
structured_extraction.contact_email: jmackereth@washco-md.net (for general questions and submission); slapole@washco-md.net (for other questions); sbuchanan@washco-md.net (for other questions)
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) charitable organizations located in Washington County that provide support in Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Organizations may request funding for programs and activities that benefit Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, and educational and cultural activities within Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. All funds must be used exclusively in Washington County and cannot be distributed outside of the County. Organizations must be located in Washington County and provide services that benefit the County.
requirements_list: Must be a 501(c)(3) charitable organization with valid status, located in Washington County

Must provide support generally benefiting Health and Human Services, emergency services, animal welfare, civic and community activities, athletic/recreational activities, educational and cultural activities
Must not be a church or religious entity (though separate organizations operating within a church facility with their own 501(c)(3) status may be eligible)
Must not be an organization holding annual tip jar operator's licenses
Must not be a political or governmental organization or sub-organization
Must not be an umbrella organization (with exception of United Way of Washington County)
Must provide services without discrimination on the basis of race, creed, sex, age, color, national origin, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, or disability
Must be a corporation, limited liability company, or unincorporated association with valid status with State Department of Taxation
If unincorporated association, must complete Notice of Responsible Person form
Must not be the Washington County Board of Education or Washington County Public Schools
Booster organizations or other entities supporting school programs must comply with specific ownership requirements or provide letter from Superintendent
Must provide complete and signed application form with all fields completed
Must provide organization's most recent annual financial statement showing revenue and expenses
Must provide copy of most recent Gaming Fund Grant Report (or statement if never received funds)
Must provide evidence of how previously received Gaming Commission funds were expended (invoices, proofs of purchase, or cancelled checks)
Must provide supporting documentation such as estimates and quotes related to the request
Must provide completed Internal Revenue Service form W-9 and Washington County vendor forms
If applying for multiple projects, must submit separate applications for each project
Request amount may not exceed $100,000 per application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Download application forms from the Office of Grant Management website at https://www.washco-md.net/grant-management/charitable-gaming-program/ beginning April 1st. 2. Complete the Gaming Commission Grant Request form (use current version; previous versions will not be accepted). 3. Prepare required attachments: signed request form, financial statements, Gaming Fund Grant Report (if applicable), supporting documentation, Notice of Responsible Person form (if applicable), completed W-9 and Washington County vendor forms. 4. Label each attachment according to the required format (REQUEST, FINANCIALS, GRPT, DOC, NORP, W-9). 5. Ensure application is complete and follows required format. 6. Submit electronic PDF copy via email to jmackereth@washco-md.net copying slapole@washco-md.net no later than 3:00 P.M. on May 6, 2020. 7. No hard copies will be accepted; all submissions must be electronic. 8. Applicants are encouraged to schedule a public funding hearing to present their request (hearings scheduled for June 23, 2020). 9. Hearing times may be scheduled on day of application submission up to June 12, 2020. 10. The Board of County Commissioners may appropriate a portion of the General Fund Contingency annually to be awarded to targeted organizations meeting the funding goals. Grants are paid to the applicant, not to vendors. Unused funds must be returned to the Office of Grant Management within 30 days of event completion. The portion of available funding may be adjusted annually at the discretion of the Board of County Commissioners.

Have provided evidence that the request meets a critical need in the community
Do not have an alternative source of funding

Organizations must not support political candidates or organizations whose primary purpose is to influence or attempt to initiate legislation

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial incentives to property owners who undertake qualified historic preservation work on eligible historic properties. The program offers stackable credits at the county (25%), state (20%), federal (20%), and additional (5%) levels, for a possible total of 70% in tax credits.
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County Historic Properties Tax Credit provides a 25% county property tax credit for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work on historic structures that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has thoughtful, sympathetic design. An additional 5% tax credit is available for exterior work on new construction attached to an existing historic structure. Credits are stackable with state (20%) and federal (20%) credits for a possible total of 70%. Unused credits may be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. The credit is applied to the property owner's tax bill through the Treasurer's Office.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Historic District Commission / Department of Planning and Zoning
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential or commercial property owners with historic properties documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties located within qualifying geographic areas in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified historic preservation work on eligible historic properties including roof repair and replacement, chimney repair and replacement, window restoration, new storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental on exterior features and new construction attached to historic structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Specifically, structures must be located within: (1) the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district; (2) contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton); (3) properties with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay applied through a rezoning process; or (4) contributing structures within towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a qualifying geographic area: Antietam Overlay district, Historic Rural Village, with Historic Preservation Overlay zoning, or in an eligible National Register municipality
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties or eligible for documentation
Work must constitute qualified rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation that minimizes destruction of historic fabric and has thoughtful, sympathetic design
Work must be consistent with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Application must be submitted before work begins; work started prior to approval may not be eligible for the tax credit
Property owner must comply with all Federal, State, and local laws including zoning, building, safety codes, and any requirements of easement holders such as Maryland Historical Trust
Applicant must be the fee-simple owner or provide Owner's Representative Affidavit if authorized representative is applying
For structures under Maryland Historical Trust Easement, a copy of the easement document must be included with Part I application
Documentation must include itemized expenses with both invoices/receipts and proof of payment for all expenses claimed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts, all submitted to the Washington County Historic District Commission at 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742 or via email at askplanning@washco-md.net. Part I (Evaluation of Significance): Determine if the structure qualifies for the tax credit by verifying it is in a qualifying area and meets historic structure criteria. Submit before work begins. Properties with Historic Preservation Overlay do not need to complete Part I unless there is a question about overlay coverage. Include property photos from all sides and documentation supporting the structure's significance. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation): Evaluate whether proposed work meets applicable rehabilitation standards and is consistent with Secretary of Interior's Standards and County Design Guidelines. This portion must be approved BEFORE rehabilitation work begins. Provide detailed description of all exterior work and new construction with photos and architectural plans as applicable. Provide estimated qualified rehabilitation expenditures. Part III (Request for Certification of Completed Work): Certify that rehabilitation work is completed as approved and verify expenses claimed. Submit after project completion with photos of completed work, final documentation of all expenses in the provided spreadsheet format, and proof of payment for each item. Each application part requires applicant signature (digital, printed and wet-signed, or digitized handwritten). The HDC reviews all documentation and may conduct site visits. The completed project may be inspected by HDC or staff to verify work meets Standards for Rehabilitation, with the right to inspect up to five years after completion.

All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report and submit it with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and/or receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state financing program that provides loans, grants, and other financial assistance to businesses and local jurisdictions for economic development projects located in priority funding areas and eligible industries.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDAAF offers six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities—loans up to the lesser of $10 million or 20 percent of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity—loans up to $5 million or conditional loans and grants up to $2 million with local jurisdiction participation; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions—up to $3 million (or more for qualified distressed counties) for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development planning; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund—grants of up to $250,000 annually to capitalize local revolving loan funds; (5) Special Purposes Loan—funding for critical initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts & Entertainment, and Child Care Centers; (6) Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund)—financing for extraordinary opportunities with minimum applicant capital investment of five times the assistance amount. Assistance generally cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in priority funding areas and eligible industries, and local jurisdictions.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, economic development planning, and project-specific financing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be located within a priority funding area. Projects in qualified distressed counties may receive higher maximum assistance.
requirements_list: Located in a priority funding area
Operating in an eligible industry sector (with some exceptions)

Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs (with limited exceptions)
